issue.title: [Fix] GLM-4.7-Flash: Load compressed-tensors W4A16 checkpoints
issue.body:
## Motivation Fixes #49369. `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` (compressed-tensors `pack-quantized`, int4 symmetric, group 32) does not load. It quantizes `q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `kv_b_proj` from layer 1 on, and keeps layer 0 and the shared experts in BF16 through its `ignore` list. On a real `sglang serve`, it fails in five places, one after the other. Each one only shows up once the one before it is fixed: ```diff sglang serve cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit build model # (3) layer 0 + shared-expert gate_up_proj built W4A16; (4) BF16 shared expert fused into W4A16 MoE load_weights - fuse q_a + kv_a # (1) weight_shape -> [4] -> AssertionError + fuse q_a + kv_a # weight_shape -> [q_out + kv_out, in] post_load_weights - kv_b_proj.weight # (2) AttributeError + dequantize kv_b_proj -> w_kc / w_vc process_weights_after_loading # Marlin repack capture CUDA graphs - fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible(layer.weight) # (5) AttributeError + packed layer -> regular path serve ``` 1. **Fused QKV-A `weight_shape`.** `load_weights` fuses `q_a_proj` and `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` by concatenating every tensor of the pair on dim 0. For `weight_shape` (`[out, in]`), that gives `[q_out, in, kv_out, in]` instead of `[q_out + kv_out, in]`, and the load asserts. `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin` has the same concatenation. 2. **`kv_b_proj` in `post_load_weights`.** The MLA post-load step reads `kv_b_proj.weight`, which a packed layer does not have. This is the issue's `AttributeError`. 3. **Empty `packed_modules_mapping`.** `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM` declares none, so `ignore` entries that name shards (`q_a_proj`, `gate_proj`, ...) never match the fused `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `gate_up_proj`. Layer 0 and the shared experts' `gate_up_proj` get built W4A16 over BF16 weights. With FP8 this fails silently: the reporter measured 3.4e38 outputs on `unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-FP8-Dynamic`, where 13.0 is expected. 4. **Shared-expert fusion.** On CUDA SM80+, GLM fuses the shared expert into the routed `FusedMoE`, but this checkpoint keeps the shared experts in BF16 beside W4A16 routed experts. 5. **Fused-A GEMM eligibility.** `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible` reads `layer.weight` on the packed `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` during the first forward (CUDA graph capture). ## Modifications - `models/deepseek_common/utils.py`: a new `fuse_qkv_a_proj_tensors`, used by both the GLM and DeepSeek loaders. - `weight_shape` adds the output rows. - A shared act-order `weight_g_idx` is kept, and differing ones are rejected. - A pair of 0-d scales is shared, as before. - Only AWQ/GPTQ-packed tensors (`qweight`, `qzeros`, `scales` under `awq`, `awq_marlin`, `moe_wna16`, `gptq`, `gptq_marlin` or `auto-round`) stack on dim 1. A projection that such a checkpoint leaves unconverted keeps a plain `[out, in]` weight. `QuantTrio/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ` keeps `self_attn` in BF16, so choosing the dim from the config alone would break it. GGUF also names a tensor `qweight`, but it is row-major and stays on dim 0. - GPTQ's `g_idx` follows the same rule as `weight_g_idx`. - `compressed_tensors_wNa16.py`: `CompressedTensorsWNA16.dequantize_weight` unpacks the checkpoint layout to a dense weight in the scale dtype. - It supports symmetric quantization without act order. - The kernel repack marks the layer, and dequantizing a repacked layer raises. Sharded-state and remote-instance loaders copy kernel-layout tensors and then call `post_load_weights`. Reading those tensors would build garbage `w_kc`/`w_vc`. - `deepseek_weight_loader.py`: `post_load_weights` dequantizes a compressed-tensors WNA16 `kv_b_proj` before the `w_kc`/`w_vc` split, next to the AWQ branch. - `glm4_moe_lite.py`: - `packed_modules_mapping` maps `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `gate_up_proj` to their shards. - The shared-expert fusion gate checks `quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion`, as DeepSeek-V2 already does. - The loader pops cached QKV-A tensors even when the fused param is absent. - `compressed_tensors.py`: `CompressedTensorsConfig.can_fuse_shared_expert` is false when `ignore` keeps a layer's shared expert unquantized while its routed experts are quantized. Both are resolved per MoE layer with `should_ignore_layer`, so names and regexes match alike. A `shared_expert_gate` entry does not count. It probes the layers the ignore list names; a regex, or a bare suffix that could match an expert, adds `model.layers.0-255`. That takes 0.4 ms on the FP8 checkpoint's 601-entry list. - `fused_a_gemm.py`: a layer without a dense `weight` is not eligible. **Behavior change outside GLM:** `can_fuse_shared_expert` is also read by DeepSeek-V2/V4, MiniMax-M3 and Qwen2-MoE / Qwen3.5. For a compressed-tensors checkpoint whose `ignore` keeps the shared-expert body unquantized beside quantized routed experts, these now skip shared-expert fusion. Fusing such a checkpoint would load BF16 weights into the quantized expert buffers. A checkpoint that ignores both the shared and the routed experts of a layer keeps fusion. modelopt already applies the same rule. ## Accuracy Tests 1x NVIDIA A40 (SM86) for the `cyankiwi` row and 1x NVIDIA RTX A6000 (SM86) for the `QuantTrio` row, image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261110-4a5c6b8f`. Every file this PR touches is identical between the image's tree and this PR's base `533c067689`. "main" is that tree unchanged, and "branch" is this PR applied to it. The launch command follows the cookbook (`--tp 1 --reasoning-parser glm45`): ``` sglang serve --model-path --tp 1 --reasoning-parser glm45 --port 30000 sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --num-examples 200 \ --num-threads 64 --max-tokens 4096 --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false ``` | Checkpoint | main | branch | |---|---|---| | `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` (this issue) | fails to load | GSM8K **0.850** (1/200 truncated) | | `QuantTrio/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ` (regression check) | GSM8K **0.910** (2/200 truncated) | GSM8K **0.890** (0/200 truncated) | All runs use the command above: greedy (temperature 0, top_p 0.95), thinking off. Every server that loads answers `17*23` with `391`. **SM90 run by the reporter** (1x H20-3e, the same commands; [comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49531#issuecomment-6769382079)): | Checkpoint | main | branch | |---|---|---| | `unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-FP8-Dynamic` | GSM8K **0.000** (200/200 truncated; `17*23` answers `!!!!!!!!…`) | GSM8K **0.890** (0/200 truncated) | | `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` | fails to load | GSM8K **0.870** (0/200 truncated) | This covers the FP8 case that SM86 cannot run, and the fused-A GEMM path, which is eligible on SM90. 1. **Truncations** are generations that hit the 4096-token cap. They happen on unpatched main too (2/200 with the AWQ checkpoint), so they are not caused by this PR. The cookbook's 0.845 is BF16 on H100 with the same `sgl-eval` command and 200 examples. It's a sanity reference, not a like-for-like comparison. An earlier A6000 run of the `cyankiwi` checkpoint on this branch is consistent: 0.874 thinking-off and 0.969 thinking-on, both partial runs without a token cap. 2. **The AWQ runs:** both trees build the same model: 17.52 GB of weights, the same KV size, the `awq_marlin` kernel and the same CUDA graphs. Answers flip both ways (10 questions right only on main, 6 only on the branch), and 51/200 greedy generations match word for word. That looks like batching nondeterminism, though I did not run main twice to confirm. 3. **FP8** (`unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-FP8-Dynamic`) cannot run on SM86 on either tree (`bmm_fp8 does not support backend 'cublas' with capability 86`); see the SM90 table above.
Before: main, cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit (the same assert on A6000 and A40) ``` File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1048, in load_model self.load_weights_and_postprocess( File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1057, in load_weights_and_postprocess DefaultModelLoader.load_weights_only(model, weights, target_device) File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 1091, in load_weights_only model.load_weights(weights) File ".../sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py", line 1043, in load_weights weight_loader(param, fused_weight) File ".../sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 377, in weight_loader AssertionError: param.shape=torch.Size([2]) param.dtype=torch.int64 loaded_weight.shape=torch.Size([4]) loaded_weight.dtype=torch.int64 ``` With fixes 1–4 applied but not 5, loading completes and the first forward fails: ``` File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2621, in prepare_qkv_latent and fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible( File ".../sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/fused_a_gemm.py", line 52, in fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible layer.weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16 AttributeError: 'ReplicatedLinear' object has no attribute 'weight' ```
After: this branch, cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit (A40) ``` [2026-11-10 09:11:58] Quantization keeps shared experts at a higher precision than the routed experts, so they cannot be fused into the quantized routed-expert path. Shared experts fusion optimization is disabled. [2026-11-10 09:12:18] Load weight end. elapsed=20.65 s, type=Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM, quant=compressed-tensors, avail mem=26.22 GB, mem usage=17.86 GB. [2026-11-10 09:12:25] KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.bfloat16, #tokens: 360675, KV size: 18.19 GB [2026-11-10 09:25:22] Capture target prefill CUDA graph end. elapsed=777.75 s, mem usage=1.73 GB, avail mem=4.63 GB. [2026-11-10 09:25:34] Capture target decode CUDA graph end. bs=[1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32], elapsed=11.78 s, mem usage=0.29 GB, avail mem=4.35 GB. [2026-11-10 09:25:51] The server is fired up and ready to roll! ``` The 778 s prefill capture was the first serve on a fresh pod. The same code captured in 26 s on the A6000 pod after an earlier serve there, so this is most likely cold kernel caches; the log does not show the cause. ``` $ curl .../v1/chat/completions # "What is 17*23? Answer with just the number." "content": "391" ``` ``` sgl-eval gsm8k (A40, 200 examples, 64 threads, max_tokens 4096, thinking off): score 0.85, stop_rate 0.995, truncated_rate 0.005, error_rate 0.0 ```
### Unit tests New CPU file `test/registered/unit/models/test_mla_compressed_tensors_wna16_loading.py` (`base-a-test-cpu`), plus a GLM case in `test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py`. I checked each regression case: it fails with its fix reverted and passes with it. The cases: - The GLM and DeepSeek loaders fuse `weight_shape` / `weight_packed` / `weight_scale`. - GLM stacks AWQ `qweight` on dim 1 and keeps unconverted BF16 attention on dim 0. - `dequantize_weight` matches compressed-tensors' own `pack_to_int32` exactly (4-bit group, 4-bit channel, 8-bit). - The real `process_weights_after_loading` marks the layer, and dequantizing it afterwards raises. - `post_load_weights` builds `w_kc`/`w_vc` from a packed `kv_b_proj`. - Layer 0's fused layers, and an FP8 checkpoint's ignored layer-1 attention, resolve to their ignored shards. - `can_fuse_shared_expert` covers the checkpoint's own ignore list, gate-only, both-ignored, regex (including `re:.*mlp\.shared.*` and a layer-anchored regex) and bare-suffix cases. - GPTQ / AutoRound `qweight` stacks on dim 1, GGUF's stays on dim 0, and GPTQ `g_idx` follows the act-order rule. - `fused_a_gemm_weight_eligible` is false on a packed layer. ``` test_mla_compressed_tensors_wna16_loading.py + test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py + test_deepseek_quark_block_fp8_loading.py: 67 passed on the A40 pod at 0a7a7e4175; 68 passed locally at 930d78d9ce ``` ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way. Code-only, no format, config or API changes; a revert restores the old behavior. **Blast radius:** MLA checkpoint loading. - Every GLM-4.7-Flash and DeepSeek-family load goes through the new QKV-A fusion helper. Only `weight_shape`, `weight_g_idx` and the AWQ `qweight`/`qzeros`/`scales` choice of dimension behave differently; every other tensor concatenates exactly as before. The unconverted-attention AWQ case is covered by the `QuantTrio` row above. - Shared-expert fusion turns off for compressed-tensors checkpoints whose `ignore` keeps shared experts unquantized beside quantized routed experts (see "Behavior change outside GLM"). That costs throughput where fusion used to run, but such checkpoints loaded BF16 weights into quantized expert buffers. - A packed compressed-tensors `kv_b_proj` reloaded through the sharded-state or remote-instance loaders now raises `NotImplementedError` instead of computing silently wrong `w_kc`/`w_vc`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No kernel changes. The fused-A GEMM change only makes packed layers take their regular path (before, they crashed). On this checkpoint, disabling shared-expert fusion is required for correctness. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No doc change: the cookbook page covers BF16 only.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #42881338214](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42881338214) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #42881337730](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42881337730) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #42881338562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42881338562) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. Use `/rerun-test` to run the tests your change touches, or copy this prompt for an agent: > > ```text > Find the registered tests this PR affects and run them with /rerun-test, following https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.agents/skills/rerun-test/SKILL.md > ```

comment.body:
Tested on 1x H20-3e (SM90), both gaps from the description.

Setup: "main" is the PR's base `533c067689`, "branch" is `0a7a7e4175`, each tree's `python/` first on `PYTHONPATH` over the same environment (sglang-kernel 0.4.10, flashinfer-python 0.7.3, the base's pins). Your commands, one GPU per server:

```
sglang serve --model-path <model> --tp 1 --reasoning-parser glm45 --port <port>
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1 --num-examples 200 \
  --num-threads 64 --max-tokens 4096 --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false
```

| Checkpoint | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| `unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-FP8-Dynamic` | GSM8K **0.000** (200/200 truncated at 4096 tokens; `17*23` answers `!!!!!!!!…`) | GSM8K **0.890** (0/200 truncated; `17*23` -> `391`) |
| `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` | fails to load: `AssertionError: param.shape=torch.Size([2]) ... loaded_weight.shape=torch.Size([4])` | GSM8K **0.870** (0/200 truncated; `17*23` -> `391`) |

So the FP8 case from the issue is fixed by the `packed_modules_mapping` change, and the AWQ checkpoint serves on SM90 with the fused-A GEMM path present: no `AttributeError` during CUDA graph capture, and the log shows the shared-expert fusion turned off ("Quantization keeps shared experts at a higher precision than the routed experts ...").

A few comments from reading the diff:

1. `fuse_qkv_a_proj_tensors`: `packed_outputs_last` only matches `awq`, `awq_marlin` and `moe_wna16`. GPTQ's `qweight` (`[in // pack, out]`), `qzeros` and `scales` also keep the output dim last, and the comment says "AWQ/GPTQ-packed", so a GPTQ-packed MLA checkpoint would still be concatenated on dim 0. Adding `gptq` and `gptq_marlin` to the tuple (or deciding from the tensor names alone, since `.qweight` / `.qzeros` / `.scales` only exist in these layouts) would cover it.
2. `can_fuse_shared_expert` scans `ignore` entries for the substring `shared_expert`, so an entry that matches the shared experts without containing it (for example `re:.*mlp\.shared.*`) is not seen. Resolving one concrete shared-expert module name and one routed-expert module name per MoE layer with `should_ignore_layer` and comparing the two answers would handle names and regexes the same way. Not blocking for these checkpoints, whose ignore lists name the modules.
3. `dequantize_weight` looks right to me: `(code - 2^(b-1))` is exact in the scale dtype, so the product rounds once, the same as computing in FP32 and casting.

issue.title: [Bug] GLM-4.7-Flash compressed-tensors W4A16: MLA post-load step reads kv_b_proj.weight, which a packed layer does not have
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin.post_load_weights` builds the MLA absorbed weights from `self_attn.kv_b_proj`: it dequantizes AWQ layers (`qweight`) and otherwise reads `kv_b_proj.weight`. A compressed-tensors `pack-quantized` (W4A16) layer has `weight_packed`, `weight_scale` and `weight_shape` instead, so the step fails:

```
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py", line 1081, in load_weights
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py", line 639, in post_load_weights
AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

Seen with `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` (29k downloads last month; compressed-tensors `pack-quantized`; from layer 1 on, `kv_b_proj` is stored as `weight_packed`/`weight_scale`/`weight_shape`), loading its own tensor names and shapes into a 4-layer model built from its config on v0.5.23. The branch is unchanged on main `d959849` (`deepseek_weight_loader.py`, around line 684). vLLM 0.33.0 loads the same tensors.

The same checkpoint keeps layer 0 in BF16 and lists its projections in `ignore` (`model.layers.0.self_attn.q_a_proj`, `...kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `model.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj`, `...up_proj`, ...). `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM` has an empty `packed_modules_mapping`, so `should_ignore_layer` cannot match the fused `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `gate_up_proj` of that layer to their shard entries, and both are built W4A16 over BF16 weights.

#19106 addressed this class of failure for GLM-4.7-Flash compressed-tensors checkpoints (`'ReplicatedLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'`) and was closed for inactivity.

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23, main `d959849`; 1x H20-3e (SM90).

comment.body: @koladefaj thanks for the fix. I ran both gaps on an H20-3e (SM90) with your commands; results and a short review are in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/49531#issuecomment-6769382079. In short: `unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-FP8-Dynamic` goes from 0.000 on main (every answer `!!!…`) to 0.890 on the branch, and `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` from failing to load to 0.870, with no crash on the SM90 fused-A GEMM path.

issue.title: Agree on frozen-prefix gradient boundaries across pipeline stages
issue.body:
Depends on
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7678 (rebased on its head `5af6ca825`; until `pull-request/7678` is updated, the commit list here also shows that commit)

Works together with
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8018

- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
<!-- Add a one line overview of what this PR aims to accomplish. -->

Let pipeline stages agree on a frozen-prefix gradient boundary, so that when only the later decoder layers are trainable (for example LoRA on the decoder half of DeepSeek-V4.1), stages that lie entirely before the first trainable layer skip their backward.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Issue tracking

For PRs from open-source community contributors:

- **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR.
- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Linked issue: <!-- e.g. Fixes #1234 / Related to #1234 -->

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

## Implementation details

- A later pipeline stage receives its input over P2P as a tensor that always requires grad, so it cannot tell on its own whether anything upstream is trainable. `sync_pipeline_gradient_boundaries` takes the minimum, over all stages, of the first decoder layer with a trainable parameter (0 when a pre-process module such as the embedding is trainable) and stores it on every decoder.
- Both pipelined schedules call it before their first microbatch. The result is cached; `reset_gradient_boundary_cache` clears it after `requires_grad` changes.
- When no decoder layer is trainable (for example only the final norm or the output layer is), the boundary stays past the last layer, so every stage runs its layers under `no_grad`.
- `backward_step` sends zero input gradients when autograd never reached a stage input, which keeps the classic P2P path in step with the previous stage.
- `infer_gradient_boundary_layer`, `get_cached_gradient_boundary_layer`, `first_local_layer_index` and `resolve_gradient_boundary` give the decoder blocks one place to find the boundary for a forward.
- `detach_state` copies a forward-local state object (dataclasses, dicts, lists, tuples) with detached tensor leaves, for cutting cross-layer state at the boundary.
- `TransformerBlock` and `HybridStack` run the frozen prefix under `no_grad`, detach the hidden state where the first trainable layer starts, and detach the output of a stage that lies entirely before it. Full recompute runs the frozen prefix without checkpoints and counts the recompute window from the boundary.
- `test_gradient_boundary_pipeline.py` compares gradients against a full backward on GPT and hybrid models with PP=2 and PP=4, eager and full recompute, including all-frozen decoders.

## Known limitations

- Multi-module pipelines do not sync the boundary yet; their stages keep full autograd.

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

issue.title: [Bug] Qwen4-Exp PLE: BF16 n-gram shards are cast to FP8 with a unit scale when the checkpoint's config sets ple_embedding_dtype (primitive-ai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4)
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`primitive-ai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (about 6.7k downloads last month) has `text_config.ple_embedding_dtype: "float8_e4m3fn"` in its `config.json`, keeps `*.ple.*` out of quantization in its `ignore` list, and stores all 128 `ngram_embedding.shard_*` tensors in BF16 with no scale tensor. `_ple_table_is_fp8` returns `True` from the config field, so the n-gram table is built in FP8 with `weight_scale` a buffer of ones, and the loader casts the BF16 rows into it. The only sign is one warning:

```
PLE checkpoint shards are torch.bfloat16 but the embedding storage is fp8 (ple_embedding_dtype / fp8 quant config); downcasting is lossy
```

On 65,536 real rows of `layers.1.ple.ple_embedding.ngram_embedding.shard_0.weight` (`[2500012, 160]`), the unit-scale FP8 cast gives:

| | value |
|---|---|
| relative error of the table | 7.6% |
| nonzero values that become 0 | 10.2% |
| median absolute value | 0.0048 (below FP8 E4M3's smallest normal value, 2^-6) |
| largest absolute value | 0.051 |
| relative error with one per-tensor scale (amax / 448) instead of 1.0 | 2.8% |

Among the 15 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoints I checked, this is the only one whose config asks for FP8 n-gram storage while its shards are BF16. Thanks, agreed. Reading #48073 the same way: its exclusion check sits inside the `fp8` branch, so the `ple_embedding_dtype == "float8_e4m3fn"` branch still returns `True` first, and this checkpoint keeps the unit-scale downcast.

The precision decision and the scale are really two questions, so one rule for both PRs could be:

1. **FP8 shards:** an FP8 table, with the checkpoint's scale (today's behavior).
2. **BF16 shards and an explicit `ple_embedding_dtype: float8_e4m3fn`:** FP8 storage as asked, but the downcast writes a per-tensor scale (amax / 448) into `weight_scale` instead of leaving it at 1.0. On the rows in the issue that is 2.8% relative error instead of 7.6%.
3. **No explicit request:** #48073's rule, so an `fp8` checkpoint whose ignore list names the PLE table keeps it in BF16.

With that order, #48073 only changes case 3 and does not need to special-case the explicit setting, and the fix for this issue lives in the load path (case 2), where the shard dtype is known. It also keeps `ple_embedding_dtype` meaning what the offload docs say it means.

If that works for you and @xuqianmamba, I can open the case-2 change on top of #48073 so the two land in one order.

issue.title: [Bug] ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION: layers with an unsupported quant_algo (FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN) are built unquantized and load FP8 codes as BF16 values
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_quant_method` builds a linear layer with the method of its per-layer `quant_algo` (`FP8`, `FP8_PB_WO`/`FP8_BLOCK_SCALES`, `MXFP8`, `NVFP4`, `W4A16_NVFP4`) and returns `UnquantizedLinearMethod` for any other algorithm. `from_config` does not check the algorithms either. So a mixed-precision checkpoint with a layer kind SGLang has no branch for loads without an error: the layer is built in BF16, the stored FP8 codes are copied in as if they were BF16 values, and the per-channel `weight_scale` is skipped (only a `Parameter ...weight_scale not found in params_dict` log line).

`AEON-7/Qwen3.8-27B-AEON-ULTIMATE-UNCENSORED-NVFP4-MIXED` (ModelOpt 0.46.0, about 10k downloads last month) stores 232 attention projections as `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` and 168 MLP projections as `NVFP4`. On SGLang the attention projections are `UnquantizedLinearMethod`. For layer 0's `linear_attn.out_proj`, loaded with its real weight and scale, the output on random BF16 inputs reaches 41728 against 60.9 for the dequantized reference (relative error about 6.6e3). vLLM builds the same layer with `ModelOptLinearMethod` and matches the reference (relative error 0.026).

### Reproduction

```python
from sglang.srt.layers.linear import LinearBase
from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant import ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig

cfg = ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.from_config({
    "quant_method": "modelopt", "quant_algo": "MIXED_PRECISION", "ignore": [],
    "quantized_layers": {
        "model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj": {"quant_algo": "FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN"},
        "model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj": {"quant_algo": "NVFP4", "group_size": 16},
    },
})
cfg.packed_modules_mapping = {"qkv_proj": ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"], "gate_up_proj": ["gate_proj", "up_proj"]}  # set by the model
layer = LinearBase.__new__(LinearBase)  # only the type matters to get_quant_method
for prefix in ("model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj", "model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj"):
    print(prefix, cfg.resolve_quant_algo(prefix), type(cfg.get_quant_method(layer, prefix)).__name__)
```

Output on v0.5.23:

```
model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN UnquantizedLinearMethod
model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj NVFP4 ModelOptFp4LinearMethod
```

The same branches are on main (`d959849`). #31827 (part B) hit this fallback for MXFP8 layers; an `MXFP8` branch was added then, but any other algorithm still falls through to `UnquantizedLinearMethod`. #15468 proposed FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN support for plain ModelOpt FP8 checkpoints and was closed; the mixed-precision path has no check that would turn an unsupported algorithm into an error.

### Expected

Either build `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` layers with a per-channel FP8 method, or raise in `from_config` for a per-layer `quant_algo` the config cannot build, instead of loading quantized codes into an unquantized layer.

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23 and main `d959849`, H20.

On v0.5.23 its `lm_head` is built unquantized: after loading, the parameter holds the raw FP8 codes (largest value 448, against 0.19 dequantized; relative error 6590 on the whole head), and `lm_head.weight_scale` is skipped (`Parameter lm_head.weight_scale not found in params_dict`). #49400 turns this into an error when the layer is built.

issue.title: [Bug] ModelOpt NVFP4 fused linear: unwritten parts decide the global scales (Gemma 4 KV-shared layers store only q_proj)
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` takes a fused linear's global scales as the largest per-part value: `layer.input_scale.max()` and `layer.weight_scale_2.max()`. A part that no checkpoint tensor writes still takes part in that max:

- `weight_scale_2` is created with `torch.empty`, so an unwritten part holds whatever the allocation held (same in `ModelOptNvFp4A16LinearMethod`);
- `input_scale` is created filled with 1.0 (for online quantization, which stores none), so an unwritten part makes the global input scale 1.0.

Gemma 4's KV-shared layers hit this. `AEON-7/Gemma-4-E4B-it-Uncensored-NVFP4` and `AEON-7/Gemma-4-E4B-DECKARD-HERETIC-NVFP4` (about 2.6k downloads last month each; 42 layers, `num_kv_shared_layers: 18`) store only `q_proj` in layers 24-41, but SGLang builds a fused `qkv_proj` there, so the k and v parts are never written.

A fused qkv layer on main where only q's scales are loaded (the script below):

```
ModelOptFp4LinearMethod before any load: weight_scale_2 [2.2505394179826282e-28, 0.0, 0.0] input_scale [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
   q written: weight global 0.003000000026077032 input global 1.0
```

The real tensors of a KV-shared layer on v0.5.23 (layer 2 of a 4-layer build of the config, real allocation, `fp4_gemm_backend` Marlin as the server picks on SM90):

| | stored q `input_scale` | `input_scale` parts | `input_global_scale` | `weight_scale_2` parts (q, k/v) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Uncensored | 0.00209 | [0.00209, 1.0, 1.0] | 1.0 | [0.00337, 0.0, 0.0] |
| DECKARD-HERETIC | 0.00595 | [0.00595, 1.0, 1.0] | 1.0 | [0.00113, 0.0, 0.0] |

- The global input scale is 1.0 instead of q's stored value in every KV-shared layer, and `alpha = input_scale * weight_scale_2` follows it. Marlin (W4A16) does not use the input scale, so on SM90 the output is unaffected; the W4A4 paths quantize the activations with it.
- The global weight scale is right here only because the k and v slots of `weight_scale_2` happened to hold 0. When those slots hold 1.0 instead (as after SGLang's dummy weight initialization), the same layer's output is 296 times too large (relative error 296 against the checkpoint's dequantized q weights).

### Reproduction

```python
import torch, torch.nn as nn
from sglang.srt.layers.linear import QKVParallelLinear
from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant import ModelOptFp4Config, ModelOptFp4LinearMethod

cfg = ModelOptFp4Config(is_checkpoint_nvfp4_serialized=True, group_size=16, use_per_token_activation=False)
qkv = QKVParallelLinear(hidden_size=16, head_size=8, total_num_heads=2, total_num_kv_heads=2, bias=False, parallel_group="replicated")
layer = nn.Module()
ModelOptFp4LinearMethod(cfg).create_weights(layer, input_size_per_partition=16, output_partition_sizes=[16, 16, 16],
                                            input_size=16, output_size=48, params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
                                            weight_loader=qkv.weight_loader_v2)
print("before any load: weight_scale_2", layer.weight_scale_2.tolist(), "input_scale", layer.input_scale.tolist())
qkv.weight_loader_v2(layer.weight_scale_2, torch.tensor(0.003), "q")
qkv.weight_loader_v2(layer.input_scale, torch.tensor(0.002), "q")
print("q written: weight global", float(layer.weight_scale_2.max()), "input global", float(layer.input_scale.max()))
```

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23 and main `d565013`, 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0.

issue.title: [Bug] compressed-tensors: a shared expert kept unquantized in `ignore` is still fused into the quantized MoE (Qwen3-Next AWQ fails to load)
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

On CUDA, Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and the DeepSeek family fuse the shared expert into the routed experts' `FusedMoE` as one more expert unless the quantization config's `can_fuse_shared_expert()` returns `False` (`qwen2_moe.can_fuse_shared_expert`, `deepseek_common.utils.quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion`). `ModelOptConfig` and `QuarkConfig` define it, so a shared expert that their exclusion list keeps in BF16 stays a separate MLP (#40628, #46800). `CompressedTensorsConfig` does not define it, so a compressed-tensors checkpoint whose `ignore` list names `mlp.shared_expert.*` is still fused: the loader renames `mlp.shared_expert.*` to `mlp.experts.<num_experts>.*`, and the BF16 `weight` tensors of the shared expert look for parameters that a quantized expert does not have.

`cyankiwi/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` (W4A16, `pack-quantized`, 16k downloads last month) lists every `mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj` in `ignore` and stores them in BF16. On v0.5.23 the server fails while loading:

```
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/qwen3_next.py", line 1247, in load_weights
    param = params_dict[name]
KeyError: 'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.w2_weight'
```

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path cyankiwi/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit --tp 1 --context-length 4096
```

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23 and main `d959849`, 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0.

comment.body:
The same fusion also hits GLM-5-Next on CUDA, without an error. `wtdcode/GLM-5.3-Flash-AWQ-W4A16` (compressed-tensors W4A16) keeps its shared experts in BF16 through `ignore: ["re:.*shared_experts.*", ...]`, but `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration.shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason` only checks ModelOpt FP4 exclusions on CUDA, so they are fused anyway. Loading the checkpoint's real tensors into a 4-layer build on v0.5.23, layer 3's `mlp.shared_experts.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` reach no parameter, and the fused slot's `mlp.experts.w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale` are never written.

issue.title: [Bug] ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION on Llama / Mistral 3: fused qkv_proj and gate_up_proj are built unquantized (the model classes declare no packed_modules_mapping)
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

ModelOpt's `quantized_layers` lists the unfused names (`q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `gate_proj`, `up_proj`), so `ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig._resolve_quant_algo` maps a fused layer to its parts through `packed_modules_mapping`. `_get_quantization_config` takes that mapping from the model class, and neither `LlamaForCausalLM` nor `LlavaForConditionalGeneration` (the base of `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`) defines one. Every `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj` then resolves to `None` and is built with `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, while `o_proj` and `down_proj`, which are listed under their own names, get the right method.

`nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4` (MIXED_PRECISION, about 30k downloads last month) stores FP8 attention projections in all 88 layers, FP8 MLPs in layers 0-3 and 87, and NVFP4 MLPs in the other 83 layers. With the checkpoint's own `hf_quant_config.json` (no weights needed):

```python
import json

from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant import ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig
from sglang.srt.models.mistral import Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration

repo = "nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4"
cfg = json.load(open(hf_hub_download(repo, "hf_quant_config.json")))
# what _get_quantization_config passes for this architecture
cfg["packed_modules_mapping"] = getattr(Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration, "packed_modules_mapping", {})
qc = ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.from_config(cfg)
for prefix in (
    "language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj",
    "language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj",
    "language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj",
    "language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj",
    "language_model.model.layers.4.mlp.gate_up_proj",
    "language_model.model.layers.4.mlp.down_proj",
):
    print(f"{prefix:52s} {qc._resolve_quant_algo(prefix)}")
```

```
language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj     None
language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj       FP8
language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj       None
language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj          FP8
language_model.model.layers.4.mlp.gate_up_proj       None
language_model.model.layers.4.mlp.down_proj          NVFP4
```

I loaded the checkpoint's real tensors for layers 0 and 4 through `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` (a 5-layer build of its config on v0.5.23). Two things happen:

- The FP8 parts are copied into the BF16 fused weights as raw FP8 values, and their scales are skipped (`Parameter model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight_scale not found in params_dict`). Compared with the checkpoint's dequantized weights, layer 0's `gate_up_proj` output has a largest value of 22656 where 1.97 is expected (relative error 9610).
- Layer 4's NVFP4 parts (packed `uint8 [28672, 6144]`) do not fit the unquantized parameter, and loading stops:

```
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/mistral.py", line 188, in load_weights
    return super().load_weights(normalize(weights))
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/llava.py", line 890, in load_weights
    getattr(self, part).load_weights([(name, loaded_weight)])
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/llama.py", line 763, in _legacy_load_weights
    weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id)
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 894, in weight_loader
    assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape
AssertionError
```

So this checkpoint cannot be loaded, and a MIXED_PRECISION Llama or Mistral checkpoint whose fused projections are all FP8 would load without an error and compute those projections with FP8 codes read as BF16 values.

### Reproduction

The script above. Serving: `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4 --tp 2`.

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23 and main `ae1347a`, 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0.

issue.title: [Fix] gemma3/mistral3: Match vision layers in quantization ignore lists
issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #49061.

Gemma 3 and Mistral 3 rename some vision modules when they load the weights, but the quantization config's `ignore` list keeps the checkpoint's names, so `should_ignore_layer` does not match these layers and builds them with the checkpoint's quantization scheme:

- Gemma 3: the SigLIP attention's `out_proj` is loaded into VisionAttention's `proj`.
- Mistral 3: `load_weights` rewrites `model.vision_tower.` (and `model.language_model.`, `model.multi_modal_projector.`); Pixtral's attention output projection is `o_proj` in the checkpoint and `proj` in VisionAttention; and the class declares no `packed_modules_mapping`, so the fused `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj` cannot be matched through their shard names.

The model loader already applies a model class's `hf_to_sglang_mapper` to the quantization config's module lists (and only to them), as Qwen2.5-VL does for its vision tower; #43616 uses the same mechanism for Gemma 4's `.linear` names.

## Modifications

- `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration.hf_to_sglang_mapper`: suffix `.self_attn.out_proj` -> `.self_attn.proj`, the rename `load_weights` already does.
- `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration.hf_to_sglang_mapper`: the three prefix renames of its `load_weights`, and suffix `.attention.o_proj` -> `.attention.proj` (the language model's attention is `self_attn`, so it is not affected).
- `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration.packed_modules_mapping`: `qkv_proj` -> q/k/v, `gate_up_proj` -> gate/up.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/models/test_vision_quant_ignore_names.py`: builds the quantization config as the loader does, from ignore lists spelled like the two checkpoints (and the older Mistral 3 layout without `model.`), and checks which vision and language layers are ignored.

Weight loading itself is unchanged: neither class calls the mapper in `load_weights`.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0. Unit test and repro on main `754185a` with and without this PR; served runs on v0.5.23 with and without the same two-file change (the files differ from main only in imports).

- Unit test: main 16 failures, 1 error; this PR 5 tests OK.
- The repro of #49061 (reads `config.json` only), this PR:

  ```
  RedHatAI/gemma-3-27b-it-FP8-dynamic
    vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj ignored (BF16)
    vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.proj ignored (BF16)
    vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.mlp.fc1      ignored (BF16)
    vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.mlp.fc2      ignored (BF16)
  RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-NVFP4
    vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.attention.qkv_proj    ignored (BF16)
    vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.attention.proj        ignored (BF16)
    vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.feed_forward.gate_up_proj ignored (BF16)
    vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.feed_forward.down_proj ignored (BF16)
  ```

- Real tensors of vision layer 0 through SGLang's load and post-load step, compared with the BF16 reference:

  | Checkpoint | v0.5.23 | v0.5.23 + this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | `RedHatAI/gemma-3-27b-it-FP8-dynamic`, `self_attn.proj` | FP8, 928 outputs inf | BF16, relative error 0.0017 |
  | `RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-NVFP4`, `attention.qkv_proj` / `attention.proj` / `feed_forward.down_proj` | NVFP4, weights not loaded (this run stopped in the post-load step on the unwritten global scales) | BF16, relative error 0.0016 / 0.0017 / 0.0017 |

  (0.0017 is BF16 rounding: the unquantized `qkv_proj` of v0.5.23, which already matched, gives the same.)

- Served, "Describe this image." about two COCO photographs (two elephants under a shelter; three people around a table with food), greedy, 64 tokens:

  | Checkpoint | v0.5.23 | v0.5.23 + this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | `RedHatAI/gemma-3-27b-it-FP8-dynamic` (`--enable-multimodal`) | both: "...a digital illustration or artwork depicting a whimsical, fantastical scene with a strong focus on a large, stylized mushroom." | "The image shows two Asian elephants standing under a simple, open-sided shelter with a corrugated metal roof." / "The image shows three people in what appears to be a community hall or cafeteria setting." |
  | `RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-NVFP4` | both: "asmussen an in with for [ for [ for [ ..." | "The image depicts two elephants standing under a shelter." / "There are three people in the foreground, standing around a table with various food items and drinks." |

  The 20 text prompts of the same runs give the same answers with and without this PR: 20 of 20 for Mistral 3; for Gemma 3, 20 of 20 against a second run of v0.5.23, which itself differs from the first v0.5.23 run on 3 of 20 (run-to-run variation, all answers correct).

- `abhishekchohan/gemma-3-12b-it-quantized-W4A16`, the same Gemma 3 rename, fails at load on v0.5.23 (`KeyError: 'vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.proj.weight'`). With this PR it loads and describes "two Asian elephants standing under a simple wooden shelter" and a group in "a community center or similar space".

issue.title: [Bug] ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION: layers with an unsupported quant_algo (FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN) are built unquantized and load FP8 codes as BF16 values
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_quant_method` builds a linear layer with the method of its per-layer `quant_algo` (`FP8`, `FP8_PB_WO`/`FP8_BLOCK_SCALES`, `MXFP8`, `NVFP4`, `W4A16_NVFP4`) and returns `UnquantizedLinearMethod` for any other algorithm. `from_config` does not check the algorithms either. So a mixed-precision checkpoint with a layer kind SGLang has no branch for loads without an error: the layer is built in BF16, the stored FP8 codes are copied in as if they were BF16 values, and the per-channel `weight_scale` is skipped (only a `Parameter ...weight_scale not found in params_dict` log line).

`AEON-7/Qwen3.8-27B-AEON-ULTIMATE-UNCENSORED-NVFP4-MIXED` (ModelOpt 0.46.0, about 10k downloads last month) stores 232 attention projections as `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` and 168 MLP projections as `NVFP4`. On SGLang the attention projections are `UnquantizedLinearMethod`. For layer 0's `linear_attn.out_proj`, loaded with its real weight and scale, the output on random BF16 inputs reaches 41728 against 60.9 for the dequantized reference (relative error about 6.6e3). vLLM builds the same layer with `ModelOptLinearMethod` and matches the reference (relative error 0.026).

### Reproduction

```python
from sglang.srt.layers.linear import LinearBase
from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant import ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig

cfg = ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.from_config({
    "quant_method": "modelopt", "quant_algo": "MIXED_PRECISION", "ignore": [],
    "quantized_layers": {
        "model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj": {"quant_algo": "FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN"},
        "model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj": {"quant_algo": "NVFP4", "group_size": 16},
    },
})
cfg.packed_modules_mapping = {"qkv_proj": ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"], "gate_up_proj": ["gate_proj", "up_proj"]}  # set by the model
layer = LinearBase.__new__(LinearBase)  # only the type matters to get_quant_method
for prefix in ("model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj", "model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj"):
    print(prefix, cfg.resolve_quant_algo(prefix), type(cfg.get_quant_method(layer, prefix)).__name__)
```

Output on v0.5.23:

```
model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN UnquantizedLinearMethod
model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj NVFP4 ModelOptFp4LinearMethod
```

The same branches are on main (`d959849`). #31827 (part B) hit this fallback for MXFP8 layers; an `MXFP8` branch was added then, but any other algorithm still falls through to `UnquantizedLinearMethod`. #15468 proposed FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN support for plain ModelOpt FP8 checkpoints and was closed; the mixed-precision path has no check that would turn an unsupported algorithm into an error.

### Expected

Either build `FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN` layers with a per-channel FP8 method, or raise in `from_config` for a per-layer `quant_algo` the config cannot build, instead of loading quantized codes into an unquantized layer.

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23 and main `d959849`, H20.

issue.title: [Bugfix] Keep modules listed in FP8 modules_to_not_convert unquantized
issue.body:
## Overview

Fixes #66113. HF FP8 checkpoints that list whole modules in `modules_to_not_convert`, such as Ministral-3 and Devstral-Small-2 (`"model.vision_tower"`, `"model.multi_modal_projector"`), got those modules built as FP8 when served with the HF config. Their BF16 weights were loaded into FP8 parameters and the image embeddings came out as zeros. `Fp8Config` now maps these entries correctly and treats a listed module as covering every layer inside it, as transformers does.

## Claims

- With `--config-format hf`, the vision tower and projector of `mistralai/Ministral-3-{3B,8B,14B}-Instruct-2512` and `mistralai/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512` are now built unquantized; the language model stays FP8.
- On a synthetic checkpoint with the same layout, image embeddings now match transformers (cosine similarity at least 0.99998 per token, largest difference 3e-4). Before, they were all zeros.
- Checkpoints that list full layer names are unchanged: the method of every linear and MoE layer is the same before and after for six other FP8 checkpoints and for the Mistral-format path (table below).
- The FP8 fused shared-expert check uses the same rule, so it refuses to fuse a shared expert whose whole module is ignored.

## Validation

GPU: NVIDIA H20-3e. vLLM nightly wheel `0.33.0rc1.dev931+g5a92788a1` with the Python sources of this branch's base, main `f358f0578`; "before" is that base, "after" adds this commit.

**New tests fail before and pass after**

```
pytest -v tests/models/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_fp8_modules_to_not_convert_keeps_modules_unquantized \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py::test_fp8_shared_expert_fse_rejects_asymmetric_ignored_layers
```

Before:

```
E               AssertionError: vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.attention.qkv_proj
E                +  where False = isinstance(<vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.fp8.Fp8LinearMethod object at 0x...>, <class 'vllm.model_executor.layers.linear.UnquantizedLinearMethod'>)
E       assert not True
FAILED tests/models/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_fp8_modules_to_not_convert_keeps_modules_unquantized
FAILED tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py::test_fp8_shared_expert_fse_rejects_asymmetric_ignored_layers[ignored_layers3]
================== 2 failed, 3 passed, 20 warnings in 10.09s ===================
```

After:

```
======================= 5 passed, 20 warnings in 10.85s ========================
```

The first test saves a small Mistral3 checkpoint the way the Ministral-3 FP8 export is laid out (BF16 vision tower and projector, FP8 language model, the same `modules_to_not_convert`), loads it with the default loader and real weights, and checks each layer's method and that the projector and vision weights equal the checkpoint's. The second is a new case of the existing FP8 shared-expert test.

Existing tests with this change: `tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py` 178 passed, 3 skipped; `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -k "not model_load_and_run and not reloading and not kv_cache_dtype_skip"` (no model downloads) 24 passed, 20 skipped; `tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py test_modelopt.py test_auto_awq.py` 132 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed. The two failures (`test_modelopt_nested_mixed_checkpoint`, `test_modelopt_mixed_dspark_checkpoint`) fail the same way on the base commit when the whole file runs ("Engine core initialization failed") and pass when run alone, with and without this change.

**Reproducer from the issue** (config.json only, dummy weights, one text and one vision layer):

| checkpoint (`--config-format hf`) | vision tower, before | projector, before | vision tower, after | projector, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ministral-3-3B/8B/14B-Instruct-2512, Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512 | 4 `Fp8LinearMethod` | 2 `Fp8LinearMethod` | 4 `UnquantizedLinearMethod` | 2 `UnquantizedLinearMethod` |

**Image embeddings** of the synthetic checkpoint (2 vision layers, one 112x84 image), `embed_multimodal` against transformers' `get_image_features` on the same weights:

| | largest abs value | largest abs difference | cosine similarity per token (min) |
|---|---|---|---|
| transformers | 0.0574 | | |
| vLLM before | 0.0000 | 0.0574 | 0.00000 |
| vLLM after | 0.0576 | 0.0003 | 0.99998 |

**Model output**: with an earlier version of this change (the same two rules) on v0.33.0, which has the same code in these paths, the real `mistralai/Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512` served with `--config-format hf --load-format safetensors --tokenizer-mode hf` describes a test photo as two elephants. Without the change it answers "I currently cannot view or analyze images directly". This is a single-prompt check, not a benchmark.

**No change for other checkpoints**: method of every linear and MoE layer, built from `config.json` with dummy weights, before vs after:

| checkpoint | layers compared | different |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-FP8 (`ignored_layers` lists every vision layer) | 124 | 0 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 | 124 | 0 |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 | 144 | 0 |
| Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 | 8 | 0 |
| MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2 (short names: `gate`) | 8 | 0 |
| Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512 and Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512, default Mistral format | 11 each | 0 |

`pre-commit run --files` on the four changed files: ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, "Check new tests are wired into Buildkite CI" and the other Python hooks pass, as does the commit-msg hook.

CI: the new model test is in `tests/models/quantization`, run by the "Quantized Models" step, whose source dependencies include `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization`. The shared-expert case runs in the AMD "Model Executor" job (the NVIDIA one is disabled).

## Details

**Root cause.** Two independent steps drop a module entry:

1. `Fp8Config.apply_vllm_mapper` maps entries with the model's rename mapper. Mistral3's prefix rules end with a dot (`"model.vision_tower.": "vision_tower."`), as most multimodal models' do, so the bare module name falls through to the catch-all `"model.": "language_model.model."` and names no layer.
2. `Fp8Config` matches entries exactly, so even `vision_tower` would not match `vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.attention.qkv_proj`. transformers' `should_convert_module` treats an entry as the module and everything inside it.

**Change.**

- `apply_vllm_mapper` keeps the old mapping of each entry and adds the mapping of `entry + "."` with the dot removed. Keeping both means no entry that mapped before is lost, for example a suffix rename of a module name.
- New `Fp8Config.is_layer_excluded(prefix)`: an entry also covers every layer whose name starts with `entry + "."`; otherwise the existing `is_layer_skipped` decides, with the same match mode, fused-shard and expert handling. `get_quant_method` uses it for linear and MoE layers. The method has the same name as ModelOpt's.
- `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` uses the same method for FP8, so the fusion check and `get_quant_method` agree. Without it, ignoring `model.layers.N.mlp.shared_experts` would leave the shared expert unquantized while the check still allowed fusing it into the FP8 routed experts.

The new rule only adds skips. A layer is newly skipped only when a listed name is a parent module of it, and then the checkpoint stores that layer unquantized under transformers' own rule.

**Alternatives.** A model-local fix, as `bailing_moe_v3_vl.py` does (prefix keys without the dot, and `quant_config=None` for a listed tower), would fix only Mistral3. Open PR #44628 switches the FP8 configs to substring matching. That would cover point 2 but not point 1 (the mapped `language_model.model.vision_tower` is no substring of the vision layers), and substring matching is broader than transformers' rule (`layers.1` would also match `layers.10`).

**Why this is not a duplicate.** Open PRs searched with `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search` for "modules_to_not_convert", "fp8 ignored_layers", "Fp8Config", "mistral3 fp8", "Ministral", "vision_tower quantization" and "is_layer_skipped". Besides #44628 (above), none changes how `Fp8Config` matches or maps ignore entries: #58770 discovers block sizes and normalizes Quark prefixes, #61010 aliases draft layer indices, #59978 is for GPTQ/AWQ in MiniCPM-V.

**Limitations.** Other configs map their ignore lists the same way (for example AWQ's `modules_to_not_convert`); they are not changed here. The model-output check above ran the real checkpoint on v0.33.0 with an earlier version of this change; I did not rerun it on main.

issue.title: [Bug] compressed-tensors: a shared expert kept unquantized in `ignore` is still fused into the quantized MoE (Qwen3-Next AWQ fails to load)
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

On CUDA, Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5 and the DeepSeek family fuse the shared expert into the routed experts' `FusedMoE` as one more expert unless the quantization config's `can_fuse_shared_expert()` returns `False` (`qwen2_moe.can_fuse_shared_expert`, `deepseek_common.utils.quant_blocks_shared_experts_fusion`). `ModelOptConfig` and `QuarkConfig` define it, so a shared expert that their exclusion list keeps in BF16 stays a separate MLP (#40628, #46800). `CompressedTensorsConfig` does not define it, so a compressed-tensors checkpoint whose `ignore` list names `mlp.shared_expert.*` is still fused: the loader renames `mlp.shared_expert.*` to `mlp.experts.<num_experts>.*`, and the BF16 `weight` tensors of the shared expert look for parameters that a quantized expert does not have.

`cyankiwi/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` (W4A16, `pack-quantized`, 16k downloads last month) lists every `mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj` in `ignore` and stores them in BF16. On v0.5.23 the server fails while loading:

```
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/qwen3_next.py", line 1247, in load_weights
    param = params_dict[name]
KeyError: 'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.w2_weight'
```

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path cyankiwi/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit --tp 1 --context-length 4096
```

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23 and main `d959849`, 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0.

issue.title: [Bug] GLM-4.7-Flash compressed-tensors W4A16: MLA post-load step reads kv_b_proj.weight, which a packed layer does not have
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin.post_load_weights` builds the MLA absorbed weights from `self_attn.kv_b_proj`: it dequantizes AWQ layers (`qweight`) and otherwise reads `kv_b_proj.weight`. A compressed-tensors `pack-quantized` (W4A16) layer has `weight_packed`, `weight_scale` and `weight_shape` instead, so the step fails:

```
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_lite.py", line 1081, in load_weights
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py", line 639, in post_load_weights
AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

Seen with `cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit` (29k downloads last month; compressed-tensors `pack-quantized`; from layer 1 on, `kv_b_proj` is stored as `weight_packed`/`weight_scale`/`weight_shape`), loading its own tensor names and shapes into a 4-layer model built from its config on v0.5.23. The branch is unchanged on main `d959849` (`deepseek_weight_loader.py`, around line 684). vLLM 0.33.0 loads the same tensors.

The same checkpoint keeps layer 0 in BF16 and lists its projections in `ignore` (`model.layers.0.self_attn.q_a_proj`, `...kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `model.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj`, `...up_proj`, ...). `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM` has an empty `packed_modules_mapping`, so `should_ignore_layer` cannot match the fused `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` and `gate_up_proj` of that layer to their shard entries, and both are built W4A16 over BF16 weights.

#19106 addressed this class of failure for GLM-4.7-Flash compressed-tensors checkpoints (`'ReplicatedLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'`) and was closed for inactivity.

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23, main `d959849`; 1x H20-3e (SM90).

issue.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V2/V2.5 with per-tensor FP8 scales (compressed-tensors): fusing q_a_proj and kv_a_proj_with_mqa concatenates their [1]-shaped scales
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin.do_load_weights` caches `q_a_proj` and `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` tensors and loads them into `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` once both arrived. For scales it handles only 0-d tensors (`shape == torch.Size([])`, the first is used); every other pair is concatenated. compressed-tensors stores static per-tensor FP8 scales with shape `[1]`, so `weight_scale` and `input_scale` of the two projections become a `[2]` tensor, and the fused layer's `[1]` parameter rejects it:

```
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py", line 505, in do_load_weights
  ...
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 376, in weight_loader
AssertionError: param.shape=torch.Size([1]) param.dtype=torch.float32 loaded_weight.shape=torch.Size([2]) loaded_weight.dtype=torch.bfloat16
```

Seen with `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-V2.5-1210-FP8` (31k downloads last month; `float-quantized`, static per-tensor weight and input scales), loading its own tensor names and shapes into a 4-layer model built from its config with `model.load_weights` on v0.5.23. The code is unchanged on main `d959849` (`deepseek_weight_loader.py`, around line 515). vLLM 0.33.0 loads the same tensors.

Every other per-projection tensor takes the same path: for a compressed-tensors `pack-quantized` checkpoint (`cyankiwi/GLM-4.7-Flash-AWQ-4bit`) the two `weight_shape` tensors (`int64`, `[2]`) are concatenated into `[4]` and fail the same assertion.

A `[1]` scale pair needs the 0-d treatment, and when the two projections store different per-tensor scales one fused scale is only right after requantizing one of the two weights to it (as vLLM does for its fused per-tensor FP8 layers).

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23, main `d959849`; 1x H20-3e (SM90).

issue.title: [Bug] compressed-tensors: block-FP8 checkpoints that list modules as targets fail to load (`weight_block_size` is None)
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

`CompressedTensorsConfig.weight_block_size` reads the block structure only from a config group whose target is `"Linear"`. llm-compressor can instead list each quantized module as a target (for example when only some layers are quantized). For such a block-FP8 checkpoint the property returns `None`, the layers are still built with `BlockQuantScaleParameter`, and loading the first one fails:

```
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 2517, in load_weights
    weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, shard_id)
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 1053, in weight_loader_v2
    raw_block_n, _ = weight_block_size[0], weight_block_size[1]
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```

`cbert33/Qwen3.8-27B-TURBO-Fable-Cold-Fusion-735-882-Heretic-Uncensored-FP8-KV-Calibrated` (48k downloads last month) is such a checkpoint: `config_groups.group_0.targets` names each `mlp.{gate,up,down}_proj` and attention projection, with `"strategy": "block"` weights (128x128 blocks) and dynamic group-128 activations.

### Reproduction

```python
from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.compressed_tensors import CompressedTensorsConfig

w = {"num_bits": 8, "type": "float", "strategy": "block", "block_structure": [128, 128], "symmetric": True, "dynamic": False}
cfg = CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config({
    "format": "float-quantized", "quant_method": "compressed-tensors", "ignore": ["lm_head"],
    "config_groups": {"group_0": {"targets": ["model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj"], "weights": w}},
})
print(cfg.weight_block_size)  # None; [128, 128] with "targets": ["Linear"]
```

### Environment

SGLang v0.5.23 and main `d959849`.

issue.title: [Bug] Mixtral, Llama 4 and FP8 Qwen3-MoE: a router stored in FP8 is loaded without its scale, with no error
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Three MoE models build the router without the quantization config: `MixtralMoE` ([mixtral.py#L86-L93](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/mixtral.py#L86-L93), "Gate always runs at half / full precision for now"), Llama 4's `router` ([llama4.py#L97-L103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/llama4.py#L97-L103)), and Qwen3-MoE for every format except ModelSlim ([qwen3_moe.py#L268-L284](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L268-L284); #49185, whose fix #49187 adds compressed-tensors only). Some public checkpoints store the router in FP8 with a `weight_scale`. The unquantized router's only parameter is `weight`, so the FP8 codes are copied into it as numbers (up to ±448) and `weight_scale`, which has no parameter, is skipped. The router logits are then off by the scale, which in these checkpoints differs per expert, so tokens are routed to other experts. The server starts and serves: Mixtral and Llama 4 log one warning per layer (`Parameter model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight_scale not found in params_dict`), and Qwen3-MoE skips the name without a message.

Layer 0's real router tensors through SGLang v0.5.23's load step, compared with the checkpoint's dequantized weights (`x @ (codes * scale)^T`, random input):

| Checkpoint | Format | Router output max | Reference max | Relative error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D` | fp8 | 7,264 | 5.07 | 1,431 |
| `frankmorales2020/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-fp8` | compressed-tensors | 7,264 | 5.07 | 1,432 |
| `sh0ck0r/L3-Arcania-4x8b-FP8-Dynamic` (Mixtral) | compressed-tensors | 22,016 | 2.92 | 7,394 |
| `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10` (Llama 4) | compressed-tensors | 16,320 | 12.45 | 1,196 |
| `SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8` (Qwen3-MoE) | fp8 | 3,920 | 12.99 | 301 |

In the same runs, layer 0's `o_proj` (FP8, built with the config) matches its reference to a relative error of 0.027 (the checkpoints with dynamic activation scales). vLLM 0.33.0 also builds the Mixtral and Llama 4 router without the config, but refuses these checkpoints at load (`There is no module or parameter named 'layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight_scale'`); it builds the Qwen3-MoE router with the config and reads `nomos-1-fp8`'s router right (0.024).

Public checkpoints whose safetensors store the router as FP8 with a `weight_scale` (Hugging Face models tagged compressed-tensors or fp8): Mixtral: the three above, `CalamitousFelicitousness/SorcererLM-8x22b-FP8-Dynamic`, `Model-SafeTensors/mistralai-Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1`, `Model-SafeTensors/mistralai-Mixtral-8x22B`; Llama 4: `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10`; Qwen3-MoE in fp8 format: `SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8`.

### A fix has to follow what the checkpoint stores

Building the router with the quantization config is not enough. Of the 238 public Qwen3-MoE, Mixtral and Llama 4 checkpoints with a compressed-tensors or fp8 config, 10 store the router in BF16 although their config would quantize it, for example `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-KV`, `RedHatAI/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-AutoFP8`, `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-w4a16-llmcompressor` and `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static`. These load right today because the router is never quantized. On `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static`, a router built with the config (the change in #49187) outputs NaN, against a relative error of 0.0017 as released; vLLM 0.33.0, which builds this router with the config, reads it wrong too (relative error 1.0). So the router should be built quantized only when the checkpoint stores it quantized.

### Reproduction

```python
# Which tensors a checkpoint stores for layer 0's router (safetensors headers only).
from huggingface_hub import get_safetensors_metadata
for repo, router in [("anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D", "model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate"),
                     ("Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10", "model.layers.0.feed_forward.router"),
                     ("SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8", "model.layers.0.mlp.gate"),
                     ("AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static", "model.layers.0.mlp.gate")]:
    md = get_safetensors_metadata(repo)
    print(repo, {n: t.dtype for f in md.files_metadata.values() for n, t in f.tensors.items() if n.startswith(router + ".")})
```

```
anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D {'model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight': 'F8_E4M3', 'model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight_scale': 'F32'}
Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10 {'model.layers.0.feed_forward.router.weight': 'F8_E4M3', 'model.layers.0.feed_forward.router.weight_scale': 'BF16'}
SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8 {'model.layers.0.mlp.gate.weight': 'F8_E4M3', 'model.layers.0.mlp.gate.weight_scale': 'F32'}
AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static {'model.layers.0.mlp.gate.weight': 'BF16'}
```

With SGLang, `model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight` of the first checkpoint loads into a BF16 parameter as values between -448 and 448, and `weight_scale` is skipped.

### Environment

- 1x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1
- SGLang v0.5.23 (layer checks), main `4003bf1` (code links); vLLM 0.33.0 (comparison)

comment.body:

| Run | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| v0.5.23 as released (router built without the quantization config) | 72.6% |
| v0.5.23 with `mixtral.py` building `block_sparse_moe.gate` with the model's `quant_config` | 86.7% |
