As released, the server logs `Parameter model.layers.N.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight_scale not found in params_dict` once per layer on each rank and then serves without an error. vLLM 0.33.0 refuses this checkpoint at load, as above.

issue.title: [Bug] TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM / TorchNativePhi3ForCausalLM build plain torch.nn.Linear layers, so a quantized checkpoint's weights load without their scales
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM` (and `TorchNativePhi3ForCausalLM`, its subclass) takes a `quant_config` but builds every projection as a plain `torch.nn.Linear` in the model dtype: `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj` ([torch_native_llama.py#L116-L126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/620413be1a8e78c9d22563c7ad86a4a77f401647/python/sglang/srt/models/torch_native_llama.py#L116-L126)), `qkv_proj` and `o_proj` ([#L217-L234](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/620413be1a8e78c9d22563c7ad86a4a77f401647/python/sglang/srt/models/torch_native_llama.py#L217-L234)). The quantization config never reaches them. With a quantized checkpoint, `load_weights_to_module` copies the stored codes into the BF16 weight as numbers, and skips `weight_scale` and `input_scale`, which have no parameter ([#L479-L490](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/620413be1a8e78c9d22563c7ad86a4a77f401647/python/sglang/srt/models/torch_native_llama.py#L479-L490): `name not in params_dict`). Nothing is logged.

This shows once the loading problem of #48917 is fixed (#48918); without that fix, nothing loads at all. With #48918's change applied to SGLang v0.5.23, `RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8` (compressed-tensors FP8, one weight scale per tensor, e.g. 0.00166 for layer 0's `q_proj`) loads 15.0 GB of weights, the BF16 size of an 8B model, and every weight comes out about 600 times too large:

| Model class | GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy) |
|---|---|
| `LlamaForCausalLM` (default) | 76.3% |
| `TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM`, v0.5.23 | 0.0% (no answer parses) |
| `TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM`, v0.5.23 + #48918 | 0.2% |

On an unquantized checkpoint (`meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B`, BF16), the TorchNative class with #48918 scores 7.1% against 6.6% for the default class in the same setup, so the loss above comes from the quantized weights.

Two ways out: build the projections with the parallel linear layers that take the quantization config, as `llama.py` does, or refuse a checkpoint with a quantization config in the TorchNative classes instead of serving it.

### Reproduction

```python
# The checkpoint stores FP8 codes with a per-tensor scale (safetensors headers only).
from huggingface_hub import get_safetensors_metadata
md = get_safetensors_metadata("RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8")
print({n: (t.dtype, t.shape) for f in md.files_metadata.values() for n, t in f.tensors.items()
       if n.startswith("model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.")})
```

```
{'model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.input_scale': ('BF16', [1]), 'model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight_scale': ('BF16', [1]), 'model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight': ('F8_E4M3', [4096, 4096])}
```

```bash
# with #48918 applied
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 --tp 1 --port 30000 \
  --json-model-override-args '{"architectures": ["TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM"]}'
```

GSM8K against the server's completions endpoint (5-shot, temperature 0, 256 tokens), the same client for every row of the table. Without `--json-model-override-args` the same command serves the default class.

### Environment

- 1x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1
- SGLang v0.5.23 with #48918's change to `torch_native_llama.py` (served runs); main `620413b` (code links)

issue.title: [Fix] qwen3_moe/mixtral/llama4: Build the MoE router as the checkpoint stores it
issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #49185. Fixes #49198.

Qwen3-MoE builds the MoE router (`mlp.gate`) with the quantization config only for ModelSlim, and Mixtral (`block_sparse_moe.gate`) and Llama 4 (`feed_forward.router`) never. A checkpoint can store the router quantized, and SGLang then misreads it without an error:

- compressed-tensors W4A16 (`weight_packed`, `weight_scale`, `weight_shape`), as in `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16`: the unquantized router has no parameter for these names, so they are skipped and the router keeps its initial weight (#49185: GSM8K 0.0%).
- FP8 with a `weight_scale` (fp8 or compressed-tensors), as in `SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8`, `anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D` or `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10` (Llama 4): the FP8 codes are copied into the BF16 weight as numbers and the scale is skipped (#49198).

Some checkpoints do the opposite: they store the router in BF16 although their config would quantize it, for example `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static`, `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-KV` and `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-w4a16-llmcompressor` (10 of the 238 public Qwen3-MoE, Mixtral and Llama 4 checkpoints with a compressed-tensors or fp8 config). They load right today, and building the router from the config alone breaks them. So the router is built from the config and rebuilt unquantized when the checkpoint stores it unquantized.

## Modifications

- `models/utils.py`:
  - `router_quant_config(quant_config)` returns the config for ModelSlim, compressed-tensors and fp8, and `None` for every other format as before.
  - `unquantize_router_if_stored_so(...)`, called by `load_weights` before it loads a name: if the name is the `weight` of a router built quantized and the checkpoint stores it as a 16- or 32-bit float tensor, it rebuilds the router as an unquantized `ReplicatedLinear` and updates `params_dict`. This also keeps the router in 16 bits when a 16-bit checkpoint is quantized to fp8 at load, as before.
- `qwen3_moe.py`: the router uses `router_quant_config`, and `load_weights` calls the helper. The ModelSlim path is unchanged.
- `mixtral.py`: the same.
- `llama4.py`: the router uses `router_quant_config`; `llama.py` (the text model's `load_weights`) and `mllama4.py` (`Llama4ForConditionalGeneration.load_weights`) call the helper for `feed_forward.router`.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_moe_router_quant_config.py`:
  - the scheme each router resolves to for the two `ignore` layouts found on the Hub (W4A16, or none);
  - the formats `router_quant_config` passes through;
  - the rebuild: a router built quantized is rebuilt for a BF16, FP16 or FP32 `weight` and kept for an FP8 one, and other names and unquantized routers are left alone.

Two behavior changes for checkpoints that were misread before:

- Three compressed-tensors Qwen3-MoE checkpoints store the router in a format with no compressed-tensors scheme in SGLang (`nm-testing/Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4A16`, `inference-optimization/Qwen3-30B-A3B-INT3xFP8`, `inference-optimization/Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4xFP8`). Building their router now raises `No compressed-tensors compatible scheme was found`.
- `frankmorales2020/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-fp8` (compressed-tensors FP8 with static activation scales) now builds its router as W8A8-FP8, and that GEMM rejects the router's 8 outputs at the first forward (`mat2 shape (4096x8) must be divisible by 16`).

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0. Unit test and pre-commit run on main `4003bf1` with this PR. Layer checks and served runs use v0.5.23 with the same changes applied to its files.

- Unit test: 7 tests OK (main does not have the helpers).
- Layer 0's real router tensors through the model's `load_weights` and post-load step, compared with the checkpoint's dequantized weights (random input). Relative error:

  | Checkpoint | Router stored as | v0.5.23 | v0.5.23 + this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16` | W4A16 | NaN (never written) | 0.0056 |
  | `SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8` (Qwen3-MoE) | FP8 | 301 | 0.024 |
  | `anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D` | FP8 | 1,431 | 0.025 |
  | `sh0ck0r/L3-Arcania-4x8b-FP8-Dynamic` (Mixtral) | FP8, compressed-tensors | 7,394 | 0.026 |
  | `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static` | BF16; the config quantizes it | 0.0017 | 0.0017 |
  | `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-KV` | BF16; the config quantizes it | 0.0014 | 0.0014 |
  | `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-w4a16-llmcompressor` | BF16; the config quantizes it | 0.0014 | 0.0014 |
  | `cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` | BF16, in `ignore` | 0.0016 | 0.0016 |
  | `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10` (Llama 4) | FP8, compressed-tensors | 1,196 | 0.027 |
  | `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8-dynamic` | BF16, in `ignore` | 0.0016 | 0.0016 |

  The BF16 rows are BF16 rounding, and the FP8 rows the FP8 rounding of the layer's own `o_proj` (0.027 for `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10`). With the first commit alone, which built the router from the config only, `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static` gave NaN.
- GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy). The second commit builds these two routers as the first did:

  | Checkpoint | v0.5.23 | v0.5.23 + this PR | vLLM 0.33.0 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16` | 0.0% (every answer invalid) | 85.7% | 85.4% |
  | `cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` (router in `ignore`) | 89.0% | 90.1% | |

  On the cyankiwi checkpoint, two v0.5.23 runs differ in their served answers as often as a v0.5.23 run and a run with the change do.

issue.title: [Bug] DFlash draft model: fp8 `ignored_layers` are not aliased to global layer indices, so excluded bf16 projections are loaded into fp8 parameters (acceptance drops from 4.3 to 1.0)
issue.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.31.1rc1.dev173+g8cbd5d030 (nightly ROCm 10 image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-8cbd5d03`), torch 2.12+rocm10.0, 2x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), TP=2. Reproduced with no out-of-tree plugin code active in the model (only a platform plugin that does not touch the draft model); the issue is in the stock draft-model construction path.

### Description

Target: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (compressed-tensors NVFP4, 64 layers). Drafter: an FP8 block-128 conversion of `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (`DFlash2DraftModel`, 5 layers, `quant_method: fp8`, `weight_block_size: [128, 128]`). The drafter's `quantization_config.modules_to_not_convert` has 45 entries naming the modules its quantization must skip by checkpoint-local layer index, e.g.

```
layers.0.attention_conv.base_kernel
layers.0.attention_conv.kernel_projection
layers.0.mlp_conv.base_kernel
layers.0.mlp_conv.kernel_projection
layers.0.input_layernorm
...
```

vLLM builds the draft layers at global indices after the target's layers (`start_layer_id` = 64 for this target), and `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py::_add_global_draft_layer_exclusions` (called from the draft model's `__init__` with `start_layer_id`) exists to add the globally-numbered aliases. It only patches `quant_config.exclude_modules`:

```python
exclusions = getattr(quant_config, "exclude_modules", None)
if not isinstance(exclusions, list):
    return
```

`Fp8Config` has no `exclude_modules`; `from_config` reads `modules_to_not_convert` into `ignored_layers`, and `ignored_layers_match_mode` is `"exact"` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py`). So the global name `layers.64.attention_conv.kernel_projection` never matches, the grouped-conv kernel projections are built as fp8 linears, and the loader logs

```
Attempted to load weight layers.0.attention_conv.kernel_projection.weight with dtype torch.bfloat16 into parameter with dtype torch.float8_e4m3fn
```

Outputs stay correct (the target verifies every draft), but the drafter degrades: acceptance falls from 4.3 to 1.03 tokens per step and decode throughput from ~210 to 46 tok/s. On the September nightly (`e97573215`) the same checkpoint was fine, because those projections were constructed with `quant_config=None` there; the regression appeared when the draft quant config started reaching them.

### Fix

Apply the same aliasing to `ignored_layers` (and any other exclusion list a quant config carries), e.g. in `_add_global_draft_layer_exclusions`:

```python
for attr in ("exclude_modules", "ignored_layers"):
    exclusions = getattr(quant_config, attr, None)
    if isinstance(exclusions, list):
        ...  # same offset_local_layer substitution
```

Working around it from outside (adding `layers.{i+start}` and `model.layers.{i+start}` aliases to the draft hf config's `modules_to_not_convert` before construction) restores 4.48 tokens per step on this nightly.

### Reproduction

```
vllm serve unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative-config '{"model": "<fp8 conversion of z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2>", "num_speculative_tokens": 7}'
```

then watch for the dtype-mismatch load message above and `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total / vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total` in `/metrics` during a decode (~1.0 per draft instead of ~4.3).

comment.body:
Some data on how far this reaches. I built drafts through vLLM's own speculative path (`EngineArgs` with a speculative config, `initialize_model` with the draft's model config, dummy weights), with a quantization config in the draft's `config.json` that leaves every Linear of draft layer 0 unquantized by its checkpoint names, and read each Linear's quantization method. Same results on 0.33.0 and nightly (`14d147a`):

| Exclusion list | DFlash / DFlash2 / DSpark drafts | EAGLE-3 drafts |
|---|---|---|
| `fp8`, `modules_to_not_convert` | every Linear of layer 0 built FP8 | every Linear of layer 0 built FP8 |
| compressed-tensors FP8, `ignore` | every Linear of layer 0 built FP8 | every Linear of layer 0 built FP8 |
| ModelOpt FP8, `exclude_modules` | only the fused `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj` built FP8 | every Linear of layer 0 built FP8 |

Drafts: `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16`, `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat`, `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2`, `ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-9B-DFlash`, `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark`, `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3`, `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.eagle3`, `nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-short-context`, `lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla`.

`map_draft_quant_config` is called only from `qwen3_dflash.py`, so #61010, which aliases `exclude_modules` and `ignored_layers` there, does not reach the EAGLE-3 drafts, and compressed-tensors' `ignore` list is not aliased for any draft. With ModelOpt FP8, the fused layers miss even where `exclude_modules` is aliased.

With their own configs, the only public quantized draft I found affected today is an FP8 conversion like the one here, `tcclaviger/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-FP8` (45 `modules_to_not_convert` entries): 10 of its 34 Linear layers are built FP8 although stored in BF16. The ModelOpt NVFP4 and compressed-tensors DFlash2/DSpark drafts on the Hub exclude by pattern or are matched, so the other cases above wait for a checkpoint that triggers them.

issue.title: [Bug] DFlash and EAGLE-3 drafts build their layers without layer names, so a draft's quantization exclusions never match
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

A quantized draft checkpoint names the layers its quantization skips (`modules_to_not_convert`, `ignore` or `exclude_modules`) by their checkpoint names, such as `layers.0.self_attn.q_proj`. SGLang matches these names against the `prefix` each Linear layer is built with, but two draft classes build their decoder layers without the layer's name:

- `DFlashDraftModel` sets `supports_quantization = False` ([dflash.py#L858](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py#L858)), so `quantizable` is false for every DFlash and DFlash2 draft except Nemotron 3.5 ([#L889](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py#L889)), and the layers get the prefix `""` ([#L912-L927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py#L912-L927)). They still get the draft's `quant_config` (L918), so their projections are built quantized under the names `qkv_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj`.
- `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3` passes the model's own prefix to its decoder layer ([llama_eagle3.py#L201](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/llama_eagle3.py#L201)), so the layer's projections are named `model.self_attn.qkv_proj` and so on, without `midlayer` or `layers.0`.

An exclusion list can therefore never match a draft layer: a draft layer the checkpoint keeps in BF16 is built quantized and its BF16 weights are loaded into quantized parameters. A config that targets layers by name fails instead: `JRamirez-UAB/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-W4A16` does not load (`ValueError: Unable to find matching target for qkv_proj in the compressed-tensors config`).

I built each draft through SGLang's draft path (`ModelConfig.from_server_args(..., is_draft_model=True)`, the loader's `_get_quantization_config` and `_initialize_model`, dummy weights) with a quantization config added to the draft's own `config.json` that excludes every Linear of draft layer 0 by its checkpoint names, in three formats: `fp8` with `modules_to_not_convert`, compressed-tensors FP8 with `ignore`, and ModelOpt FP8 with `exclude_modules`. On SGLang v0.5.23, in every format, every Linear of layer 0 is built quantized:

| Draft | Class | Layer-0 Linears built quantized |
|---|---|---|
| `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` | DFlashDraftModel | 4 of 4 |
| `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat` | DFlashDraftModel | 4 of 4 |
| `ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-9B-DFlash` | DFlashDraftModel | 4 of 4 |
| `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` | DFlash2DraftModel | 4 of 4 |
| `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` | DFlash2DraftModel | 4 of 4 |
| `nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-short-context` | LlamaForCausalLMEagle3 | 4 of 4 |
| `lightseekorg/kimi-k2.6-eagle3-mla` | Eagle3DeepseekV2ForCausalLM | 6 of 6 |

The other layers, which the config quantizes, are built quantized as they should be. The public quantized DFlash2 drafts I tried with their own configs load right today, only because their exclusions name modules that SGLang does not build as quantized Linears (`kernel_projection`, `candidate_selector`) or use patterns; a draft that keeps a whole layer in BF16 would be misread.

### Reproduction

Add to the `config.json` of `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16`:

```json
"quantization_config": {"quant_method": "fp8", "activation_scheme": "dynamic", "weight_block_size": [128, 128],
  "modules_to_not_convert": ["layers.0.self_attn.q_proj", "layers.0.self_attn.k_proj", "layers.0.self_attn.v_proj",
                             "layers.0.self_attn.o_proj", "layers.0.mlp.gate_proj", "layers.0.mlp.up_proj",
                             "layers.0.mlp.down_proj"]}
```

and build it as the draft of `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` (`--speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-draft-model-path <dir>`): `layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj`, `o_proj`, `mlp.gate_up_proj` and `down_proj` all get `Fp8LinearMethod` with float8 weights, and the BF16 checkpoint weights of layer 0 are loaded into them.

### Environment

- 1x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1
- SGLang v0.5.23; code links at main `4003bf1`

issue.title: [Fix] qwen3_moe/mixtral/llama4: Build the MoE router as the checkpoint stores it
issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #49185. Fixes #49198.

Qwen3-MoE builds the MoE router (`mlp.gate`) with the quantization config only for ModelSlim, and Mixtral (`block_sparse_moe.gate`) and Llama 4 (`feed_forward.router`) never. A checkpoint can store the router quantized, and SGLang then misreads it without an error:

- compressed-tensors W4A16 (`weight_packed`, `weight_scale`, `weight_shape`), as in `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16`: the unquantized router has no parameter for these names, so they are skipped and the router keeps its initial weight (#49185: GSM8K 0.0%).
- FP8 with a `weight_scale` (fp8 or compressed-tensors), as in `SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8`, `anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D` or `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10` (Llama 4): the FP8 codes are copied into the BF16 weight as numbers and the scale is skipped (#49198).

Some checkpoints do the opposite: they store the router in BF16 although their config would quantize it, for example `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static`, `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-KV` and `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-w4a16-llmcompressor` (10 of the 238 public Qwen3-MoE, Mixtral and Llama 4 checkpoints with a compressed-tensors or fp8 config). They load right today, and building the router from the config alone breaks them. So the router is built from the config and rebuilt unquantized when the checkpoint stores it unquantized.

## Modifications

- `models/utils.py`:
  - `router_quant_config(quant_config)` returns the config for ModelSlim, compressed-tensors and fp8, and `None` for every other format as before.
  - `unquantize_router_if_stored_so(...)`, called by `load_weights` before it loads a name: if the name is the `weight` of a router built quantized and the checkpoint stores it as a 16- or 32-bit float tensor, it rebuilds the router as an unquantized `ReplicatedLinear` and updates `params_dict`. This also keeps the router in 16 bits when a 16-bit checkpoint is quantized to fp8 at load, as before.
- `qwen3_moe.py`: the router uses `router_quant_config`, and `load_weights` calls the helper. The ModelSlim path is unchanged.
- `mixtral.py`: the same.
- `llama4.py`: the router uses `router_quant_config`; `llama.py` (the text model's `load_weights`) and `mllama4.py` (`Llama4ForConditionalGeneration.load_weights`) call the helper for `feed_forward.router`.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_moe_router_quant_config.py`:
  - the scheme each router resolves to for the two `ignore` layouts found on the Hub (W4A16, or none);
  - the formats `router_quant_config` passes through;
  - the rebuild: a router built quantized is rebuilt for a BF16, FP16 or FP32 `weight` and kept for an FP8 one, and other names and unquantized routers are left alone.

Two behavior changes for checkpoints that were misread before:

- Three compressed-tensors Qwen3-MoE checkpoints store the router in a format with no compressed-tensors scheme in SGLang (`nm-testing/Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4A16`, `inference-optimization/Qwen3-30B-A3B-INT3xFP8`, `inference-optimization/Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4xFP8`). Building their router now raises `No compressed-tensors compatible scheme was found`.
- `frankmorales2020/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-fp8` (compressed-tensors FP8 with static activation scales) now builds its router as W8A8-FP8, and that GEMM rejects the router's 8 outputs at the first forward (`mat2 shape (4096x8) must be divisible by 16`).

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0. Unit test and pre-commit run on main `4003bf1` with this PR. Layer checks and served runs use v0.5.23 with the same changes applied to its files.

- Unit test: 7 tests OK (main does not have the helpers).
- Layer 0's real router tensors through the model's `load_weights` and post-load step, compared with the checkpoint's dequantized weights (random input). Relative error:

  | Checkpoint | Router stored as | v0.5.23 | v0.5.23 + this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16` | W4A16 | NaN (never written) | 0.0056 |
  | `SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8` (Qwen3-MoE) | FP8 | 301 | 0.024 |
  | `anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D` | FP8 | 1,431 | 0.025 |
  | `sh0ck0r/L3-Arcania-4x8b-FP8-Dynamic` (Mixtral) | FP8, compressed-tensors | 7,394 | 0.026 |
  | `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static` | BF16; the config quantizes it | 0.0017 | 0.0017 |
  | `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-KV` | BF16; the config quantizes it | 0.0014 | 0.0014 |
  | `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-w4a16-llmcompressor` | BF16; the config quantizes it | 0.0014 | 0.0014 |
  | `cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` | BF16, in `ignore` | 0.0016 | 0.0016 |
  | `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10` (Llama 4) | FP8, compressed-tensors | 1,196 | 0.027 |
  | `RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8-dynamic` | BF16, in `ignore` | 0.0016 | 0.0016 |

  The BF16 rows are BF16 rounding, and the FP8 rows the FP8 rounding of the layer's own `o_proj` (0.027 for `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10`). With the first commit alone, which built the router from the config only, `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static` gave NaN.
- GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy). The second commit builds these two routers as the first did:

  | Checkpoint | v0.5.23 | v0.5.23 + this PR | vLLM 0.33.0 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16` | 0.0% (every answer invalid) | 85.7% | 85.4% |
  | `cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` (router in `ignore`) | 89.0% | 90.1% | |

  On the cyankiwi checkpoint, two v0.5.23 runs differ in their served answers as often as a v0.5.23 run and a run with the change do.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

issue.title: [Bug] Mixtral, Llama 4 and FP8 Qwen3-MoE: a router stored in FP8 is loaded without its scale, with no error
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Three MoE models build the router without the quantization config: `MixtralMoE` ([mixtral.py#L86-L93](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/mixtral.py#L86-L93), "Gate always runs at half / full precision for now"), Llama 4's `router` ([llama4.py#L97-L103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/llama4.py#L97-L103)), and Qwen3-MoE for every format except ModelSlim ([qwen3_moe.py#L268-L284](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L268-L284); #49185, whose fix #49187 adds compressed-tensors only). Some public checkpoints store the router in FP8 with a `weight_scale`. The unquantized router's only parameter is `weight`, so the FP8 codes are copied into it as numbers (up to ±448) and `weight_scale`, which has no parameter, is skipped. The router logits are then off by the scale, which in these checkpoints differs per expert, so tokens are routed to other experts. The server starts and serves: Mixtral and Llama 4 log one warning per layer (`Parameter model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight_scale not found in params_dict`), and Qwen3-MoE skips the name without a message.

Layer 0's real router tensors through SGLang v0.5.23's load step, compared with the checkpoint's dequantized weights (`x @ (codes * scale)^T`, random input):

| Checkpoint | Format | Router output max | Reference max | Relative error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D` | fp8 | 7,264 | 5.07 | 1,431 |
| `frankmorales2020/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-fp8` | compressed-tensors | 7,264 | 5.07 | 1,432 |
| `sh0ck0r/L3-Arcania-4x8b-FP8-Dynamic` (Mixtral) | compressed-tensors | 22,016 | 2.92 | 7,394 |
| `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10` (Llama 4) | compressed-tensors | 16,320 | 12.45 | 1,196 |
| `SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8` (Qwen3-MoE) | fp8 | 3,920 | 12.99 | 301 |

In the same runs, layer 0's `o_proj` (FP8, built with the config) matches its reference to a relative error of 0.027 (the checkpoints with dynamic activation scales). vLLM 0.33.0 also builds the Mixtral and Llama 4 router without the config, but refuses these checkpoints at load (`There is no module or parameter named 'layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight_scale'`); it builds the Qwen3-MoE router with the config and reads `nomos-1-fp8`'s router right (0.024).

Public checkpoints whose safetensors store the router as FP8 with a `weight_scale` (Hugging Face models tagged compressed-tensors or fp8): Mixtral: the three above, `CalamitousFelicitousness/SorcererLM-8x22b-FP8-Dynamic`, `Model-SafeTensors/mistralai-Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1`, `Model-SafeTensors/mistralai-Mixtral-8x22B`; Llama 4: `Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10`; Qwen3-MoE in fp8 format: `SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8`.

### A fix has to follow what the checkpoint stores

Building the router with the quantization config is not enough. Of the 238 public Qwen3-MoE, Mixtral and Llama 4 checkpoints with a compressed-tensors or fp8 config, 10 store the router in BF16 although their config would quantize it, for example `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-KV`, `RedHatAI/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-AutoFP8`, `amd/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-w4a16-llmcompressor` and `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static`. These load right today because the router is never quantized. On `AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static`, a router built with the config (the change in #49187) outputs NaN, against a relative error of 0.0017 as released; vLLM 0.33.0, which builds this router with the config, reads it wrong too (relative error 1.0). So the router should be built quantized only when the checkpoint stores it quantized.

### Reproduction

```python
# Which tensors a checkpoint stores for layer 0's router (safetensors headers only).
from huggingface_hub import get_safetensors_metadata
for repo, router in [("anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D", "model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate"),
                     ("Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10", "model.layers.0.feed_forward.router"),
                     ("SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8", "model.layers.0.mlp.gate"),
                     ("AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static", "model.layers.0.mlp.gate")]:
    md = get_safetensors_metadata(repo)
    print(repo, {n: t.dtype for f in md.files_metadata.values() for n, t in f.tensors.items() if n.startswith(router + ".")})
```

```
anyisalin/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-FP8-D {'model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight': 'F8_E4M3', 'model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight_scale': 'F32'}
Sathvik265/8bit-epoch-10 {'model.layers.0.feed_forward.router.weight': 'F8_E4M3', 'model.layers.0.feed_forward.router.weight_scale': 'BF16'}
SalmanHabeeb/nomos-1-fp8 {'model.layers.0.mlp.gate.weight': 'F8_E4M3', 'model.layers.0.mlp.gate.weight_scale': 'F32'}
AngelSlim/Qwen3-30B-A3B_fp8_static {'model.layers.0.mlp.gate.weight': 'BF16'}
```

With SGLang, `model.layers.0.block_sparse_moe.gate.weight` of the first checkpoint loads into a BF16 parameter as values between -448 and 448, and `weight_scale` is skipped.

### Environment

- 1x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1
- SGLang v0.5.23 (layer checks), main `4003bf1` (code links); vLLM 0.33.0 (comparison)

issue.title: [Bug] Whisper: fc1/fc2 are built without the quantization config, so a quantized checkpoint transcribes nothing
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`WhisperEncoderLayer` and `WhisperDecoderLayer` build `fc1` and `fc2` without the quantization config ([whisper.py#L161-L162](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/whisper.py#L161-L162), [#L230-L231](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/whisper.py#L230-L231)), while the attention projections of the same layers get it. A checkpoint that quantizes the feed-forward layers therefore loads into unquantized `fc1`/`fc2` parameters:

- When the stored tensors have names the unquantized layer lacks (W4A16: `weight_packed`, `weight_scale`, `weight_shape`), `load_weights` skips them without a message ([whisper.py#L415-L416](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/whisper.py#L415-L416)), and `fc1`/`fc2` keep their initial weights.

`Yehor/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized-uk` (32,233 downloads in the last 30 days) is W4A16 on every Linear layer with no `ignore` list. Loading layer 0's real tensors through SGLang's own load and post-load step, encoder and decoder `fc1` output only their bias (relative error 0.99 against the checkpoint's dequantized weights), while `self_attn.qkv_proj` of the same layers reads its W4A16 weights right.

The server starts with default flags and returns HTTP 200 with an empty `text` for every request. `/v1/audio/transcriptions` on the first 10 clips of `hf-internal-testing/librispeech_asr_dummy`, `language=en`, `temperature=0`, one H20, SGLang v0.5.23 (main `4003bf1` has the same code). Word error rate, lower case, punctuation removed:

| | Word error rate |
|---|---|
| SGLang v0.5.23, `Yehor/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized-uk` | 100% (every transcript empty) |
| SGLang v0.5.23 with `fc1`/`fc2` built with `quant_config`, same checkpoint | 6.3% |
| vLLM 0.33.0, same checkpoint | 6.3% |
| SGLang v0.5.23, `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo` (BF16 source model) | 6.3% |


Passing `quant_config=quant_config` to the four layers is the change in the second row. A `prefix` for them (and for the attention projections, which have none today) would also let an `ignore` list that names Whisper layers match them, as #37848 describes for other models.

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Yehor/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized-uk --port 30000
```

```python
import requests
from datasets import load_dataset  # or any 16 kHz English speech file

ds = load_dataset("hf-internal-testing/librispeech_asr_dummy", "clean", split="validation")
import io, soundfile as sf
buf = io.BytesIO(); sf.write(buf, ds[0]["audio"]["array"], 16000, format="WAV"); buf.seek(0)
r = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/audio/transcriptions",
                  files={"file": ("clip.wav", buf, "audio/wav")},
                  data={"model": "Yehor/whisper-large-v3-turbo-quantized-uk", "language": "en", "temperature": "0"})
print(r.status_code, repr(r.json()["text"]))  # 200 '' ; reference: "MISTER QUILTER IS THE APOSTLE OF THE MIDDLE CLASSES ..."
```

### Environment

- 1x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1
- SGLang v0.5.23 (served runs), main `4003bf1` (code links); vLLM 0.33.0 (comparison)

issue.title: [Bug] Qwen3-MoE: a router stored quantized (compressed-tensors) is never loaded, and the server answers garbage without an error
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock` builds the MoE router (`mlp.gate`) with the quantization config only when the format is ModelSlim, and with `quant_config=None` otherwise ([qwen3_moe.py#L268-L284](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L268-L284)). A compressed-tensors checkpoint can store the router quantized too. `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16` (38,425 downloads in the last 30 days) lists only `lm_head` in `ignore` and stores every layer's router as `mlp.gate.weight_packed`, `weight_scale` and `weight_shape`. SGLang builds an unquantized `ReplicatedLinear` whose only parameter is `weight`, so none of the stored names has a parameter, and `load_weights` skips them without a message ([qwen3_moe.py#L1246-L1247](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L1246-L1247); the warning for a name with no parameter, [#L1256](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/4003bf1077debcca3fccfa6e0d7b56ed584aa727/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L1256), is never reached because of that `continue`). The router weight is never written: loading layer 0's real tensors through SGLang's own load and post-load step, the router outputs NaN for all 128 experts, where the reference computed from the checkpoint's tensors reaches 9.5, while `self_attn.o_proj` of the same checkpoint (W4A16) matches the reference to a relative error of 0.002.

The server starts with default flags and raises no error. On one H20 with SGLang v0.5.23 (main `4003bf1` has the same code), every prompt is answered with backslashes or line breaks (`\\\\\\\\...`, `\r\n\r\n\r\n...`). GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy):

| | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| SGLang v0.5.23 | 0.0% (every answer invalid) |
| SGLang v0.5.23, router built with the quantization config | 85.7% |
| vLLM 0.33.0 (builds the Qwen3-MoE router with the quantization config) | 85.4% |

The change for the second row is one condition: pass `quant_config` to the router for `compressed_tensors` as well, so the checkpoint's `ignore` list decides per layer. Other compressed-tensors Qwen3-MoE checkpoints keep the router in BF16 and list it in `ignore`, so they are unaffected: of the eight below, only RedHatAI's stores the router quantized, and it is the only one whose config asks for a quantized router. On the most downloaded of them, `cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit` (503,059 downloads), GSM8K is 89.0% as released and 90.1% with the change, and two release runs differ in their served answers as often as a release run and a run with the change do.

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16 --port 30000
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "The capital of France is", "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0}'
```

`repro.py` reads only `config.json` and the safetensors index of eight compressed-tensors Qwen3-MoE checkpoints, prints which router tensors each stores, and asks SGLang's compressed-tensors config what it would build for `model.layers.0.mlp.gate` if the router were given the config.

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# Which compressed-tensors Qwen3-MoE checkpoints store the MoE router (mlp.gate) quantized, and what SGLang's
# compressed-tensors config would decide for it if Qwen3MoeSparseMoeBlock passed the config to the router. Reads
# config.json and model.safetensors.index.json only; no GPU.
import json

from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.compressed_tensors import CompressedTensorsConfig
from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.utils import should_ignore_layer
from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_moe import Qwen3MoeForCausalLM

REPOS = ["RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16", "cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit",
         "cyankiwi/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-AWQ-4bit", "stelterlab/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-AWQ",
         "stelterlab/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ", "dark-side-of-the-code/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ",
         "YuYu1015/Huihui-Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-abliterated-NVFP4", "null-space/Qwen3-235B-A22B-abliterated-FP8"]
for repo in REPOS:
    q = json.load(open(hf_hub_download(repo, "config.json")))["quantization_config"]
    q["packed_modules_mapping"] = dict(getattr(Qwen3MoeForCausalLM, "packed_modules_mapping", {}))
    cfg = CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config(q)
    w = json.load(open(hf_hub_download(repo, "model.safetensors.index.json")))["weight_map"]
    stored = sorted({k.rsplit(".", 1)[1] for k in w if k.startswith("model.layers.0.mlp.gate.")})
    ignored = should_ignore_layer("model.layers.0.mlp.gate", ignore=cfg.ignore, fused_mapping=cfg.packed_modules_mapping)
    print(f"{repo:62s} stored router: {','.join(stored):35s} config says: {'BF16 (ignored)' if ignored else 'QUANTIZED'}")
```

</details>

Output on SGLang v0.5.23:

```
RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-quantized.w4a16           stored router: weight_packed,weight_scale,weight_shape config says: QUANTIZED
cyankiwi/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ-4bit                 stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
cyankiwi/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-AWQ-4bit                  stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
stelterlab/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-AWQ                     stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
stelterlab/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ                    stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
dark-side-of-the-code/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-AWQ         stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
YuYu1015/Huihui-Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-abliterated-NVFP4  stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
null-space/Qwen3-235B-A22B-abliterated-FP8                     stored router: weight                              config says: BF16 (ignored)
```

### Environment

- 1x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1
- SGLang v0.5.23 (served runs), main `4003bf1` (code links); vLLM 0.33.0 (comparison)

issue.title: [Bug] Gemma 3 and Mistral 3 build ignored vision layers quantized: the quantization ignore list is not renamed like the weights
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Quantized vision-language checkpoints usually keep the vision tower in BF16 and list its layers in the quantization config's `ignore`, under the checkpoint's module names. SGLang renames some vision modules when it loads the weights, but compares `ignore` with its own module names without the same renames. Those layers are then built with the checkpoint's quantization scheme. The load succeeds, text prompts are unaffected, and image answers are wrong.

- **Gemma 3** (`Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration`). `load_weights` loads the SigLIP attention's `out_proj` into VisionAttention's `proj` ([gemma3_mm.py#L505](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/754185aab52995b0df1c514a03b0701d25625969/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma3_mm.py#L505)), but the ignore entry `vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.N.self_attn.out_proj` is compared with `...self_attn.proj` ([utils.py#L26](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/754185aab52995b0df1c514a03b0701d25625969/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py#L26)). For `RedHatAI/gemma-3-27b-it-FP8-dynamic`, all 27 vision `proj` layers are built FP8: the BF16 weight is cast into the FP8 parameter and its `weight_scale` keeps its initial value. q/k/v and `fc1`/`fc2` match and stay BF16.
- **Mistral 3** (`Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`, Pixtral tower). `load_weights` rewrites `model.vision_tower.` to `vision_tower.` ([mistral.py#L177-L178](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/754185aab52995b0df1c514a03b0701d25625969/python/sglang/srt/models/mistral.py#L177-L178)); VisionAttention calls the output projection `proj` where the checkpoint has `o_proj`; and the class has no `packed_modules_mapping`, so `should_ignore_layer` cannot expand the fused `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj` into the `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` and `gate_proj`/`up_proj` names of `ignore` ([utils.py#L42](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/754185aab52995b0df1c514a03b0701d25625969/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/utils.py#L42)). For `RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-NVFP4`, the whole Pixtral tower is built NVFP4. Its BF16 checkpoint weights then have no parameter to load into, and Pixtral's `load_weights` skips them without a message ([pixtral.py#L1034-L1051](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/754185aab52995b0df1c514a03b0701d25625969/python/sglang/srt/models/pixtral.py#L1034-L1051)), so the tower runs on uninitialized parameters.

Effect, on one H20 with SGLang v0.5.23 (main `754185a` has the same code). "Layer check" loads the real tensors of vision layer 0 through SGLang's own load and post-load step and compares the layer's output with the BF16 reference. "Image" asks "Describe this image." about two COCO photographs (two elephants under a shelter; three people around a table with food), greedy, 64 tokens.

| Checkpoint (downloads, last 30 days) | Layer check, vision layer 0 | Image |
|---|---|---|
| `RedHatAI/gemma-3-27b-it-FP8-dynamic` (66,131) | `self_attn.proj` built FP8; 928 outputs are inf | both photos: "The image is a digital illustration or artwork depicting a whimsical, fantastical scene with a strong focus on a large, stylized mushroom." |
| `RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-NVFP4` (74,757) | every vision linear layer built NVFP4; weights not loaded | both photos: "asmussen an in with for [ for [ for [ ..." |

Gemma 3 takes images in v0.5.23 only with `--enable-multimodal`. Mistral 3 runs with default flags. One `RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.2` layer-check run also stopped in the post-load step with `ValueError: NVFP4 weight-only linear requires all fused projections to share one weight_global_scale, got [27264.0, 27265.0, 27266.0]`: the vision tower's global scales are never written, so that check sees whatever the memory held.

The same Gemma 3 rename makes `abhishekchohan/gemma-3-12b-it-quantized-W4A16` (149,947 downloads) fail at load instead: its vision `proj` is built W4A16, which has no `weight` parameter for the BF16 tensor (`KeyError: 'vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.proj.weight'`).

### Reproduction

`repro.py` builds the quantization config as the model loader does (the model class's `packed_modules_mapping`, then its `hf_to_sglang_mapper`) and asks the check that `get_linear_scheme` makes. It reads only `config.json`.

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# Which vision layers SGLang builds quantized although the checkpoint's quantization config lists them in
# `ignore`. Builds the quantization config as the model loader does (the model class's packed_modules_mapping,
# then its hf_to_sglang_mapper) and asks the check that get_linear_scheme makes. Reads config.json only; no GPU.
import json

from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.compressed_tensors import CompressedTensorsConfig
from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.utils import should_ignore_layer
from sglang.srt.models.gemma3_mm import Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration
from sglang.srt.models.mistral import Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration

CASES = [
    ("RedHatAI/gemma-3-27b-it-FP8-dynamic", Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration,
     [f"vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.{n}" for n in ("self_attn.qkv_proj", "self_attn.proj", "mlp.fc1", "mlp.fc2")]),
    ("RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-NVFP4", Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration,
     [f"vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.{n}" for n in ("attention.qkv_proj", "attention.proj",
                                                          "feed_forward.gate_up_proj", "feed_forward.down_proj")]),
]
for repo, cls, layers in CASES:
    q = json.load(open(hf_hub_download(repo, "config.json")))["quantization_config"]
    q["packed_modules_mapping"] = dict(getattr(cls, "packed_modules_mapping", {}))
    cfg = CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config(q)
    mapper = getattr(cls, "hf_to_sglang_mapper", None)
    if mapper is not None:
        cfg.apply_weight_name_mapper(mapper)
    print(repo)
    for name in layers:
        ok = should_ignore_layer(name, ignore=cfg.ignore, fused_mapping=cfg.packed_modules_mapping)
        print(f"  {name:55s} {'ignored (BF16)' if ok else 'QUANTIZED'}")
```

</details>

Output on main `754185a`:

```
RedHatAI/gemma-3-27b-it-FP8-dynamic
  vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj ignored (BF16)
  vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.proj QUANTIZED
  vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.mlp.fc1      ignored (BF16)
  vision_tower.vision_model.encoder.layers.0.mlp.fc2      ignored (BF16)
RedHatAI/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506-NVFP4
  vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.attention.qkv_proj    QUANTIZED
  vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.attention.proj        QUANTIZED
  vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.feed_forward.gate_up_proj QUANTIZED
  vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.feed_forward.down_proj QUANTIZED
```

### Environment

- 1x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0
- SGLang v0.5.23 (served runs), main `754185a` (repro)

issue.title: [Bug]: Compressed-tensors NVFP4/MXFP4 row-parallel layers load with other groups' block scales when the TP split cuts a scale group (Gemma-4-26B-A4B NVFP4 at TP=8: GSM8K 24% -> 1.4%)
issue.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py (trimmed) ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.14.0+cu130 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 12:30:59) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H20-3e ... GPU 7: NVIDIA H20-3e Nvidia driver version : 570.133.20 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.2.post1 [pip3] torch==2.14.0 [pip3] transformers==5.20.2 [pip3] triton==3.8.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.33.0rc1.dev848+g14d147a7a (git sha: 14d147a7a) ``` `compressed-tensors==0.17.0`, `humming-kernels==0.1.18`.
The served numbers below come from that nightly. The layer reproductions ran with the Python sources of main `8176238c9` (2026-11-07) on top of it; the loading code involved (`parameter.py`, the compressed-tensors FP4 schemes and MoE methods, `RoutedExperts._load_w2`) is the same in both. ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary** A row-parallel layer (dense `down_proj` / `o_proj`, the experts' `w2`) gives rank `r` the input columns `[r*K_r, (r+1)*K_r)` with `K_r = K / tp`. NVFP4 and MXFP4 store one block scale per group of 16 / 32 input columns. When `K_r` is not a multiple of the group size `G`, vLLM loads the layer without any error, but slices the packed codes at element offset `r*K_r` and the block scales at group offset `r*(K_r // G)`. Every rank after the first then multiplies its codes by other groups' scales, and rank 0 has no scale for its last `K_r % G` columns. Affected, checked on main: - compressed-tensors NVFP4 W4A4 and W4A16, and MXFP4, `RowParallelLinear` (`CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4`, `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4`), with `HummingNvFp4LinearKernel` / `MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel` and `HummingMxFp4LinearKernel` / `MarlinMxFp4LinearKernel`; - NVFP4 MoE `w2` under compressed-tensors (`CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod`, W4A4 and W4A16) and ModelOpt (`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE`), with the `HUMMING` MoE backend: loading, the post-load step and the forward all run without error. The compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE method slices `w2` the same way; on SM90 its Marlin backend rejected the shapes I tried with an unrelated tile-size error, and I could not test other MXFP4 MoE backends. The ModelOpt MoE case is already reported in #49949 (fix PR #49951, open), where it surfaced as a Marlin error on Nemotron-3-Nano at TP=8; with the Humming MoE backend on main it loads and runs silently. This report adds the dense row-parallel layers and the compressed-tensors MoE. ModelOpt NVFP4 linear layers already refuse these shapes (`modelopt.py:2139-2142`), and compressed-tensors WNA16 refuses them through `verify_group_size_divides_partition` (#46236). **Impact on a real checkpoint** `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4` (compressed-tensors NVFP4 W4A4, revision `5557756b`) has dense `mlp.down_proj` K = 2112 and expert `down_proj` K = 704. At TP=8 that is 264 and 88 columns per rank (16.5 and 5.5 groups); at TP=4 and TP=2 the groups are whole. With the SM90 defaults (Humming linear and MoE), TP=8 loads without a warning. Comparing the loaded scales of all 30 layers and 8 ranks with the checkpoint: 49,920 of 63,360 rank-local dense `down_proj` columns hold another group's scale and 1,920 hold none, so 68.7% of the elements with nonzero codes are read with a wrong scale; for the experts' `w2`, 1,996,800 of 2,703,360 columns hold another group's scale and 245,760 none (70.0%). At TP=4 every column is right. GSM8K, all 1,319 test questions, 5-shot, greedy (temperature 0, `max_tokens` 256), raw few-shot text on the completions endpoint without the chat template (which is why the absolute scores are low for this instruct model): | `--tensor-parallel-size` | GSM8K | |---|---| | 8 | **1.44%** (19 / 1319) | | 4 | 24.34%, 25.32% (two runs) | | 2 | 22.82% | | 8, with group-aligned shards (see "Suggested fix") | 24.79% | TP=4 vs TP=8: 315 questions are right only at TP=4 and 13 only at TP=8 (exact McNemar p = 2.4e-76), while the two TP=4 runs differ by 161 vs 174 (p = 0.51). Server: `vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4 --revision 5557756b8dce33ac72f2bd702b11729fdba3b839 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 --seed 0 --kv-cache-dtype auto --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "audio": 0, "video": 0}'` (CUDA graphs on, default kernels). `unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4` has the same shapes, and `tcclaviger/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MXFP4-FP8-GPTQ` has MXFP4 expert and shared-expert `down_proj` K = 640 (2.5 groups per rank at TP=8). **Reproduction** One `RowParallelLinear` at TP=2; nothing is downloaded. K is 45 groups, so each rank gets 22.5 groups. Every FP4 code is +1.0 and the block scale of group `g` is `2 ** (g % 8)`; with identity inputs, output row `k` is column `k` of the weight as the kernel reads it. ```python # Run: torchrun --nproc-per-node 2 repro_row_parallel_fp4_tp.py [nvfp4|nvfp4a16|mxfp4] [groups] import os import sys import torch from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config from vllm.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import RowParallelLinear from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.compressed_tensors import ( # noqa: E501 CompressedTensorsConfig, ) fmt = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "nvfp4" G = 32 if fmt == "mxfp4" else 16 K, N = int(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 45) * G, 16 # 45: 22.5 per rank at TP=2 weights = {"num_bits": 4, "type": "float", "symmetric": True, "dynamic": False, "strategy": "group" if fmt == "mxfp4" else "tensor_group", "group_size": G} scheme = {"targets": ["Linear"], "weights": weights} if fmt == "nvfp4": # W4A4, as RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4 scheme["input_activations"] = dict(weights, dynamic="local") quant_config = CompressedTensorsConfig.from_config({ "quant_method": "compressed-tensors", "format": "mxfp4-pack-quantized" if fmt == "mxfp4" else "nvfp4-pack-quantized", "config_groups": {"group_0": scheme}, }) rank, world = int(os.environ["RANK"]), int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"]) torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])) with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()): init_distributed_environment(world, rank, "env://", int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])) initialize_model_parallel(world) with torch.device("cuda"): layer = RowParallelLinear(K, N, bias=False, input_is_parallel=False, quant_config=quant_config, params_dtype=torch.bfloat16, prefix="model.layers.0.mlp.down_proj") # Checkpoint: every FP4 code is +1.0 (0x2), global scales 1, and the block # scale of input group g is 2 ** (g % 8), so column k must read 2 ** (k // G % 8). scale = (2.0 ** (torch.arange(K // G) % 8)).expand(N, -1).contiguous() ckpt = {"weight_packed": torch.full((N, K // 2), 0x22, dtype=torch.uint8)} if fmt == "mxfp4": ckpt["weight_scale"] = (scale.log2() + 127).to(torch.uint8) else: ckpt["weight_scale"] = scale.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) ckpt["weight_global_scale"] = torch.ones(1) if fmt == "nvfp4": ckpt["input_global_scale"] = torch.ones(1) for name, tensor in ckpt.items(): param = getattr(layer, name) param.weight_loader(param, tensor.cuda()) layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer) # Input row k is 6 * e_k (exact in FP4), so output row k is column k of the # weight as the kernel reads it. x = 6 * torch.eye(K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") with torch.inference_mode(): read = layer(x)[0][:, 0].float().cpu() / 6 expected = 2.0 ** (torch.arange(K) // G % 8).float() if rank == 0: print("kernel:", type(layer.scheme.kernel).__name__) k_r = K // world for r in range(world): cols = range(r * k_r, (r + 1) * k_r) wrong = [k for k in cols if read[k] != expected[k]] print(f"rank {r}: {len(wrong)} of {k_r} input columns read the wrong scale") for k in wrong[:3]: print(f" column {k} (group {k // G}): read {read[k].item():g}, " f"expected {expected[k].item():g}") ``` `torchrun --nproc-per-node 2 repro_row_parallel_fp4_tp.py nvfp4` on main: ```text kernel: HummingNvFp4LinearKernel rank 0: 8 of 360 input columns read the wrong scale column 352 (group 22): read 0, expected 64 column 353 (group 22): read 0, expected 64 column 354 (group 22): read 0, expected 64 rank 1: 184 of 360 input columns read the wrong scale column 368 (group 23): read 64, expected 128 column 369 (group 23): read 64, expected 128 column 370 (group 23): read 64, expected 128 ``` Every format and kernel (`VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=HummingNvFp4LinearKernel,HummingMxFp4LinearKernel` selects Marlin): | format | kernel | wrong columns, rank 0 | wrong columns, rank 1 | |---|---|---|---| | NVFP4 W4A4 (`nvfp4`) | Humming / Marlin | 8 of 360 / 8 of 360 | 184 of 360 / 184 of 360 | | NVFP4 W4A16 (`nvfp4a16`) | Humming / Marlin | 8 of 360 / 8 of 360 | 184 of 360 / 184 of 360 | | MXFP4 (`mxfp4`) | Humming / Marlin | 16 of 720 / 16 of 720 | 368 of 720 / 368 of 720 | With 46 groups (23 per rank) every column is right. A `FusedMoE` layer with intermediate size 720 at TP=2, loaded through `load_weights`, gives the same counts for the `w2` scales under compressed-tensors NVFP4 W4A4 and W4A16 and under ModelOpt NVFP4 (`HUMMING` backend). **Expected**: correct results, or an error at load time as for ModelOpt NVFP4 linear layers and compressed-tensors WNA16. **Root cause** (line numbers at main `8176238c9`) - `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.create_weights` (`compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py:56,76`) and `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4.create_weights` (`compressed_tensors_w4a4_mxfp4.py:68,81`) allocate `input_size_per_partition // 2` code bytes and `input_size_per_partition // group_size` scales without checking that the division is exact. - `RowvLLMParameter.load_row_parallel_weight` (`parameter.py:211-221`, used by `ModelWeightParameter` and `GroupQuantScaleParameter`) narrows each tensor at `tp_rank * shard_size` in its own units: element `r*K_r` for the codes, group `r*(K_r // G)` for the scales. A rank whose slice starts inside a group would need two scales for each of its local groups, which a per-rank scale tensor cannot hold, so exact per-rank narrowing is impossible here. - MoE: `CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` (`compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_nvfp4.py:127,157`), `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` (`compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_mxfp4.py:123,152`) and `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.create_weights` (`modelopt.py:1011`) allocate `w2` the same way, and `RoutedExperts._load_w2` (`routed_experts.py:635-636`) slices codes and scales at `loaded_weight.shape[shard_dim] // tp_size * tp_rank`. **Suggested fix** Refuse at load time: call `verify_group_size_divides_partition` in the compressed-tensors NVFP4/MXFP4 linear schemes when their input dimension is sharded, and in the compressed-tensors NVFP4/MXFP4 MoE methods for `w2` (ModelOpt MoE is handled by #49951). Users then get a clear error and can use TP=4, or expert parallelism for the MoE layers. Serving TP=8 exactly needs group-aligned shards: for the MoE, padded per-rank partitions as in #49951; for the dense layers, a zero-padded, group-aligned rank buffer that holds the cut group's scale on both ranks, with the input padded to match. I tested such a change (the last row of the table above), but it is much larger, so I would start with the refusal. I have a patch with a regression test and can open a PR. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [ ] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comment.body:
Follow-up: GSM8K through the chat template. The raw few-shot completions in the report leave this instruct checkpoint near 24% even when it is read correctly, so here are the same configurations with `--use-chat-completions --temperature 0` (same build 14d147a, checkpoint revision 5557756b, BF16 KV cache, text only, all 1,319 questions, 5-shot):

| config | GSM8K |
|---|---|
| TP=8, as is | 0.30% (17% of answers contain no number) |
| TP=4, four identical runs | 91.51 / 92.80 / 92.19 / 92.42% |
| TP=2 | 91.89% |
| TP=8 with group-aligned shards | 92.34% |

Next-token top-1 agreement with a TP=4 run on 64 WikiText-2 prefixes: 9.9% at TP=8, against 81.0-81.5% between TP=4 runs and 80.7% for TP=8 with group-aligned shards.

A rank whose slice starts inside a group would need two scales for each of its local groups, which a per-rank scale tensor cannot hold, so exact per-rank narrowing is impossible here. - MoE: `CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` (`compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_nvfp4.py:127,157`), `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod.create_weights` (`compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_mxfp4.py:123,152`) and `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.create_weights` (`modelopt.py:1011`) allocate `w2` the same way, and `RoutedExperts._load_w2` (`routed_experts.py:635-636`) slices codes and scales at `loaded_weight.shape[shard_dim] // tp_size * tp_rank`. **Suggested fix** Refuse at load time: call `verify_group_size_divides_partition` in the compressed-tensors NVFP4/MXFP4 linear schemes when their input dimension is sharded, and in the compressed-tensors NVFP4/MXFP4 MoE methods for `w2` (ModelOpt MoE is handled by #49951). Users then get a clear error and can use TP=4, or expert parallelism for the MoE layers. Serving TP=8 exactly needs group-aligned shards: for the MoE, padded per-rank partitions as in #49951; for the dense layers, a zero-padded, group-aligned rank buffer that holds the cut group's scale on both ranks, with the input padded to match. I tested such a change (the last row of the table above), but it is much larger, so I would start with the refusal. I have a patch with a regression test and can open a PR. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [ ] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issue.title: [Bugfix][Quantization] NVFP4 linear: apply each fused shard's own global scale
issue.body:
## Purpose

The NVFP4 linear kernels take one global weight scale per layer. For a fused layer (`q/k/v`, `gate/up`) whose shards store different ones, the ModelOpt scheme (`KNvfp4Static`, shared by W4A4 and W4A16) kept the largest and the compressed-tensors scheme kept the smallest, and both only warned. Every other shard was then dequantized with the wrong scale.

ModelOpt quantizes each projection with its own per-tensor amax, so fused shards often differ. Example: `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (ModelOpt 0.46.0 W4A16). Its shared-expert and dense-MLP gate/up global scales differ in nearly every MoE layer, with up/gate ratios from 0.46 to 2.51 across a layer sample. Greedy output stays coherent, which hides it. Sampled output at the checkpoint's defaults (temperature 1, top_p 0.95) degenerates within a few hundred tokens.

## Changes

- `nvfp4_utils.fused_global_scale_ratio()` returns the scale the GEMM runs with (the largest dequantization multiplier, in either convention: compressed-tensors stores a divisor) and a per-output-column ratio, own scale over the kept one (<= 1). `None` when all shards share one scale.
- `apply_fused_global_scale_ratio()` multiplies the GEMM output by that ratio in place, before the bias. The product is computed in fp32 and rounded once.
- `KNvfp4Static.process` and `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.process_weights_after_loading` keep that scale and store the ratio. `ModelOptLinearMethod.apply` and `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.apply_weights` apply it. Shared-scale layers get no ratio and take the same path as before.
- If the scale count does not match the shard widths, the largest scale is kept and the warning stays.
- Readers of `weight_global_scale` outside the quant method's forward: Flint's fused qkv and gate/up GEMVs raise at load on unequal merged scales, and the DSpark gathered `markov_w2` is a single shard, so neither sees a ratio. The helper's docstring states the rule for new direct readers.

An earlier revision of this PR rescaled each smaller shard's e4m3 block scales at load instead. That re-rounds the block scales to 3 mantissa bits and can push small ones into the e4m3 subnormal range, which Marlin decodes as zero. The output rescale is exact up to output rounding. Thanks to @HollowMan6, who proposed it, wrote the core of this change and shared a per-element readout across kernels (in the thread below).

## Related work

- #47515 fixes the compressed-tensors two-partition case with the same output rescale. This PR covers ModelOpt and compressed-tensors with one helper, for any number of shards.
- #55073 / #54974 are the NVFP4 MoE w13 counterpart.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

Plus a GPU probe on the real Marlin W4A16 kernel (RTX 5090, sm_120): two fused shards quantized ModelOpt-style (global = amax / (6 * 448), log-normal block magnitudes), 64 tokens, K = N_shard = 4096, compared against exact per-shard dequantization in fp32. The floor is each shard run alone through Marlin with its own scale.

## Test Result

- `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py` on CPU: 118 passed, 7 skipped, 2 failed. The 2 failures (`test_modelopt_nested_mixed_checkpoint`, `test_modelopt_mixed_dspark_checkpoint`) are engine-start tests that fail identically on `main` without this change.
- New tests cover the ratio in both conventions, no ratio for a shared scale, `KNvfp4Static` keeping the largest scale plus the ratio, the forward of both `ModelOptLinearMethod.apply` and `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.apply_weights` against per-shard dequantization (bias added after the rescale, for 2 and 3 shards), the in-place single rounding, and the warning on mismatched widths. With the rescale removed, the 4 forward and equivalence tests fail; without the warning, the warning test fails.
- Marlin probe, relative output error of the smaller shard (the larger shard is identical in every row):

| activations | scale ratio | main | load-time block rescale | this PR | floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 0.53 | 0.887 | 0.0351 | 0.00231 | 0.00166 |
| bf16 | 0.109 | 8.20 | 0.0292 | 0.00234 | 0.00165 |
| fp16 | 0.50 | 0.996 | 0.00183 | 0.00028 | 0.00021 |
| fp16 | 0.108 | 8.29 | 0.0315 | 0.00029 | 0.00021 |

- Forward-time cost of the rescale on that layer (Marlin W4A16 gate/up, K = 4096, N = 2 x 11008, CUDA graphs): +9.8% at M=1, +19.3% at M=16, +9.0% at M=256, +13.7% at M=2048. It applies only to layers whose shards have different scales.
- End to end on the earlier load-time revision: 2x DGX Spark (GB10, TP2, Marlin W4A16), `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`, temperature 1 / top_p 0.95. Mean log-probability of sampled tokens in the last quarter went from -6.17 to -7.50 (word salad, 3 runs) to -0.28 to -0.53 (coherent, 4 runs). Not rerun on this revision.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and the probe. I reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

What it does:
- `nvfp4_utils.fused_global_scale_ratio()` returns the global scale to keep (the largest dequantization multiplier; compressed-tensors stores its reciprocal, so both conventions are handled) and a per-output-column ratio, own scale over the kept one (≤ 1), or `None` when all shards share one scale. `apply_fused_global_scale_ratio()` multiplies the GEMM output by it in fp32, before the bias.

issue.title: [Bug] modelopt NVFP4 MoE: mismatched w1/w3 global scales are detected, warned about, and then used anyway
issue.body:
### The behaviour

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE.process_weights_after_loading` fuses `gate_proj` and `up_proj` into `w13` and keeps only the **gate** per-tensor global scale:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py#L967-L975

```python
# Use a single gscale for w13.
if self.moe.is_act_and_mul and not torch.allclose(
    layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0], layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 1]
):
    logger.warning_once(
        "w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected."
    )
w13_weight_scale_2 = layer.w13_weight_scale_2[:, 0].contiguous()
```

When the two differ, the up-projection half of `w13` is then dequantised with the gate half's global scale. The mismatch is detected, logged once, and the wrong scale is used anyway.

### How far apart they can be

Measured directly from the checkpoints on disk (reading only the `weight_scale_2` scalars — no GPU, no inference):

| checkpoint | modelopt | gate/up pairs | pairs that differ | ratio median / p99 / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-ABLITERATED-NVFP4` | 0.45.0 | 12,384 | **8,563 (69.1%)** | 1.077 / 1.69 / **10.0** |
| `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` | 0.46.0 | 24,576 | 0 (0.0%) | — |
| `mazinb/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-NVFP4` | 0.46.0-compatible-rtn | 24,576 | 0 (0.0%) | — |

All 43 MoE layers of the GLM checkpoint are affected; the worst layer has 272 of 288 experts mismatched. So this is not universal — the two modelopt 0.46 checkpoints tie the two scales exactly — but when a checkpoint does not tie them, the divergence is large and the whole model is affected.

Script used, if it is useful for triage:

```python
from safetensors import safe_open
# for each "...experts.N.gate_proj.weight_scale_2", compare with the
# matching "...up_proj.weight_scale_2" in the same checkpoint
```

### Why I am filing this rather than sending a patch

The detection is already there — the question is what to do on detection, and that is a design call I would rather not make unilaterally:

1. **Refuse to load** when the ratio exceeds some threshold, rather than warn and produce a quietly mis-scaled model. `warning_once` is easy to miss in a long startup log, and there is no runtime signal afterwards.
2. **Rescale** the `w3` half's per-block scales into the common global scale at load. The block scales are e4m3 with limited range, so this trades one error for another and needs care — I do not know whether it is a net win.
3. **Leave as-is** and treat it as a checkpoint-producer bug, but make the warning louder / include the measured ratio so a user can tell a 1.01x from a 10x.

Happy to implement whichever direction a maintainer prefers.

### Environment

Reproduced on a checkpoint on disk; no GPU needed for the measurement above. The model that surfaced it is GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 served on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120).

comment.body:
A measurement of how much this costs on a public checkpoint, in case it helps prioritize #55073.

`tattrongvu/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` stores different w1 and w3 global scales in 8,532 of its 12,384 expert groups (up to 10x apart). I served it with vLLM 0.33.0 on 8x H20-3e (TP 8) four ways: on the Humming MoE backend, which applies both scales; a second Humming run, for the run-to-run floor; Humming with each expert's w3 global scale replaced by its w1 scale before the weights are converted (the collapse this issue describes, on the same kernel, nothing else changed); and on Marlin, which collapses the scales itself.

| | WikiText-2 ppl (16,376 positions) | top-1 agreement with run 1 | GSM8K, 5-shot, 1,319 q. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Humming | 2.37 | — | 92.1% |
| Humming, second run | 2.38 | 96.4% | 91.4% |
| Humming, w1 scale used for w3 | 2.47 | 91.8% | 88.0% |
| Marlin | 2.45 | 91.6% | 88.4% |

So the collapse alone costs about 4 GSM8K points, several times the run-to-run difference, and the Marlin path (and the SM100/SM120 paths that get the same collapsed scale) would see the same.
