issue.title: [Bugfix] Load FP8 KV-cache scales for Kimi-Linear's MLA and MiniMax-M3's sparse attention
issue.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #65946.
Fixes #66120.

With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` and a compressed-tensors or ModelOpt checkpoint that stores static `k_scale`/`v_scale`, two attention layers that are not `Attention` never load those scales and run with 1.0.

**Kimi-Linear (#65946).** Two things cause this, and both have to be fixed:

1. Kimi's `MultiHeadLatentAttention` is neither `Attention` nor `MLAAttention`, so the compressed-tensors and ModelOpt configs give it no KV-cache method. This PR makes those checks match the common base class `AttentionLayerBase`.
2. The generic cache-scale mapper renames the scales to `self_attn.attn.*`, but Kimi's scales live at `self_attn.*`. `KimiLinearModel.load_weights` now maps `.self_attn.attn.` back to `.self_attn.` when that parameter exists.

**MiniMax-M3 sparse attention (#66120).** It needs the same `AttentionLayerBase` check, so it is in this PR. `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention` only registered default scale buffers, so `juspay/MiniMax-M3-FP8`'s sparse-layer scales were dropped with a warning. It now initializes KV-cache quantization the way `Attention` does, and its loader maps the scales onto the layer. Loading them alone would make the read side wrong. `fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert`, which writes the sparse layers' cache, quantized an FP8 cache with scale 1.0, while sparse attention dequantizes with the layer's scales. The insert now applies `kv_k_scale`/`kv_v_scale` to an FP8 cache too, as it already did for NVFP4 and as `reshape_and_cache_flash` does, and keeps 1.0 when none are passed. Other callers of the op pass no scales and are unchanged.

**Side effect for reviewers:** with the broader class check, compressed-tensors also gives DeepSeek-style MLA layers a KV-cache method. With real checkpoints this alone does not change what is loaded (details in the comment below; #65948 completes that path). With dummy weights, their scales are now random instead of 1.0. `Fp8Config` is deliberately left unchanged.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kv_cache_scales.py
pytest tests/models/minimax_m3/test_kv_cache_scales.py
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_norm_rope_nvfp4_insert.py
pytest tests/quantization -k "kv_cache or modelopt or compressed_tensors"
```

The kernel change was built from source (`_C_stable_libtorch`, SM90) and tested on H20.

## Test Result

- **Kimi-Linear test:** 4 of its cases fail before the change; all pass after.
- **MiniMax-M3 loader test:** both cases (compressed-tensors, ModelOpt) fail before the change and pass after.
- **Insert kernel:** the new `test_sparse_fp8_insert_applies_kv_scales` compares the FP8 cache with `reshape_and_cache_flash` using the same scales, for the row-group kernel (rotary dim 64) and the fallback (32). Its 6 cases fail on the unmodified kernel (up to 525,294 elements differ by more than one FP8 step) and pass after. The other 69 cases of the file pass before and after; the SM100-only cases are skipped on H20.
- **End to end:** shrunk `juspay/MiniMax-M3-FP8` config with dummy weights and the checkpoint's layer-3 scales (0.0234 / 0.0054) on the sparse layer. Mean |Δ prompt log-prob| against a BF16 cache: 0.0011 with this change, 0.0167 with only the loader change (cache written with 1.0, read with the scales).
- **Nearby test suites:** the results are the same before and after.
  - Two ModelOpt tests fail in both runs with a forked-process CUDA initialization error, and pass when run alone, before and after.
- **pre-commit:** passes on the changed files (ruff, clang-format, mypy, typos, test tethering).
- **Repro:** Kimi-Linear now applies 0.25 / 0.5 from the checkpoint in both formats, instead of 1.0 / 1.0.

**Why this is not a duplicate.** No open PR references #65946 or #66120. `gh pr list --state open --search` for "kimi linear kv cache", "kimi_k3 kv scale", "_init_kv_cache_quant", "minimax m3 kv scale" and "fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert" finds no PR that gives these layers a KV-cache method or scales the sparse FP8 insert; #61245 changes Kimi-Linear's Mamba state dtype, a different setting.

Parts of this change were drafted with AI assistance and reviewed and tested by the author.

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

comment.body:
A note on the side effect mentioned in the description: compressed-tensors DeepSeek-style MLA checkpoints.

I loaded three compressed-tensors MLA configs with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` and a distinct `k_scale`/`v_scale` per layer in the checkpoint, and checked which value each MLA layer ends up with (nightly `14d147a`, 4 layers each):

| Config | main | main + this PR | main + this PR + #65948 |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V3 | no scale parameter, 1.0 used | parameter exists, still 1.0 | checkpoint scale, 8/8 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat | no scale parameter, 1.0 used | parameter exists, still 1.0 | checkpoint scale, 8/8 |
| Kimi-K2.6 (`intel-ai/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4-FP8KV-CT-AutoRound` names) | no scale parameter, 1.0 used | parameter exists, still 1.0 | checkpoint scale, 8/8 |

With this PR alone, the MLA layers now get a KV-cache method, but the generic cache-scale mapper still renames `self_attn.k_scale` to `self_attn.attn.k_scale`, so the loader logs `not found the expected name in the model (e.g. layers.0.self_attn.attn.attn.k_scale)` and keeps 1.0, the same value as on main. #65948 fixes that renaming. So this PR does not change what compressed-tensors MLA models compute on its own, and together with #65948 these checkpoints load their KV-cache scales.

issue.title: [Bugfix] Reconcile mismatched NVFP4 MoE w13 global scales
issue.body:
## Summary

NVFP4 fused MoE checkpoints may contain different per-expert global
scales for the gate and up projections.

The previous loading path detected this mismatch but retained only the
gate scale for fused w13, causing the up half to use the wrong effective
dequantization scale.

## Fix

- Reconcile gate/up `scale_2` per expert using their shared maximum.
- Rescale each half's E4M3 block scales to preserve its original
  effective dequantization scale.
- Leave the FP4 payload unchanged.
- Keep matching-scale checkpoints on a no-op path.
- Reuse the logic across ModelOpt, Quark, and compressed-tensors.
- Skip HUMMING because its converter already folds each half's
  `scale_2` into its block scales.

This follows the same max-scale policy used by vLLM's fused FP8 paths.

## Tests

Coverage includes:

- Matching-scale no-op.
- gate < up.
- gate > up.
- Multiple experts with independent reconciliation.
- Effective dequantization-scale invariant within E4M3 rounding.
- Regression coverage for the previous gate-only behavior.

Validation:

- Targeted reconciliation tests: 4 passed.
- Quark NVFP4 tests: 2 passed.
- Runnable compressed-tensors NVFP4 targets: 2 passed.
- Changed-files pre-commit hooks, including Ruff and mypy: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Full `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py`:

- 38 passed.
- 2 skipped.
- 1 unrelated existing FP8/Marlin failure:
  `QKVParallelLinear` has no `orig_dtype` attribute in
  `test_modelopt_fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup`.

Model evaluation:

- NOT RUN locally.
- The available RTX 4060 Laptop is SM89 and cannot execute the affected
  Blackwell NVFP4 MoE path; the affected checkpoint also exceeds the
  available 8 GiB VRAM.
- Numerical unit coverage validates preservation of the effective
  dequantization scale. End-to-end Blackwell evaluation remains
  hardware-blocked locally.

## Duplicate work

GitHub open-PR searches for #54974 and the relevant NVFP4 MoE w1/w3
scale-reconciliation terms found no PR addressing this issue.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex was used to inspect the implementation, prepare the patch,
and run the checks above. I reviewed the changes and am responsible for
the submitted code and validation.

## Issue

Fixes #54974

comment.body:
For the Marlin MoE path there is an exact alternative to re-rounding: give the kernel the gate's global scale and multiply the up half of the GEMM1 output by up / gate per expert before the activation. A global scale is a per-expert factor on that projection's output, so nothing is requantized. We did this in SGLang (sgl-project/sglang#48931) and checked it with an exact readout on its real `FusedMoE`: before, the up projection read the gate's scale; after, each expert's own.

The fused SM100/SM120 kernels (TRT-LLM, FlashInfer CUTLASS) do not expose the GEMM1 output, so re-rounding remains the option there. On Marlin, re-rounding also risks the e4m3 subnormal case: scaling block scales down can move small ones into the subnormal range, which Marlin decodes as zero in some cases.

issue.title: [Fix] qwen3: load FP8 KV-cache scales in the Qwen3-family wrapper loaders
issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #48904.

This PR is stacked on #48750 and #46527. Its first commit is #48750 (it passes `quant_config` to `Qwen3MoeAttention` and the attention of other models) and its second is #46527 (the same for `Qwen3Attention`). Only the last commit, `[Fix] qwen3: load FP8 KV-cache scales in the Qwen3-family wrapper loaders`, is new. Please merge #48750 and #46527 first; I will rebase this PR after that.

With those two, the attention of the Qwen3 family has `k_scale`/`v_scale`, but several wrapper loaders still drop the checkpoint's scale names, so the FP8 KV cache runs with a scale of 1.0:

- no rule for KV-scale names in [qwen3_classification.py#L77](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_classification.py#L77) (`Qwen3ForSequenceClassification`, `Qwen3ForRewardModel`), [qwen3_vl.py#L1702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1702) (Qwen3-VL, and Cosmos3 through it) and [qwen3_asr.py#L126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_asr.py#L126): the compressed-tensors name `<attn>.k_scale` is skipped as unknown, and the ModelOpt name `<attn>.k_proj.k_scale` is renamed to `qkv_proj.k_scale` and then skipped;
- Qwen3-VL-MoE and Qwen3-Omni-MoE also list `.k_scale`/`.v_scale` among the suffixes they skip ([qwen3_vl_moe.py#L235](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl_moe.py#L235), [qwen3_omni_moe.py#L580](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_omni_moe.py#L580)).

## Modifications

- Call `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` before the stacked-parameter mapping, as `llama.py` and the `Qwen3ForCausalLM` loader do, in `qwen3_classification.py`, `qwen3_vl.py`, `qwen3_vl_moe.py`, `qwen3_omni_moe.py` and `qwen3_asr.py`. Scale names that have no parameter are still skipped.
- Not changed: `Qwen3ForCausalLM`, `Qwen3Model` and LightOnOCR (which passes its language-model weights to `Qwen3ForCausalLM`) already have the rule. The Qwen3-MoE causal loader's rule is in #39943.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, dummy weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. "Main" is `91fd6756`; "base" is #48750 (head `9a927b7e`) with #46527.

- New test `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_kv_cache_scale_loading.py` builds each attention with a compressed-tensors config that declares a static FP8 KV cache and loads compressed-tensors and ModelOpt scale names through the real loaders of 10 classes (22 cases). On main all 22 cases fail; on base 14 fail (the 7 loaders above, both namings); with this PR all pass.
- The repro in #ISSUE (configs of `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, `tomaarsen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-seq-cls`, `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct`; scales 0.25 / 0.0625 for layer 0):

| model class | main | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3ForCausalLM` | no KV-cache method | 0.25 / 0.0625 | 0.25 / 0.0625 |
| `Qwen3ForSequenceClassification` | no KV-cache method | 1.0 / 1.0 | 0.25 / 0.0625 |
| `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration` | no KV-cache method | 1.0 / 1.0 | 0.25 / 0.0625 |
| `Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration` | no KV-cache method | 1.0 / 1.0 | 0.25 / 0.0625 |

  The same for compressed-tensors and ModelOpt FP8 names.
- A loader check that builds each model from its config with every layer's scale under a distinct value (compressed-tensors, ModelOpt FP8 and ModelOpt NVFP4 configs): on base `Qwen3ForCausalLM`, `Qwen3Model` and LightOnOCR get every layer's own scale, and Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3-ASR, Cosmos3 and the Qwen3 classification and reward models get none; with this PR all of them get every layer's own scale.
- These related unit tests pass on base and with this PR: `test_attention_kv_cache_scale_loading`, `test_cosmos3`, `test_cosmos3_edge`, `test_qwen3_embedding_registration`, `test_qwen3_vl_feature_materialization`, `test_qwen3_vl_image_generation_reject`. `test_qwen3_qk_norm_rope` imports `pytest`, which my environment does not have, so it did not run on either.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel changes. The loaders call the same name helper that `llama.py` uses, once per weight name that contains `scale`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Parts of this change were drafted with AI assistance and reviewed and tested by the author.

comment.body: Confirmed: SGLang v0.5.20's `http_server.py` has no `/begin_weight_update` or `/end_weight_update` route; only SGLang main does. Fixed in e91b59b6 by detecting support rather than raising the pin: if `begin_weight_update` returns 404, the adapter logs once, remembers that the server has no sessions, and sends the buckets without one as before, without probing again on later syncs. Any other error (e.g. a 400 for a duplicate session) still raises. Tests cover a server with sessions (begin, buckets, end), one without (buckets only, probed once) and a 400 rejection.

issue.title: [Bugfix][Quantization] NVFP4 linear: apply each fused shard's own global scale
issue.body:
## Purpose

The NVFP4 linear kernels take one global weight scale per layer. For a fused layer (`q/k/v`, `gate/up`) whose shards store different ones, the ModelOpt scheme (`KNvfp4Static`, shared by W4A4 and W4A16) kept the largest and the compressed-tensors scheme kept the smallest, and both only warned. Every other shard was then dequantized with the wrong scale.

ModelOpt quantizes each projection with its own per-tensor amax, so fused shards often differ. Example: `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` (ModelOpt 0.46.0 W4A16). Its shared-expert and dense-MLP gate/up global scales differ in nearly every MoE layer, with up/gate ratios from 0.46 to 2.51 across a layer sample. Greedy output stays coherent, which hides it. Sampled output at the checkpoint's defaults (temperature 1, top_p 0.95) degenerates within a few hundred tokens.

## Changes

- `nvfp4_utils.fused_global_scale_ratio()` returns the scale the GEMM runs with (the largest dequantization multiplier, in either convention: compressed-tensors stores a divisor) and a per-output-column ratio, own scale over the kept one (<= 1). `None` when all shards share one scale.
- `apply_fused_global_scale_ratio()` multiplies the GEMM output by that ratio in place, before the bias. The product is computed in fp32 and rounded once.
- `KNvfp4Static.process` and `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.process_weights_after_loading` keep that scale and store the ratio. `ModelOptLinearMethod.apply` and `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.apply_weights` apply it. Shared-scale layers get no ratio and take the same path as before.
- If the scale count does not match the shard widths, the largest scale is kept and the warning stays.
- Readers of `weight_global_scale` outside the quant method's forward: Flint's fused qkv and gate/up GEMVs raise at load on unequal merged scales, and the DSpark gathered `markov_w2` is a single shard, so neither sees a ratio. The helper's docstring states the rule for new direct readers.

An earlier revision of this PR rescaled each smaller shard's e4m3 block scales at load instead. That re-rounds the block scales to 3 mantissa bits and can push small ones into the e4m3 subnormal range, which Marlin decodes as zero. The output rescale is exact up to output rounding. Thanks to @HollowMan6, who proposed it, wrote the core of this change and shared a per-element readout across kernels (in the thread below).

## Related work

- #47515 fixes the compressed-tensors two-partition case with the same output rescale. This PR covers ModelOpt and compressed-tensors with one helper, for any number of shards.
- #55073 / #54974 are the NVFP4 MoE w13 counterpart.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

Plus a GPU probe on the real Marlin W4A16 kernel (RTX 5090, sm_120): two fused shards quantized ModelOpt-style (global = amax / (6 * 448), log-normal block magnitudes), 64 tokens, K = N_shard = 4096, compared against exact per-shard dequantization in fp32. The floor is each shard run alone through Marlin with its own scale.

## Test Result

- `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py` on CPU: 118 passed, 7 skipped, 2 failed. The 2 failures (`test_modelopt_nested_mixed_checkpoint`, `test_modelopt_mixed_dspark_checkpoint`) are engine-start tests that fail identically on `main` without this change.
- New tests cover the ratio in both conventions, no ratio for a shared scale, `KNvfp4Static` keeping the largest scale plus the ratio, the forward of both `ModelOptLinearMethod.apply` and `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.apply_weights` against per-shard dequantization (bias added after the rescale, for 2 and 3 shards), the in-place single rounding, and the warning on mismatched widths. With the rescale removed, the 4 forward and equivalence tests fail; without the warning, the warning test fails.
- Marlin probe, relative output error of the smaller shard (the larger shard is identical in every row):

| activations | scale ratio | main | load-time block rescale | this PR | floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 0.53 | 0.887 | 0.0351 | 0.00231 | 0.00166 |
| bf16 | 0.109 | 8.20 | 0.0292 | 0.00234 | 0.00165 |
| fp16 | 0.50 | 0.996 | 0.00183 | 0.00028 | 0.00021 |
| fp16 | 0.108 | 8.29 | 0.0315 | 0.00029 | 0.00021 |

- Forward-time cost of the rescale on that layer (Marlin W4A16 gate/up, K = 4096, N = 2 x 11008, CUDA graphs): +9.8% at M=1, +19.3% at M=16, +9.0% at M=256, +13.7% at M=2048. It applies only to layers whose shards have different scales.
- End to end on the earlier load-time revision: 2x DGX Spark (GB10, TP2, Marlin W4A16), `tiyuvta/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`, temperature 1 / top_p 0.95. Mean log-probability of sampled tokens in the last quarter went from -6.17 to -7.50 (word salad, 3 runs) to -0.28 to -0.53 (coherent, 4 runs). Not rerun on this revision.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and the probe. I reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

comment.body:
We checked this path with an exact per-element readout on a two-shard ModelOpt NVFP4 layer (identity inputs; each shard's global scale and each block scale set to digits of its own index, so every output names the scale it used), for both ModelOpt formats and the kernels vLLM accepts on an H20 (Humming, Marlin, emulation). On main, every element of the shard with the smaller `weight_scale_2` reads the larger one.

Rescaling each shard's output columns by its own scale over the kept one, as #47515 does for compressed-tensors, removes this for every kernel and any number of shards, with no e4m3 re-rounding. In our test the change is one helper used by `KNvfp4Static.process` and `ModelOptLinearMethod.apply` (about 40 lines), and the readout then matches each shard's own scale on all of these kernels.

One more reason to prefer it over re-rounding: scaling a shard's block scales down can move small ones into the e4m3 subnormal range, which Marlin decodes as zero in some cases (with bf16 activations when the tensor's largest block scale exceeds 224, and always with fp16).

Happy to share the patch and the readout if that helps.

issue.title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Avoid Humming's fused-E8M0 path for MXFP4 layers it would round
issue.body:
## Overview

Fixes #66074.

With FP8 activations (the default for compressed-tensors MXFP4 checkpoints on Hopper), Humming runs MXFP4 linear layers on its fused-E8M0 path. That path keeps only 11 binades of E8M0 scales below the largest scale of the layer's fused weight tensor and silently rounds or zeroes the weights of blocks further down. This PR checks each Humming MXFP4 linear layer once at load time. A layer that would lose weights runs with 16-bit activations instead, which decode the checkpoint exactly, and vLLM logs one warning naming it. Every other layer is unchanged.

## Claims

- Humming MXFP4 linear layers now use exactly the checkpoint's weights. On `ibm-granite/granite-4.2-30b-mxfp4`, main decodes 28,000,270 weights wrongly (14,154,257 of them as 0); with this PR, 0. The issue's reproducer goes from 69 wrong weights to 0, and its N-padded case from 524,288 of 524,288 (all 0) to 0.
- Layers whose scales fit the range keep FP8 activations and the same kernel configuration as on main: 253 of the 256 MXFP4 layers of Granite-4.2-30B, and every layer of Granite-4.2-8B and 3B. On 8B and 3B, the prompt log-probs are bit-identical to main.
- Cost: only the layers that switch get slower. Per GEMM, 16-bit activations take 1.0 to 1.2x the FP8 time at M ≤ 16 and 1.8 to 1.9x at M ≥ 256 (still faster than Marlin). On Granite-4.2-30B, where 3 of 256 layers switch, end-to-end throughput is unchanged within run-to-run noise (3,852 vs 3,863 tokens/s, 2 runs each). The load-time check adds 0.2 to 0.4 ms per MXFP4 layer.

## Validation

Setup: one NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), TP 1, torch 2.14.0, humming-kernels 0.1.19, compressed-tensors 0.17.0. The unit tests and the issue's reproducer ran on current main `3cd3a7a` with and without this PR. The model runs used the same change on earlier main commits (`6c13a38` for WikiText-2, the first GSM8K run and throughput; `8656497` for the second GSM8K run); the commits since then do not touch the Humming linear path.

**New test.** `tests/kernels/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_scale_range.py` has CPU tests of the block count and a GPU test that builds a real `ReplicatedLinear` through `CompressedTensorsConfig`, loads MXFP4 weights with the weight loaders, runs `process_weights_after_loading`, reads the weights the Humming kernel uses back with identity inputs, and compares them exactly with the checkpoint decode. It also checks that only the out-of-range cases switch to 16-bit activations and log the warning.

```text
$ pytest -v tests/kernels/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_scale_range.py
main + new test only: 9 failed, 2 passed
  test_blocks_below_range[*] (6), test_per_row_range: AttributeError: ... has no attribute '_fused_e8m0_lossy_blocks'
  test_humming_mxfp4_layer_decodes_checkpoint[below_range]: Mismatched elements: 101 / 131072 (0.1%)
  test_humming_mxfp4_layer_decodes_checkpoint[n_padded]:    Mismatched elements: 65536 / 65536 (100.0%)
  test_humming_mxfp4_layer_decodes_checkpoint[in_range], [zero_block]: passed
PR: 11 passed
```

**Issue reproducer** (the script in #66074):

| Case | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| default (blocks at 2^-12, 2^-14, 2^-15 next to 2^0) | 69 of 1,048,576 wrong (36 as 0), FP8 fused E8M0 | 0 wrong, 16-bit activations, warning: 3 blocks |
| `--padded` (N = 128, all scales 2^-16) | 524,288 of 524,288 wrong (all 0) | 0 wrong, 16-bit activations, warning: 16,384 blocks |

**Model evaluation.** `vllm.LLM`, BF16 KV cache. Wrong weights are counted by reading every MXFP4 layer back through its kernel with identity inputs right after loading. Perplexity is over eight 2,048-token WikiText-2 windows (the issue's setup); GSM8K uses `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (`evaluate_gsm8k_offline`, 5-shot, 1,319 questions, greedy, 256 tokens).

| Checkpoint | Layers on 16-bit activations | Wrong weights (main → PR) | WikiText-2 ppl (main → PR) | GSM8K (main → PR), 2 runs each |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| granite-4.2-30b-mxfp4 | 3 of 256 (`layers.{4,6,7}.self_attn.qkv_proj`) | 28,000,270 → 0 | 11.3483 → 11.2636 | 86.35%, 86.35% → 86.66%, 86.73% |
| granite-4.2-8b-mxfp4 | 0 of 160 | 0 → 0 | 18.7949 → 18.7949 (all 16,376 log-probs bit-identical) | not run (no layer changes) |
| granite-4.2-3b-mxfp4 | 0 of 160 | 0 → 0 | 15.4617 → 15.4617 (all 16,376 log-probs bit-identical) | not run (no layer changes) |

As the issue shows, the weights Humming changes in Granite-4.2-30B do not move its output (Marlin gives bit-identical log-probs on the original and on a copy re-encoded to Humming's decode). The perplexity and GSM8K changes above come from the three layers now running with 16-bit activations. Prompt log-probs are bit-identical between two runs of the same build; 64-token greedy generations are not (2 to 4 of 20 identical between two main runs), so I do not use them to compare.

**Throughput.** `vllm bench throughput`, granite-4.2-30b-mxfp4, random dataset, 1,024 input and 128 output tokens, 256 prompts, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.35`, same GPU, runs alternated:

| Build | Runs (order) | Requests/s | Total tokens/s | Output tokens/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 2nd, 4th | 3.36, 3.35 | 3,870.1, 3,855.3 | 430.0, 428.4 |
| PR | 1st, 3rd | 3.35, 3.34 | 3,857.2, 3,846.8 | 428.6, 427.4 |

The means differ by 0.3%, about the spread between two runs of the same build (up to 0.4%). (The first main attempt stopped at vLLM's memory-profiling check because another process on the GPU changed its memory use; it was rerun last.)

<details>
<summary>GEMM time of one MXFP4 layer, FP8 vs 16-bit activations (µs per call, CUDA-graph replays)</summary>

Random weights with scales from 2^-7 to 2^0. For "16-bit", one block is set 20 binades lower, so the PR switches the layer. `bench_fallback.py`, H20-3e.

| N x K | M | Humming FP8 | Humming 16-bit (this PR's fallback) | Marlin | 16-bit / FP8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6144 x 4096 (Granite-30B qkv) | 1 | 13.8 | 13.8 | 14.6 | 1.00 |
| | 16 | 15.0 | 17.2 | 18.5 | 1.15 |
| | 64 | 29.8 | 34.6 | 51.6 | 1.16 |
| | 256 | 57.3 | 103.8 | 159.4 | 1.81 |
| | 1024 | 199.0 | 371.7 | 605.3 | 1.87 |
| | 8192 | 1569.1 | 2907.7 | 4834.4 | 1.85 |
| 4096 x 4096 | 1 / 256 / 8192 | 10.6 / 42.6 / 1057.6 | 11.6 / 69.3 / 1943.0 | 12.9 / 109.1 / 3190.5 | 1.10 / 1.63 / 1.84 |
| 65536 x 4096 | 1 / 256 / 8192 | 66.3 / 528.4 / 16071.0 | 91.0 / 981.5 / 30938.0 | 106.3 / 1606.5 / 51009.1 | 1.37 / 1.86 / 1.93 |
| 4096 x 32768 | 1 / 256 / 8192 | 40.6 / 275.7 / 8292.5 | 47.1 / 500.1 / 15379.3 | 53.5 / 788.5 / 24842.6 | 1.16 / 1.81 / 1.85 |

</details>

**Existing tests**, same results on main and with the PR:

```text
tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py   47 passed, 1 skipped
tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py tests/quantization/test_humming_compile.py   23 passed
tests/model_executor/test_utils.py                          32 passed
tests/quantization/test_online_mxfp4.py                     11 passed, 8 skipped
tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_tile_padding.py      98 passed, 13 skipped
tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k mxfp4      4 passed, 55 deselected
```

**Lint.** `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files: all hooks pass, including mypy and the test-tethering check (actionlint was skipped: it only checks workflow files and its Go dependencies could not be downloaded on the test machine).

**Why the regression test is at the layer level.** `tests/AGENTS.md` asks for a test through `LLM` with real weights. I looked for a small public MXFP4 checkpoint that hits this case by reading the E8M0 scales of the MXFP4 checkpoints vLLM's tests already load: `nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-MXFP4` has at most exactly 11 binades in a fused layer (in range), and `INCModel/Qwen3-1.7B-AutoRound-MXFP4-W4A4`, `amd-quark/Qwen3-1.7B-MXFP4` and `amd-quark/internal-testing-qwen3_0.6b-mxfp4-hadamard` have at most 8. The smallest checkpoint I know that hits it is granite-4.2-30b-mxfp4 (16 GB). So the test builds the layer with the same constructors and loading steps a checkpoint goes through, which fails on main for the reported reason and passes with the PR, and the LLM-level check is the Granite run above, outside CI. The test runs in the "(L4) Quantization Kernels" step (`tests/kernels/quantization`, which depends on `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization`); I could only run it on SM90.

**Duplicate check.** `gh issue view 66074 --comments` (no comments), `gh pr list --state open --search "66074 in:body"` (none), and searches for `humming mxfp4`, `humming e8m0`, `fused_e8m0` in vllm-project/vllm and vllm-project/humming found no PR that changes this range or the activation choice for out-of-range layers.

## Details

**Root cause.** `process_fused_e8m0_scale` in humming/transform.py takes the largest E8M0 code of the layer's weight tensor (per row only on the INT8 path, which adds a per-channel secondary scale), raises the scale of every block more than 11 (FP8) or 3 (INT8) binades below it to that limit, and re-encodes the block's E2M1 values relative to the raised scale (`process_mxfp4_w4a8_weight`). Values that do not fit are rounded or flushed to 0. The tensor is the fused one vLLM serves, so a small q or k shard next to a large v shard is affected. Humming also pads N to a multiple of 256 with scale 2^0, so on a padded layer whose scales are all 12 or more binades below 2^0, every weight becomes 0.

**Change.** In `prepare_humming_linear_layer_config`, after `check_and_fallback_input_schema` picks the activation schema, build Humming's `LayerConfig` with `prepare_layer_config` (same layout arguments as the transform; they are now shared). If it uses fused E8M0 scales, `_fused_e8m0_lossy_blocks` counts the blocks with a nonzero value outside the kept range, taking the per-row range and the 2^0 padding scale into account. If there are any, the layer gets `HummingInputSchema()` (16-bit activations; Humming then applies the E8M0 group scales as they are) and a warning, for example:

```text
model.layers.4.self_attn.qkv_proj: 494727 MXFP4 weight blocks have an E8M0 scale more than 11 binades below the largest scale of their weight tensor (scales range from 2^-28 to 2^-7), which Humming rounds or zeroes with float8e4m3 activations. Using 16-bit activations for this layer.
```

`vllm/utils/humming.py` exports `prepare_layer_config`, and `docs/features/quantization/README.md` describes the behavior.

**Why 16-bit activations.** It keeps the layer on Humming and on a path Humming already uses for group-scaled weights. Other options I considered:
- Padding N with an in-range scale, or leaving the padding out of the largest scale, would let padded layers keep FP8. But the padding happens inside humming-kernels (`check_and_pad_tensors`), so that is a follow-up there.
- Humming has a per-row range only together with a per-channel secondary scale (the INT8 path). Using it for FP8 would change the numerics of every MXFP4 layer.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- Layers that switch are slower (see the tables). On the three Granite checkpoints, 3 of 576 MXFP4 layers switch.
- The count is conservative: a block counts if it has any nonzero value, although at 12 binades the largest E2M1 values still survive (in the test's `below_range` case, 101 of the 128 values in the 4 out-of-range blocks change). A layer can therefore switch when no value would change; it stays exact, only slower.
- The check also applies when the checkpoint declares FP8 activations (`HummingMxFp4LinearKernel` passes `allow_input_schema_fallback=False` then), because keeping FP8 there changes the weights.
- Under tensor parallelism the decision is per rank, as each rank's shard has its own largest scale in Humming.
- The check runs once in `process_weights_after_loading` (two host reads per MXFP4 layer). The forward path is unchanged, with no new synchronization during inference.

**Not covered here.**
- Humming MXFP4 MoE: the same range applies per expert (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/humming/moe.py`).
- The native `quantization="humming"` linear path in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/humming.py`, which calls `prepare_and_transform_humming_tensors` directly.
- Padding N with an in-range scale inside humming-kernels, as a follow-up there.

---

comment.body:
Thanks, that makes sense. Fixing it in Humming is better than copying its rules here. A few details from our tests that may help with the patch:

- The window is set by the largest E8M0 scale in the whole (fused) tensor. Blocks fewer than 12 binades below it decode exactly, blocks 12 to 14 below are rounded, and from 15 below every value decodes as 0. With fused projections, one projection's large scales push the others out: in one layer of granite-4.2-30b-mxfp4, about a third of the nonzero weights.
- Of 34 public MXFP4 checkpoints we checked, 13 have blocks outside the window, about 298M weights in all.

I'm happy to run the same exact check (identity inputs, exact comparison) on your patch, including `use_fused_e8m0_scale=False` with FP8 activations, and on those checkpoints. Should I close this PR in favor of your patch, or keep it open until the Humming fix lands?

issue.title: [Bug] NVFP4 MoE: the Marlin backend applies the gate's global scale to the up projection
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

For a ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE checkpoint, each expert stores one `weight_scale_2` for the gate projection (w1) and one for the up projection (w3). The FP4 Marlin MoE kernel takes a single w13 global scale per expert, so `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` keeps the gate's and drops the up's ([modelopt_quant.py#L2738-L2755](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/0afb736d0aab96e3ab80b4c54a376213a1db67a6/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py#L2738-L2755)), with a one-time warning (`w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected.`). The up projection of every expert whose two scales differ is then dequantized with the gate's global scale. #27588 split the two scales for the other NVFP4 MoE backends; Marlin still collapses them.

Marlin is the default NVFP4 MoE runner up to Hopper GPUs (on an H20 the runner resolves to `MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN` with default flags). For compressed-tensors names, the same kernel path refuses such checkpoints at load ([compressed_tensors_w4a16_nvfp4_moe.py#L186-L202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/0afb736d0aab96e3ab80b4c54a376213a1db67a6/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w4a16_nvfp4_moe.py#L186-L202)).

Public checkpoints with differing gate and up scales:

| checkpoint | expert gate/up pairs that differ | median ratio | largest ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tattrongvu/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` | 8,532 of 12,384 | 1.08 | 9.96 |
| `LibertAIDAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` | 8,563 of 12,384 | 1.08 | 10.0 |
| `nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4` | 2 of 1,281 | 1.05 | 1.06 |

v0.5.23 has the same code.

### Reproduction

`repro.py` builds SGLang's `FusedMoE` with a ModelOpt NVFP4 config and the default runner, loads four experts through the layer's own weight loader and post-load step, and routes one token to each expert. The weights are chosen so the output reads off the global scale applied to the up projection: gate values 2 with block scale 32 make the gate output 64 (SiLU(64) is exactly 64), up values 1 with block scale 1 make the up output its global scale, and down values 1 sum it.

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# Which global scale SGLang's NVFP4 MoE (ModelOpt names, default runner) applies to each expert's up projection.
# Gate values 2 x block scale 32 make the gate output 64, for which SiLU is exact; up values 1 x block scale 1 make
# the up output its global scale; down values 1 sum it. So every output is I * 64 * g_gate * g_up_applied.
import json
import os
import socket
import tempfile

import torch

TINY = {"architectures": ["Qwen3ForCausalLM"], "model_type": "qwen3", "hidden_size": 1024, "intermediate_size": 3072,
        "num_hidden_layers": 1, "num_attention_heads": 16, "num_key_value_heads": 8, "head_dim": 128,
        "vocab_size": 4096, "max_position_embeddings": 4096, "rms_norm_eps": 1e-6, "torch_dtype": "bfloat16",
        "quantization_config": {"quant_method": "modelopt", "quant_algo": "NVFP4", "group_size": 16}}


def setup():
    from sglang.srt.configs.load_config import LoadConfig
    from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig
    from sglang.srt.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel
    from sglang.srt.layers.dp_attention import initialize_dp_attention
    from sglang.srt.layers.moe.utils import initialize_moe_config
    from sglang.srt.model_loader.loader import _get_quantization_config
    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import SpawnRanks, publish
    from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    json.dump(TINY, open(os.path.join(d, "config.json"), "w"))
    torch.cuda.set_device(0)
    sa = ServerArgs(model_path=d, load_format="dummy", tp_size=1, mem_fraction_static=0.05, disable_cuda_graph=True,
                    skip_tokenizer_init=True)
    publish(sa, role="scheduler", ranks=SpawnRanks(world_rank=0, gpu_id=0))
    s = socket.socket(); s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)); port = s.getsockname()[1]; s.close()
    init_distributed_environment(backend="nccl", world_size=1, rank=0, local_rank=0,
                                 distributed_init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}")
    initialize_model_parallel()
    mc = ModelConfig.from_server_args(sa)
    initialize_dp_attention(server_args=sa)
    try:
        from sglang.srt.distributed.bootstrap import init_layer_runtime
        init_layer_runtime(model_config=mc)
    except ImportError:
        pass
    initialize_moe_config()
    return _get_quantization_config(mc, LoadConfig(load_format="dummy"))


qc = setup()
from sglang.srt.layers.moe.fused_moe_triton.layer import FusedMoE  # noqa: E402
from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import TopK  # noqa: E402

E, H, I = 4, 512, 256
with torch.device("cuda"):
    moe = FusedMoE(num_experts=E, hidden_size=H, intermediate_size=I, layer_id=0, top_k=1,
                   params_dtype=torch.bfloat16, quant_config=qc, prefix="model.layers.0.mlp.experts")
    topk = TopK(top_k=1, renormalize=True, layer_id=0)
topk.bind_runner_backend(moe.runner_backend, routing_method_type=moe.routing_method_type)
params = dict(moe.named_parameters())
pairs = [(1.0, 2.0), (2.0, 1.0), (1.0, 1.0), (1.0, 4.0)]  # (gate, up) weight_scale_2 per expert
f8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn


def packed(n, k, code):  # two equal E2M1 codes per byte (code 4 = 2.0, code 2 = 1.0)
    return torch.full((n, k // 2), code | (code << 4), dtype=torch.uint8)


for e, (gg, gu) in enumerate(pairs):
    for shard, proj, rows, cols, code, block, g in (("w1", "gate_proj", I, H, 4, 32.0, gg),
                                                    ("w3", "up_proj", I, H, 2, 1.0, gu),
                                                    ("w2", "down_proj", H, I, 2, 1.0, 1.0)):
        pre = "w2_" if shard == "w2" else "w13_"
        for kind, t in (("weight", packed(rows, cols, code)),
                        ("weight_scale", torch.full((rows, cols // 16), block).to(f8)),
                        ("weight_scale_2", torch.tensor(g)), ("input_scale", torch.tensor(1.0))):
            moe.weight_loader(params[pre + kind], t.cuda(), f"model.layers.0.mlp.experts.{e}.{proj}.{kind}", shard, e)
moe.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(moe)
x = torch.zeros(E, H, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
x[torch.arange(E), torch.arange(E)] = 1.0
logits = torch.zeros(E, E, device="cuda")
logits[torch.arange(E), torch.arange(E)] = 10.0  # token e goes to expert e
with torch.inference_mode():
    y = moe(x, topk(x, logits)).float()
print("MoE runner:", moe.runner_backend)
for e, (gg, gu) in enumerate(pairs):
    print(f"expert {e}: gate scale {gg}, up scale {gu} -> up scale applied {y[e, 0].item() / (I * 64 * gg):g}")
```

</details>

Output on main `0afb736` (H20-3e, SM90):

```
w1_weight_scale_2 must match w3_weight_scale_2. Accuracy may be affected.
MoE runner: MoeRunnerBackend.MARLIN
expert 0: gate scale 1.0, up scale 2.0 -> up scale applied 1
expert 1: gate scale 2.0, up scale 1.0 -> up scale applied 2
expert 2: gate scale 1.0, up scale 1.0 -> up scale applied 1
expert 3: gate scale 1.0, up scale 4.0 -> up scale applied 1
```

The up projection of experts 0 and 3 gets the gate's scale (1.0 instead of 2.0 and 4.0), and expert 1's gets 2.0 instead of 1.0.

### Environment

1x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1, SGLang main `0afb736` (also v0.5.23).

issue.title: [Bug] NVFP4 W4A4 linear keeps the largest weight global scale of fused q/k/v and gate/up layers without a check
issue.body:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug The NVFP4 GEMMs take one weight global scale per layer. A fused layer (q/k/v, gate/up) loads one global scale per projection, and the post-load step of the W4A4 linear schemes keeps the largest one for all projections, with no check or warning: - `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4` ([compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py#L96-L102](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py#L96-L102)), which serves compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoints on SM100 and SM120 by default; - `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod` ([modelopt_quant.py#L1887](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py#L1887)), for ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints, on every backend it supports (FlashInfer, Marlin). The other projections keep their own block scales, so their weights are dequantized with the wrong global scale: with compressed-tensors' divisor convention, a projection whose global scale is 10048 next to one of 12992 is scaled by 10048/12992 = 0.77. The weight-only paths check this. `CompressedTensorsW4A16Fp4`, which serves the same compressed-tensors checkpoints on SM80-SM90, refuses them at load ([compressed_tensors_w4a16_nvfp4.py#L204-L210](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w4a16_nvfp4.py#L204-L210)), and `ModelOptNvFp4A16LinearMethod` warns ([modelopt_quant.py#L2272-L2276](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py#L2272-L2276)). So the same checkpoint is refused on an H100 and served with changed weights on a B200. Public checkpoints with such layers: in `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-NVFP4`, 9 of 60 q/k/v groups have differing global scales (largest ratio 1.57; layer 11: q_proj 12992, k_proj 10048); in `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4`, 5 of 30 (largest ratio 1.76). v0.5.23 has the same code. ### Reproduction `repro.py` runs the post-load step of both schemes on a fused q/k/v layer with dummy weights and the global scales of layer 11 above. It does not run the GEMM, so it needs no SM100 GPU.
repro.py ```python # The post-load step of the NVFP4 W4A4 linear schemes on a fused q/k/v layer whose parts have different # global scales, as in RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-NVFP4 (layer 11: k_proj 10048, q_proj 12992). Dummy weights. import logging import torch from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.schemes import CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4 from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp4_utils import initialize_fp4_gemm_config from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant import ModelOptFp4Config, ModelOptFp4LinearMethod from sglang.srt.runtime_context import publish from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s") publish(ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", device="cuda"), role="test") initialize_fp4_gemm_config() torch.set_default_device("cuda") sizes = [512, 128, 128] # q_proj, k_proj, v_proj def load(param, w, *args): param.data.copy_(w) # compressed-tensors NVFP4 (served by CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4 on SM100 and SM120) scheme, layer = CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4(), torch.nn.Module() scheme.create_weights(layer, output_partition_sizes=sizes, input_size_per_partition=2048, params_dtype=torch.bfloat16, weight_loader=load) layer.weight_global_scale.data.copy_(torch.tensor([12992.0, 10048.0, 10048.0])) layer.input_global_scale.data.fill_(100.0) before = layer.weight_global_scale.tolist() try: scheme.process_weights_after_loading(layer) print(f"compressed-tensors: checkpoint weight_global_scale {before} -> used for all parts: " f"{layer.weight_global_scale.item()}") except ValueError as e: print(f"compressed-tensors: ValueError: {e}") # ModelOpt NVFP4 (ModelOptFp4LinearMethod) config = ModelOptFp4Config(is_checkpoint_nvfp4_serialized=True, group_size=16) method, layer = ModelOptFp4LinearMethod(config), torch.nn.Module() method.create_weights(layer, input_size_per_partition=2048, output_partition_sizes=sizes, input_size=2048, output_size=sum(sizes), params_dtype=torch.bfloat16, weight_loader=load) layer.weight_scale_2.data.copy_(1 / torch.tensor([12992.0, 10048.0, 10048.0])) layer.input_scale.data.fill_(0.01) layer.weight_scale.data.fill_(1.0) before = layer.weight_scale_2.tolist() method.process_weights_after_loading(layer) used = (layer.alpha / 0.01).item() # alpha = input_scale * weight_scale_2 print(f"ModelOpt: checkpoint weight_scale_2 {[f'{x:.3e}' for x in before]} -> used for all parts: {used:.3e}") ```
On main `91fd675` (1x H20-3e; the ModelOpt method takes its Marlin branch there): ``` $ python repro.py compressed-tensors: checkpoint weight_global_scale [12992.0, 10048.0, 10048.0] -> used for all parts: 12992.0 ModelOpt: checkpoint weight_scale_2 ['7.697e-05', '9.952e-05', '9.952e-05'] -> used for all parts: 9.952e-05 ``` ### Environment
python3 -m sglang.check_env (trimmed) ``` Python: 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 12:30:59) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H20-3e GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 570.133.20 PyTorch: 2.14.1+cu130 sglang: 0.5.23 sglang-kernel: 0.4.10 flashinfer_python: 0.7.2 triton: 3.8.0 transformers: 5.19.0 huggingface_hub: 1.33.0 Hypervisor vendor:: KVM ```
Main `91fd675` was run from source in the same environment.

issue.title: [Bug]: `enable_weights_track` refuses correct weight-only NVFP4 checkpoints (input scales that no export writes and no kernel reads)
issue.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py (trimmed) ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.14.0+cu130 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 12:30:59) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H20-3e ... GPU 7: NVIDIA H20-3e Nvidia driver version : 570.133.20 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.3 [pip3] torch==2.14.0 [pip3] transformers==5.22.1 [pip3] triton==3.8.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.33.0rc1.dev931+g5a92788a1 (git sha: 5a92788a1) ``` `compressed-tensors==0.17.0`.
The Python sources were those of main `f358f0578` (2026-11-06) on top of that nightly wheel; the files involved are the same in both and on main `3012587f0`. ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary** With `--model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_weights_track": true}'`, vLLM refuses correct weight-only NVFP4 checkpoints: ```text ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: {'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.routed_experts.w13_input_global_scale', 'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.routed_experts.w2_input_global_scale'} ``` The weight-only NVFP4 methods register activation input scales that weight-only exports do not write and that no weight-only kernel reads: - compressed-tensors NVFP4A16 MoE: `w13_input_global_scale` / `w2_input_global_scale` (`compressed_tensors_moe_w4a4_nvfp4.py:194-208`, also registered when `use_a16`); - ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE with weight-only activations (`use_a16`): `w13_input_scale` / `w2_input_scale` (`modelopt.py:1040-1057`); - ModelOpt `W4A16_NVFP4` linear layers: `input_scale` (`_DropInputScale`, `modelopt.py:2647`; it is registered so that older exports that do write it still load, and then dropped). Since #57108, `track_weights_loading` (`default_loader.py:556-607`) checks every parameter of a quantized layer except KV-cache, online-quantization, empty and config-built parameters. These input scales are not exempt, so the check reports them as missing and aborts the load. Loading without the check is correct; only the check is wrong. Public checkpoints in these formats store none of these input scales, for example `furiosa-ai/K-EXAONE-236B-A23B-NVFP4A16` (compressed-tensors NVFP4A16, MoE; no input scale in its safetensors index) and `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4` (ModelOpt mixed precision; its `W4A16_NVFP4` experts, shared experts and `lm_head` have no `input_scale`). **Reproduction** The script writes a one-layer Qwen3-MoE checkpoint in compressed-tensors NVFP4A16 format (as LLM Compressor writes it: `weight_packed`, `weight_scale`, `weight_global_scale`, no input scales; values are random) and loads it with the check enabled. Nothing is downloaded. ```python import json import os import tempfile import torch from safetensors.torch import save_file from vllm import LLM H, I, E, HEADS, KV, D, V = 512, 256, 8, 4, 2, 128, 256 def nvfp4(prefix, out, inp): return { f"{prefix}.weight_packed": torch.randint(0, 256, (out, inp // 2), dtype=torch.uint8), f"{prefix}.weight_scale": torch.full((out, inp // 16), 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), f"{prefix}.weight_global_scale": torch.tensor([100.0]), } def write_checkpoint(path): bf16, p = torch.bfloat16, "model.layers.0" t = { "model.embed_tokens.weight": torch.randn(V, H, dtype=bf16) * 0.02, "model.norm.weight": torch.ones(H, dtype=bf16), "lm_head.weight": torch.randn(V, H, dtype=bf16) * 0.02, f"{p}.input_layernorm.weight": torch.ones(H, dtype=bf16), f"{p}.post_attention_layernorm.weight": torch.ones(H, dtype=bf16), f"{p}.self_attn.q_norm.weight": torch.ones(D, dtype=bf16), f"{p}.self_attn.k_norm.weight": torch.ones(D, dtype=bf16), f"{p}.mlp.gate.weight": torch.randn(E, H, dtype=bf16) * 0.02, } for name, out, inp in (("q_proj", HEADS * D, H), ("k_proj", KV * D, H), ("v_proj", KV * D, H), ("o_proj", H, HEADS * D)): t |= nvfp4(f"{p}.self_attn.{name}", out, inp) for e in range(E): for name, out, inp in (("gate_proj", I, H), ("up_proj", I, H), ("down_proj", H, I)): t |= nvfp4(f"{p}.mlp.experts.{e}.{name}", out, inp) save_file(t, os.path.join(path, "model.safetensors")) weights = {"num_bits": 4, "type": "float", "strategy": "tensor_group", "group_size": 16, "symmetric": True, "dynamic": False} config = { "architectures": ["Qwen3MoeForCausalLM"], "model_type": "qwen3_moe", "hidden_size": H, "intermediate_size": 2 * H, "moe_intermediate_size": I, "num_hidden_layers": 1, "num_attention_heads": HEADS, "num_key_value_heads": KV, "head_dim": D, "num_experts": E, "num_experts_per_tok": 2, "decoder_sparse_step": 1, "mlp_only_layers": [], "norm_topk_prob": True, "vocab_size": V, "max_position_embeddings": 64, "rms_norm_eps": 1e-6, "tie_word_embeddings": False, "torch_dtype": "bfloat16", "quantization_config": { "quant_method": "compressed-tensors", "format": "nvfp4-pack-quantized", "config_groups": {"group_0": {"targets": ["Linear"], "weights": weights, "input_activations": None}}, "ignore": ["lm_head", "re:.*mlp.gate$"], }, } with open(os.path.join(path, "config.json"), "w") as f: json.dump(config, f) if __name__ == "__main__": with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as path: write_checkpoint(path) llm = LLM( model=path, skip_tokenizer_init=True, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=32, kv_cache_memory_bytes=16 << 20, gpu_memory_utilization=0.05, model_loader_extra_config={"enable_weights_track": True}, ) print("loaded:", type(llm).__name__) ``` Output: ```text ValueError: Following weights were not initialized from checkpoint: {'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.routed_experts.w13_input_global_scale', 'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.routed_experts.w2_input_global_scale'} ``` The same checkpoint in the two ModelOpt weight-only layouts (`quant_algo: W4A16_NVFP4`, and `quant_algo: NVFP4` with `input_activations: null`) is refused the same way, listing `self_attn.qkv_proj.input_scale`, `self_attn.o_proj.input_scale` and the experts' `w13_input_scale` / `w2_input_scale`. The W4A4 variants of both formats, which do store input scales, load. **Expected**: the checkpoint loads; the check still reports tensors these layers do need (for example a missing `weight_scale`), and the input scales of W4A4 checkpoints. **Suggested fix** Let a quantization method mark a parameter as optional in the checkpoint (it stays registered for exports that write it), mark these weight-only input scales, and skip such parameters in `track_weights_loading`. I have a patch with tests and can open a PR. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [ ] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issue.title: [Fix] Keep the KV-cache method of NVFP4 draft models (NextN, MTP, Eagle3)
issue.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #48725.

This PR is stacked on #48716. Its first two commits are #48716; the new changes are the last two commits, `[Fix] deepseek_nextn: keep the KV-cache method of NVFP4 NextN drafts` and `[Fix] qwen3_5_mtp, kimi_k25_eagle3: keep the KV-cache method of NVFP4 drafts`. Please merge #48716 first. I will rebase this PR after that.

For `modelopt_fp4` checkpoints, `DeepseekModelNextN` builds the NextN layer with `quant_config=None` (#7376), because NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoints keep that layer in BF16. This also removes the KV-cache method from the draft's `RadixAttention`. With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, the draft attention then has no `k_scale`/`v_scale`. The target's attention layers have them, and so does the draft of a ModelOpt FP8 checkpoint. The GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-OCR NextN drafts copy the override, and the GLM-5 and GLM-5.x-Flash drafts inherit it. The Qwen3.5 and Qwen4Exp MTP drafts build their MTP layer unquantized for `modelopt_fp4` and `MIXED_PRECISION` checkpoints, and the Kimi-K2.5 Eagle3 draft does so for `modelopt_fp4`, with the same effect.

## Modifications

- `layers/quantization/kv_cache.py`: a new helper, `add_kv_cache_quant_methods(module, quant_config, prefix)`. For every `RadixAttention` in a module built with `quant_config=None`, it sets the KV-cache method of `quant_config` and creates the scale parameters.
- `deepseek_nextn.py`, `glm4_moe_lite_nextn.py`, `glm_ocr_nextn.py`: the NextN layer is still built unquantized, and its attention layers then get the checkpoint's KV-cache method through the helper.
- With #48716, the MLA drafts (DeepSeek, GLM-4.7-Flash, GLM-5, GLM-5.x-Flash) still skip the checkpoint's KV-cache scales and use 1.0, like their targets. The GLM-OCR draft uses standard attention and now has `k_scale`/`v_scale`, like its target.
- `qwen3_5_mtp.py`: a new `_mtp_kv_cache_quant_config` returns the checkpoint's quant config when `_mtp_quant_config` builds the MTP module of a `modelopt_fp4` or `modelopt_mixed` checkpoint unquantized; `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` passes it to the helper after building the MTP module. `qwen4_exp_mtp.py` does the same for `Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP`.
- `kimi_k25_eagle3.py`: for `modelopt_fp4`, the draft is still built unquantized, and its attention gets the checkpoint's KV-cache method through the helper. It uses MLA, so with #48716 it keeps 1.0, like its target.
- The drafts' other layers keep the quant methods they had. The Quark and NPU cases of `_mtp_quant_config` are not changed.

## Accuracy Tests

Setup: 1x H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, dummy weights, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. "Base" is main `91fd6756` with the two commits of #48716; "this PR" adds the last commit.

- New test `test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_nextn_kv_cache_quant.py` (2 cases): it fails on base and passes with this PR.
- KV-cache method of the NextN draft's attention, ModelOpt FP8 and NVFP4 configs:

| draft class | FP8, base and this PR | NVFP4, base | NVFP4, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN` | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` | none | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` |
| `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLMNextN` | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` | none | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` |
| `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN` (GLM-5) | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` | none | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` |
| `Glm5NextForConditionalGenerationNextN` (GLM-5.3-Flash) | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` | none | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` |
| `GlmOcrForConditionalGenerationNextN` | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` | none | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` |

- New test `test/registered/unit/models/test_mtp_draft_kv_cache_quant.py` (5 cases): 4 fail before the last commit and all pass with it. It checks that the BF16 MTP drafts of NVFP4 and `MIXED_PRECISION` configs keep unquantized weights and get `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod`, that the Qwen3.5 MTP layer's ModelOpt scales load through the draft's loader, and that a quantized FP8 draft does not change.
- MTP and Eagle3 drafts, built from the configs of `codecho/Qwen3.5-0.8B-text-only`, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` and `lightseekorg/kimi-k2.5-eagle3-mla`, with `mtp.layers.0.self_attn.{k_proj.k_scale, v_proj.v_scale}` = 0.0625 / 0.03125 in the checkpoint:

| draft class | FP8, before and after | NVFP4, before | NVFP4, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod`, 0.0625 / 0.03125 | none, no scales | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod`, 0.0625 / 0.03125 |
| `Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP` | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod`, 0.0625 / 0.03125 | none, no scales | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod`, 0.0625 / 0.03125 |
| `Eagle3DeepseekV2ForCausalLM` | not run (the draft's post-load step raises `NotImplementedError` for FP8 weights, before and after) | none, no scales | `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod`, 1.0 / 1.0 (MLA) |

- The repro in #48725 (DeepSeek-V3 config, 4 layers) gives `quant_method=None` and no scales for the NVFP4 draft on base. With this PR it gives `ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod` with `k_scale = v_scale = 1.0`, the same as the FP8 draft.
- These related unit tests pass on base and with this PR: `test_compressed_tensors_kv_cache`, `test_deepseek_mla_kv_scale_loading`, `test_deepseek_nextn_mm_embed`, `test_deepseek_pp_mtp_embedding`, `test_deepseek_quark_block_fp8_loading`, `test_glm4_moe_lite_weight_loading`, `test_glm5_next_modelopt`, `test_glm_nextn_moe_ptpc`, `test_kv_calibration_loader_layout`, `test_modelopt_nvfp4`, `test_qwen3_5_mtp_quant_config`, and for the last commit also `test_nemotron_h_mtp`, `test_qwen3_5_modelopt_fp4`, `test_qwen3_5_packed_weight_loader`, `test_qwen3_5_pipeline_parallel`, `test_qwen4_exp_decode_comm` and `test_qwen4_exp_ple_table`. pre-commit passes on all commits.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel changes. The helper runs once, when the draft model is built.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Parts of this change were drafted with AI assistance and reviewed and tested by the author.

issue.title: [Bug] TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM / TorchNativePhi3ForCausalLM load no checkpoint tensors and no KV-cache scales
issue.body:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug `TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM` and `TorchNativePhi3ForCausalLM` are selected with `--json-model-override-args '{"architectures": ["TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM"]}'`, as the module docstring shows for `sglang.benchmark.one_batch`. With the default load format they load no checkpoint tensor, and they lose the checkpoint's FP8 KV-cache scales for three more reasons: 1. `load_weights` calls `load_weights_to_module("", weights)` ([torch_native_llama.py#L493-L498](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/torch_native_llama.py#L493-L498)), which collects the parameters of the root module only (`recurse=False`, [#L460](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/torch_native_llama.py#L460)). The root module has none of its own, so every tensor is skipped and the model keeps its initial values. Nothing is logged. 2. `LlamaAttention` builds `RadixAttention` without `quant_config` ([#L243](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/torch_native_llama.py#L243)), so attention has no KV-cache method and no `k_scale`/`v_scale`; an FP8 KV cache runs with a scale of 1.0. 3. The loader has no rule for KV-scale names: `.k_scale` (compressed-tensors) is skipped and `.k_proj.k_scale` (ModelOpt) is renamed to `qkv_proj.k_scale` and skipped. 4. Phi-3 checkpoints store fused `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj` tensors, but `qkv_proj_weight_loader` and `gate_up_proj_weight_loader` ([#L72](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/torch_native_llama.py#L72), [#L140](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/torch_native_llama.py#L140)) need a shard id, so once (1) is fixed `TorchNativePhi3ForCausalLM` cannot load them. Separately, `--load-format layered` (`LayeredModelLoader`, the other user of `load_weights_to_module`) passes one weight generator to every submodule ([loader.py#L1150-L1168](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py#L1150-L1168)), so only the first submodule it fills gets its tensors. This issue does not cover that. v0.5.23 has the same code. ### Reproduction `repro.py` builds a tiny random Llama or Phi-3 checkpoint (2 layers) with per-layer KV-cache scales under the names LLM Compressor uses and a compressed-tensors config that declares a static FP8 KV cache, loads it with the TorchNative class, and prints whether `embed_tokens` holds the checkpoint tensor and what each attention layer loaded.
repro.py ```python # usage: python repro.py # A tiny random Llama or Phi-3 checkpoint with per-layer KV-cache scales under the names LLM Compressor uses. import glob import json import os import sys import torch import transformers as tf from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file from sglang.srt.configs.device_config import DeviceConfig from sglang.srt.configs.load_config import LoadConfig from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig from sglang.srt.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel from sglang.srt.distributed.bootstrap import init_layer_runtime from sglang.srt.layers.dp_attention import initialize_dp_attention from sglang.srt.layers.radix_attention import RadixAttention from sglang.srt.model_loader.loader import get_model_loader from sglang.srt.runtime_context import SpawnRanks, publish from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs arch, load_format, work = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] path = f"{work}/{arch}" if not os.path.exists(f"{path}/config.json"): torch.manual_seed(0) c = dict(num_hidden_layers=2, hidden_size=256, intermediate_size=512, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, vocab_size=1024, max_position_embeddings=512) cfg = tf.Phi3Config(**c, pad_token_id=0) if "Phi3" in arch else tf.LlamaConfig(**c, head_dim=64) tf.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(cfg).to(torch.bfloat16).save_pretrained(path) [shard] = glob.glob(f"{path}/model*.safetensors") t = load_file(shard) for i, (k, v) in enumerate([(0.5, 0.125), (0.25, 0.0625)]): t[f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.k_scale"], t[f"model.layers.{i}.self_attn.v_scale"] = torch.tensor(k), torch.tensor(v) save_file(t, shard, metadata={"format": "pt"}) j = json.load(open(f"{path}/config.json")) j["quantization_config"] = {"quant_method": "compressed-tensors", "format": "dense", "config_groups": {}, "kv_cache_scheme": {"num_bits": 8, "type": "float", "strategy": "tensor", "dynamic": False, "symmetric": True}} json.dump(j, open(f"{path}/config.json", "w")) args = ServerArgs(model_path=path, load_format=load_format, kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3", json_model_override_args=json.dumps({"architectures": [arch]})) publish(args, role="scheduler", ranks=SpawnRanks(world_rank=0, gpu_id=0)) torch.cuda.set_device(0) init_distributed_environment(world_size=1, rank=0, local_rank=0, distributed_init_method="tcp://127.0.0.1:29591") initialize_model_parallel() initialize_dp_attention(server_args=args) cfg = ModelConfig.from_server_args(args) init_layer_runtime(model_config=cfg) model = get_model_loader(LoadConfig(load_format=load_format)).load_model( model_config=cfg, device_config=DeviceConfig("cuda")) ref = load_file(glob.glob(f"{path}/model*.safetensors")[0])["model.embed_tokens.weight"] print(f"{arch} {load_format}: embed_tokens loaded: {torch.equal(model.model.embed_tokens.weight.cpu(), ref)}") for n, m in model.named_modules(): if isinstance(m, RadixAttention): method = type(m.quant_method).__name__ if m.quant_method is not None else None tensors = [None if t is None else round(t.item(), 4) for t in (m.k_scale, m.v_scale)] print(f" {n}: quant_method={method} k_scale={m.k_scale_float} v_scale={m.v_scale_float} " f"(tensors {tensors[0]} / {tensors[1]})") ```
On main `91fd675` (1x H20-3e): ``` $ python repro.py TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM auto /tmp/tn TorchNativeLlamaForCausalLM auto: embed_tokens loaded: False model.layers.0.self_attn.attn: quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None (tensors None / None) model.layers.1.self_attn.attn: quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None (tensors None / None) $ python repro.py TorchNativePhi3ForCausalLM auto /tmp/tn TorchNativePhi3ForCausalLM auto: embed_tokens loaded: False model.layers.0.self_attn.attn: quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None (tensors None / None) model.layers.1.self_attn.attn: quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None (tensors None / None) ``` The checkpoint stores k/v scales 0.5/0.125 (layer 0) and 0.25/0.0625 (layer 1). ### Environment
python3 -m sglang.check_env (trimmed) ``` Python: 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 12:30:59) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H20-3e GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 570.133.20 PyTorch: 2.14.1+cu130 sglang: 0.5.23 sglang-kernel: 0.4.10 flashinfer_python: 0.7.2 triton: 3.8.0 transformers: 5.19.0 huggingface_hub: 1.33.0 Hypervisor vendor:: KVM ```
Main `91fd675` was run from source in the same environment.

issue.title: [Bug] Gemma 4 and Gemma 3n KV-shared layers read the FP8 KV cache with scale 1.0 instead of the writing layer's scales
issue.body:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug The last `num_kv_shared_layers` layers of Gemma 4 and Gemma 3n write no KV cache. Their `RadixAttention` is built with the `layer_id` of an earlier layer of the same type, the owner, and reads the owner's cache ([gemma4_causal.py#L428-L440](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_causal.py#L428-L440), [gemma3n_causal.py#L412-L424](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma3n_causal.py#L412-L424); `save_kv_cache=False` at [gemma4_causal.py#L541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_causal.py#L541) and [gemma3n_causal.py#L495](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma3n_causal.py#L495)). With an FP8 KV cache and checkpoint KV-cache scales, the owner writes K/V divided by its own `k_scale`/`v_scale`. The KV-shared layer reads that cache with its own scales, which are separate parameters: Gemma 4 checkpoints have no scales for these layers, so they stay at the default 1.0 ([kv_cache.py#L51-L63](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/kv_cache.py#L51-L63)), and Gemma 3n checkpoints can have their own values for them. Either way, attention in the KV-shared layers dequantizes the owner's cache with the wrong scale. Nothing is logged. v0.5.23 has the same code. This affects Gemma 4 (`Gemma4ForCausalLM`, `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`, and Gemma 4 Unified, which uses the same text model) and Gemma 3n. For `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, 20 of 35 layers are KV-shared. #43532 (closed, not merged) had a fix for Gemma 4. ### Reproduction `repro.py` uses one GPU and dummy weights, and only reads `config.json` of the given model. It declares a static FP8 KV cache, loads a distinct `k_scale`/`v_scale` for every layer under the compressed-tensors names, runs the post-load step, and compares the scales of each KV-shared layer with those of the layer whose cache it reads.
repro.py ```python # usage: python repro.py import json import re import sys import torch from sglang.srt.configs.load_config import LoadConfig from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig from sglang.srt.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel from sglang.srt.distributed.bootstrap import init_layer_runtime from sglang.srt.layers.dp_attention import initialize_dp_attention from sglang.srt.layers.moe import initialize_moe_config from sglang.srt.layers.radix_attention import RadixAttention from sglang.srt.model_loader.loader import DefaultModelLoader, _get_quantization_config, _initialize_model from sglang.srt.model_loader.utils import set_default_torch_dtype from sglang.srt.runtime_context import SpawnRanks, publish from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs repo, prefix = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] # a compressed-tensors checkpoint that only declares a static FP8 KV cache qc = {"quant_method": "compressed-tensors", "config_groups": {}, "kv_cache_scheme": {"num_bits": 8, "type": "float", "strategy": "tensor", "dynamic": False, "symmetric": True}} args = ServerArgs(model_path=repo, load_format="dummy", kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3", json_model_override_args=json.dumps({"quantization_config": qc})) publish(args, role="scheduler", ranks=SpawnRanks(world_rank=0, gpu_id=0)) torch.cuda.set_device(0) init_distributed_environment(world_size=1, rank=0, local_rank=0, distributed_init_method="tcp://127.0.0.1:29581") initialize_model_parallel() initialize_dp_attention(server_args=args) cfg, lc = ModelConfig.from_server_args(args), LoadConfig(load_format="dummy") init_layer_runtime(model_config=cfg) initialize_moe_config() with set_default_torch_dtype(cfg.dtype), torch.device("cuda"): model = _initialize_model(cfg, lc, _get_quantization_config(cfg, lc)) attns = {int(re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.", n).group(1)): m for n, m in model.named_modules() if isinstance(m, RadixAttention)} # a distinct k/v scale for every layer, named the way LLM Compressor names them weights = [] for i in attns: weights += [(f"{prefix}.{i}.self_attn.k_scale", torch.tensor(0.01 * (i + 1))), (f"{prefix}.{i}.self_attn.v_scale", torch.tensor(0.001 * (i + 1)))] model.load_weights(weights) DefaultModelLoader.postprocess_weights(model, torch.device("cuda")) shared = [i for i, m in attns.items() if m.layer_id != i] wrong = [i for i in shared if (attns[i].k_scale_float, attns[i].v_scale_float) != (attns[attns[i].layer_id].k_scale_float, attns[attns[i].layer_id].v_scale_float)] print(f"{type(model).__name__}: {len(attns)} layers, {len(shared)} read another layer's KV cache, " f"{len(wrong)} of them with scales other than that layer's") for i in shared[:2] + shared[-1:]: o = attns[i].layer_id print(f"layer {i}: reads the KV cache of layer {o}; k_scale={attns[i].k_scale_float:.4g} " f"v_scale={attns[i].v_scale_float:.4g}, layer {o}: k_scale={attns[o].k_scale_float:.4g} v_scale={attns[o].v_scale_float:.4g}") ```
