issue.title: [Bug] More model loaders drop checkpoint FP8 KV-cache scales (Qwen1.5/2-MoE, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-Next, AFMoE, Gemma 3n, Gemma 4 Unified, Bailing-V2.5, DBRX, HRM-Text, Nanbeige, ...)
issue.body:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug The attention of these models is built with `quant_config`, so it has `k_scale`/`v_scale` parameters, but their `load_weights` never maps the checkpoint's scale names to them. With a checkpoint that declares a static FP8 KV cache (compressed-tensors `kv_cache_scheme`, or ModelOpt `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8`) and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, the scales are skipped and the FP8 KV cache runs with a scale of 1.0. #39942 reports the same for Qwen3-MoE, Qwen2 and Mixtral, and a comment there lists GLM-4, GLM-4V, GLM-OCR, Phi, OPT, Starcoder2, Persimmon, Grok-1, Zaya, Spark2.5, LocateAnything and Cohere2-MoE. The loaders below are not reported there. There are four ways the names get lost: 1. No rule for KV-scale names. The compressed-tensors name `.k_scale` is skipped as unknown, and the ModelOpt name `.k_proj.k_scale` is renamed to `qkv_proj.k_scale` by the stacked mapping and then skipped: - Qwen1.5-MoE / Qwen2-MoE ([qwen2_moe.py#L1315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py#L1315)), AFMoE ([afmoe.py#L595](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/afmoe.py#L595)), `QuantMixtralForCausalLM` ([mixtral_quant.py#L392](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/mixtral_quant.py#L392)), EmbeddingGemma 2 ([embedding_gemma2.py#L831](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/embedding_gemma2.py#L831)), Gemma 4 Unified ([gemma4_unified.py#L339](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_unified.py#L339); the closed #43537 had a fix), Bailing-V2.5 ([bailing_moe_linear.py#L1364](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/bailing_moe_linear.py#L1364)). - Qwen2.5-VL ([qwen2_5_vl.py#L904](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_5_vl.py#L904)): the same, and the ModelOpt name raises `KeyError: 'model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale'`. 2. A rule in the wrong place or for one naming only. Gemma 3n (text and multimodal loaders) calls `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` after the stacked rename ([gemma3n_causal.py#L1002](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma3n_causal.py#L1002), [gemma3n_mm.py#L482](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/gemma3n_mm.py#L482)), so ModelOpt names are lost. Qwen3-Next (also used by its MTP draft) and Qwen4Exp map the ModelOpt names only ([qwen3_next.py#L1201-L1204](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_next.py#L1201-L1204), [qwen4_exp.py#L2533-L2536](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp.py#L2533-L2536)), so compressed-tensors names are lost. 3. The ModelOpt branch of `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` only knows attention modules named `self_attn` or `mixer` ([weight_utils.py#L1833](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py#L1833)). ModelOpt names the scales after the attention module, whatever it is called. DBRX has the rule, but its `transformer.blocks.0.norm_attn_norm.attn.k_proj.k_scale` is mapped to `...attn.k_proj.attn.k_scale` and dropped with a warning; Bailing-V2.5's `model.layers.0.attention.k_proj.k_scale` has the same problem once its loader has a rule. 4. One `RadixAttention` per loop or recurrence step. HRM-Text ([hrm_text.py#L462](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/hrm_text.py#L462)) and Nanbeige loop models ([nanbeige.py#L492](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/nanbeige.py#L492)) keep one attention per step under `.attn.`, while the checkpoint has one scale per layer. Neither loader maps it; Nanbeige also renames the ModelOpt name to `qkv_proj.k_scale` first. Most of these drop the names silently. DBRX (ModelOpt names), Nanbeige and the Gemma 3n text model log a warning per dropped name. Three fail loudly on one naming: Qwen2.5-VL and the Gemma 3n multimodal model raise `KeyError` on the ModelOpt names, and Qwen3-Next raises `AssertionError` on the compressed-tensors names. v0.5.23 has the same code. ### Reproduction `repro.py` uses one GPU and dummy weights, and only reads `config.json` of the given model. It declares a static FP8 KV cache in the format's own config, loads two scales for one layer under the names that format uses, runs the post-load step, and prints that layer's attention.
repro.py ```python # usage: python repro.py [''] import json import re import sys import torch from sglang.srt.configs.load_config import LoadConfig from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig from sglang.srt.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel from sglang.srt.distributed.bootstrap import init_layer_runtime from sglang.srt.layers.dp_attention import initialize_dp_attention from sglang.srt.layers.moe import initialize_moe_config from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import initialize_fp8_gemm_config from sglang.srt.layers.radix_attention import RadixAttention from sglang.srt.model_loader.loader import DefaultModelLoader, _get_quantization_config, _initialize_model from sglang.srt.model_loader.utils import set_default_torch_dtype from sglang.srt.runtime_context import SpawnRanks, publish from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs repo, fmt, prefix = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] ov = json.loads(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else {} ov["quantization_config"] = { # a static FP8 KV cache, in each format's own config "ct": {"quant_method": "compressed-tensors", "config_groups": {}, "kv_cache_scheme": {"num_bits": 8, "type": "float", "strategy": "tensor", "dynamic": False, "symmetric": True}}, "modelopt": {"quant_method": "modelopt", "quant_algo": "FP8", "kv_cache_quant_algo": "FP8", "exclude_modules": ["lm_head"]}, }[fmt] # per-layer KV-cache scales of one layer, named the way each tool exports them names = {"ct": ("self_attn.k_scale", "self_attn.v_scale"), "modelopt": ("self_attn.k_proj.k_scale", "self_attn.v_proj.v_scale")}[fmt] args = ServerArgs(model_path=repo, load_format="dummy", kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3", json_model_override_args=json.dumps(ov)) publish(args, role="scheduler", ranks=SpawnRanks(world_rank=0, gpu_id=0)) torch.cuda.set_device(0) init_distributed_environment(world_size=1, rank=0, local_rank=0, distributed_init_method="tcp://127.0.0.1:29571") initialize_model_parallel() initialize_dp_attention(server_args=args) cfg, lc = ModelConfig.from_server_args(args), LoadConfig(load_format="dummy") init_layer_runtime(model_config=cfg) initialize_moe_config() initialize_fp8_gemm_config() with set_default_torch_dtype(cfg.dtype), torch.device("cuda"): model = _initialize_model(cfg, lc, _get_quantization_config(cfg, lc)) model.load_weights([(f"{prefix}.{names[0]}", torch.tensor(0.25)), (f"{prefix}.{names[1]}", torch.tensor(0.0625))]) DefaultModelLoader.postprocess_weights(model, torch.device("cuda")) layer = re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)", prefix).group(1) for n, m in model.named_modules(): if isinstance(m, RadixAttention) and f"layers.{layer}." in n: method = type(m.quant_method).__name__ if m.quant_method is not None else None print(f"{type(model).__name__} {fmt}: {n} quant_method={method} k_scale={m.k_scale_float} v_scale={m.v_scale_float}") ```
`cases.txt` (model, attention module of layer 0 or 3, config overrides that shrink the model): ``` Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat|model.layers.0.self_attn|{"num_hidden_layers": 2, "num_experts": 8, "num_experts_per_tok": 2} arcee-ai/Trinity-Nano-Preview|model.layers.0.self_attn|{"num_hidden_layers": 2, "num_experts": 8, "num_experts_per_tok": 2} Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct|model.layers.0.self_attn|{"text_config": {"num_hidden_layers": 2}} google/gemma-3n-E2B-it|model.language_model.layers.0.self_attn|{} inclusionAI/Ring-2.5-1T|model.layers.0.attention|{"num_hidden_layers": 8, "num_experts": 8, "num_experts_per_tok": 2, "n_group": 1, "topk_group": 1} trl-internal-testing/tiny-DbrxForCausalLM|transformer.blocks.0.norm_attn_norm.attn|{"ffn_config": {"moe_num_experts": 8}} Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.2-3B|model.layers.0.self_attn|{"num_hidden_layers": 2} Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct|model.layers.3.self_attn|{"num_hidden_layers": 4, "num_experts": 8, "num_experts_per_tok": 2} ``` On main `91fd675`: ``` $ while IFS='|' read -r repo attn ov; do for f in ct modelopt; do python repro.py "$repo" $f "$attn" "$ov" 2>&1 | grep -E 'quant_method=|^[A-Za-z]+Error' done; done < cases.txt Qwen2MoeForCausalLM ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 Qwen2MoeForCausalLM modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 AfmoeForCausalLM ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 AfmoeForCausalLM modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 KeyError: 'language_model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale' BailingMoeV2_5ForCausalLM ct: model.layers.0.attention.attn quant_method=CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 issue.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 sparse attention layers drop checkpoint FP8 KV-cache scales and run with scale 1.0
issue.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py (trimmed) ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.14.0+cu130 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 12:30:59) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H20-3e ... GPU 7: NVIDIA H20-3e Nvidia driver version : 570.133.20 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.3 [pip3] torch==2.14.0 [pip3] transformers==5.22.1 [pip3] triton==3.8.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.33.0rc1.dev931+g5a92788a1 (git sha: 5a92788a1) ```
The Python sources were those of main `f358f0578` (2026-11-06) on top of that nightly wheel; the files involved are the same in both and on main `3012587f0`. ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary** `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention` (`vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py`) writes and reads its own KV cache. Its sparse attention reader (`sparse_attention_msa.py:389-407`, `552-583`) and its SM100 fused NVFP4 insert (`model.py:1136-1137`) take the scales from the layer's `_k_scale` / `_k_scale_float` / `_v_scale` / `_v_scale_float`, like `Attention` does. But the layer only calls `set_default_quant_scales(self, register_buffer=True)` (`model.py:1000`): it gets no KV-cache quantization method and no `k_scale` / `v_scale` parameters. So checkpoint KV-cache scales of the sparse layers are never loaded. `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` (`model.py:1789`) drops them with a one-time warning, and with an FP8 KV cache every sparse layer stores and reads K and V with scale 1.0. The dense attention layers of the same checkpoint (layers 0-2, plain `Attention`) do use their stored scales. **Checkpoint** `juspay/MiniMax-M3-FP8` (ModelOpt FP8, `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration`) stores per-layer `self_attn.k_proj.k_scale` / `self_attn.v_proj.v_scale` (F32 scalars). In the shards I read (layers 0-5), all are different from 1.0, for example sparse layer 3: k 0.023438, v 0.005441; dense layer 0: k 0.019252, v 0.005371. Its config does not set `kv_cache_quant_algo`, so the scales are used when FP8 KV cache is requested with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. **Reproduction** Only `config.json` of `juspay/MiniMax-M3-FP8` is downloaded; weights are dummy, with 4 layers (0-2 dense, 3 sparse) and 8 experts. ```python import torch from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config from vllm.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs from vllm.model_executor.model_loader import get_model_loader from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import init_workspace_manager def shrink(config): if getattr(config, "model_type", None) == "minimax_m3_vl": config.text_config.num_hidden_layers = 4 config.text_config.num_local_experts = 8 return config vllm_config = EngineArgs( model="juspay/MiniMax-M3-FP8", hf_overrides=shrink, kv_cache_dtype="fp8", load_format="dummy", skip_tokenizer_init=True, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=1024, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0, "video": 0}, ).create_engine_config() with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config): init_distributed_environment( world_size=1, rank=0, local_rank=0, distributed_init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{get_open_port()}", backend="nccl", ) initialize_model_parallel(1, 1) init_workspace_manager(torch.device("cuda")) model = get_model_loader(vllm_config.load_config).load_model( vllm_config=vllm_config, model_config=vllm_config.model_config ) # Values as stored in juspay/MiniMax-M3-FP8 (rounded) model.load_weights( [ ("language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.k_scale", torch.tensor(0.019252)), ("language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.v_proj.v_scale", torch.tensor(0.005371)), ("language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.k_proj.k_scale", torch.tensor(0.023438)), ("language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.v_proj.v_scale", torch.tensor(0.005441)), ] ) for name in ( "language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.attn", "language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn", ): layer = model.get_submodule(name) method = getattr(layer, "quant_method", None) if method is not None: method.process_weights_after_loading(layer) print( f"{name}: {type(layer).__name__}, quant method {type(method).__name__}, " f"k_scale {layer._k_scale_float:.6f}, v_scale {layer._v_scale_float:.6f}" ) ``` Output (relevant lines): ```text WARNING ... [weight_utils.py:1860] Found k_scale in the checkpoint (e.g. layers.3.self_attn.attn.k_scale), but not found the expected name in the model (e.g. layers.3.self_attn.attn.attn.k_scale). k_scale is not loaded. language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.attn: Attention, quant method ModelOptKVCacheMethod, k_scale 0.019287, v_scale 0.005371 language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn: MiniMaxM3SparseAttention, quant method NoneType, k_scale 1.000000, v_scale 1.000000 ``` The same happens with `MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM` and with compressed-tensors names (`self_attn.k_scale`, `kv_cache_scheme` FP8). **Expected**: layer 3 uses its stored k 0.023438 and v 0.005441, as layer 0 uses its own scales. **Why loading the scales alone is not enough** The sparse layers' FP8 cache writer always uses scale 1.0. On every path except the SM100 fused QKV epilogue (which is used only with an NVFP4 KV cache), the layer writes K/V with `ops.fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert` (`model.py:1214`), which takes no FP8 k/v scale: `csrc/fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu:214-240` stores FP8 "with identity scale" (`scaled_convert(..., 1.0f)`). The reader, however, dequantizes with the layer's `_k_scale_float` / `_v_scale_float` (`sparse_attention_msa.py:389-407`, `552-583`). Today both sides use 1.0, so the FP8 cache is consistent but unscaled. I tried the Python side only: initializing the layer with `_init_kv_cache_quant(self, quant_config, prefix)` instead of `set_default_quant_scales` (on top of #65950) and mapping `...self_attn.attn.k_scale` to `...self_attn.k_scale` in `load_weights`. The repro above then prints `k_scale 0.023438, v_scale 0.005432` for layer 3, but the insert kernel still writes with 1.0, so the reader would rescale unscaled values by 0.023 and 0.0054. A fix therefore needs the insert kernel to take the FP8 k/v scales (as `reshape_and_cache_flash` does) together with that loader change. **Not covered by #65950** #65946 / #65950 make the compressed-tensors and ModelOpt configs return a KV-cache method for any `AttentionLayerBase`, not only `Attention`. `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention` is an `AttentionLayerBase` but never asks for that method, so with #65950 applied the output above is the same. **Related code with the same setup** The AMD MiniMax-M3 model (`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:851`) and the Qwen4Exp QSA layers (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/{nvidia,amd}/qsa.py`) also only call `set_default_quant_scales`; I have not checked their cache writers. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [ ] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issue.title: [Bug]: LFM2, LFM2-MoE, Jamba, Zamba2, Step3, Bailing MoE and PLaMo3 build `Attention` without `quant_config`, so checkpoints with static FP8 KV-cache scales fail to load
issue.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py (trimmed) ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.14.0+cu130 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 12:30:59) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H20-3e ... GPU 7: NVIDIA H20-3e Nvidia driver version : 570.133.20 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.3 [pip3] torch==2.14.0 [pip3] transformers==5.22.1 [pip3] triton==3.8.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.33.0rc1.dev931+g5a92788a1 (git sha: 5a92788a1) ``` `compressed-tensors==0.17.0`.
The Python sources were those of main `f358f0578` (2026-11-06) on top of that nightly wheel; the model files involved are the same in both. ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary** Several model files build their `Attention` layer without passing `quant_config`: | model file | line on main | architectures | |---|---|---| | `lfm2.py` | 165 | `Lfm2ForCausalLM`, `Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration` | | `lfm2_moe.py` | 234 | `Lfm2MoeForCausalLM` | | `jamba.py` | 231 | `JambaForCausalLM` | | `zamba2.py` | 195 | `Zamba2ForCausalLM` | | `step3_text.py` | 201 | `Step3TextForCausalLM`, `Step3VLForConditionalGeneration` | | `bailing_moe.py` | 147 | `BailingMoeForCausalLM` | | `plamo3.py` | 199 | `Plamo3ForCausalLM` | The attention layer then gets no KV-cache quantization method and has no `k_scale` / `v_scale` parameters. A checkpoint that stores static FP8 KV-cache scales (compressed-tensors `kv_cache_scheme`, or ModelOpt `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8`) cannot be loaded, whatever `--kv-cache-dtype` is set to (PLaMo3 loads it and drops the scales): ```text ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'layers.2.self_attn.attn.k_scale' in Lfm2MoeModel. The available parameters belonging to layers.2.self_attn.attn (Attention) are: set() ``` This affects a public checkpoint: `CoolJohn-AI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-NVFP4-AutoRound` (`Lfm2MoeForCausalLM`, compressed-tensors, static FP8 `kv_cache_scheme`). Its safetensors headers have 20 KV-cache scales, `model.layers.{2,6,10,...,38}.self_attn.{k,v}_scale` (F32, shape `[1]`), none of them 1.0 (for example layer 2: k 0.019671, v 0.000279). **Reproduction** Only `config.json` of `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B` is downloaded; weights are dummy. The k/v scales use the names and values of the checkpoint above. ```python import torch from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config from vllm.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention import Attention from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.utils import initialize_model from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype vllm_config = EngineArgs( model="LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B", hf_overrides={ "num_hidden_layers": 3, "layer_types": ["conv", "conv", "full_attention"], "num_experts": 8, "quantization_config": { "quant_method": "compressed-tensors", "format": "dense", "config_groups": {}, "kv_cache_scheme": { "num_bits": 8, "type": "float", "strategy": "tensor", "dynamic": False, "symmetric": True, }, }, }, kv_cache_dtype="fp8", load_format="dummy", skip_tokenizer_init=True, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=1024, ).create_engine_config() with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config): init_distributed_environment( world_size=1, rank=0, local_rank=0, distributed_init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{get_open_port()}", backend="nccl", ) initialize_model_parallel(1, 1) with set_default_torch_dtype(vllm_config.model_config.dtype), torch.device("cuda"): model = initialize_model(vllm_config=vllm_config) attn = model.model.layers[2].self_attn.attn print("attention quant method:", type(getattr(attn, "quant_method", None)).__name__) # Names and values as stored in CoolJohn-AI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-NVFP4-AutoRound model.load_weights( [ ("model.layers.2.self_attn.k_scale", torch.tensor([0.019671])), ("model.layers.2.self_attn.v_scale", torch.tensor([0.000279])), ] ) attn.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(attn) print("k_scale / v_scale used by attention:", attn._k_scale_float, attn._v_scale_float) ``` Output: ```text attention quant method: NoneType ... ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'layers.2.self_attn.attn.k_scale' in Lfm2MoeModel. The available parameters belonging to layers.2.self_attn.attn (Attention) are: set() ``` **Expected**: the attention layer gets `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod`, and attention uses `k_scale = 0.019671`, `v_scale = 0.000279`. **Other architectures** The same check with each model's public `config.json` (shrunk, dummy weights) and k/v scales named as each format writes them: | model | compressed-tensors names | ModelOpt names | |---|---|---| | LFM2, LFM2-VL, LFM2-MoE | `ValueError` as above | `ValueError` as above | | Jamba | `ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'model.layers.4.k_scale' in JambaForCausalLM` | `AttributeError: 'QKVParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'data'` | | Zamba2 | `ValueError: ... 'model.layers.5.shared_transformer.self_attn.k_scale' in Zamba2ForCausalLM` | `AttributeError: 'QKVParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'data'` | | Step3 text and Step3-VL | `KeyError: 'layers.0.self_attn.k_scale'` | `KeyError: 'layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.k_scale'` | | Bailing MoE | `ValueError: ... 'layers.0.attention.attn.k_scale' in BailingMoeModel` | not tested | | PLaMo3 | no error; the scales are dropped and attention uses 1.0 | ``AttributeError: QKVParallelLinear has no attribute `attn` `` (a separate name-mapping gap for the fused `mixer.qkv_proj`) | LFM2 and LFM2-VL used `LiquidAI/LFM2-1.2B` and `LiquidAI/LFM2-VL-450M`, LFM2-MoE `LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B`, Jamba `ai21labs/Jamba-tiny-dev`, Zamba2 `Zyphra/Zamba2-1.2B`, Step3 `stepfun-ai/step3` and Bailing `inclusionAI/Ling-lite-1.5`. The PLaMo3 configs are gated, so PLaMo3 used a small hand-written config. Configs that need remote code were read as plain `PretrainedConfig` data; no remote code was run. **Root cause** `Attention.__init__` creates the KV-cache quantization method, and with it the `k_scale` / `v_scale` parameters, from the `quant_config` it is given. These model files have `quant_config` at hand (they pass it to the linear layers) but do not pass it to `Attention`. Jamba, Zamba2 and Step3 also keep no `quant_config` attribute on the model, so `AutoWeightsLoader` does not apply the KV-cache scale name mapper there (hence the different errors above). Zamba2 has one more detail: hybrid layers share an attention block, and the checkpoint stores one set of scales per block, while vLLM builds one `Attention` per hybrid layer. **Suggested fix** Pass `quant_config=quant_config` to these `Attention(...)` calls, set `self.quant_config` on the Jamba, Zamba2 and Step3 models, and let Zamba2 give a shared block's scales to each of its attention layers. I have a patch with a regression test and can open a PR. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [ ] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issue.title: [Bug] NVFP4 Marlin path (default on SM80-SM90) decodes E4M3 subnormal block scales as 0 with bfloat16 activations
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On SM80 to SM9x GPUs (A100, L40S, H100, H200, H20, ...), SGLang serves NVFP4 linear layers through the FP4 Marlin path by default (`initialize_fp4_gemm_config` picks `marlin` there), and NVFP4 MoE layers through the Marlin fallback. `nvfp4_marlin_process_scales` stores each E4M3 block scale as an S0E5M3 byte (scale * 2^7, 5-bit exponent with bias 15). With bfloat16 activations, `dequant_fp8_scales<nv_bfloat162, kFE4M3fn>` in `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/gemm/marlin/dequant.h` builds the bfloat16 exponent from the top bit of that byte. That is right only when the top bit is 1, i.e. for block scales of 2^-6 or more. Every smaller scale, i.e. every E4M3 subnormal (2^-9 to 7 * 2^-9), decodes to about 2^-112 of its value, so the 16 weights of its block become 0. With float16 activations the same bytes decode exactly.

E4M3 subnormal block scales occur in real checkpoints:

- in normalized ModelOpt exports, in tensors whose largest block scale is near 448. nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-NVFP4 has 165,266 of them, in five tensors whose largest block scales are 320 to 448: 162,143 in `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj` (of its 4,194,304 block scales; its largest is 352), 749 in `k_proj`, and 2,374 in `mlp.gate_proj` and `mlp.up_proj` of layers 0 and 33. They hold 2,236,146 nonzero weights; in layer 0's fused qkv projection they touch 5,409 of its 10,240 output rows.
- in checkpoints exported with a global scale of 1, where many block scales are small. This is the case of #44998.

Served through the offline `Engine` (H20, bfloat16 activations, default settings except `mem_fraction_static=0.4`, so the KV cache is FP8 as the checkpoint asks), nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-NVFP4 has a WikiText-2 perplexity of 3.5664 over 16,376 positions. A copy of the checkpoint whose subnormal block scales are set to 0 gives the same per-token log-probabilities, so SGLang drops exactly these blocks. With the kernel fixed to decode them, perplexity is 3.5558 and the next-token prediction changes at 3.35% of positions. GSM8K (5-shot, 1,319 questions) moves from 93.2% to 92.9%, so on this model the dropped weights do not cost accuracy; the problem is that the kernel computes with different weights from the ones the checkpoint stores, and checkpoints with small block scales (`--small` below, #44998) lose most of their weights.

The vLLM rescale that #45031 ports does not help the first case: when a layer's largest block scale is above 224, the rescale factor is 1, so its subnormal scales stay below 2^-6. #45031 also sets every scale below 2^-6 to zero for float16, which decodes them exactly today.

vLLM has the same bfloat16 decode and sets these scales to zero on the host for both activation dtypes; vllm-project/vllm#66109 reports the float16 part.

### Reproduction

The script below runs one 256 x 4096 NVFP4 layer through the two functions `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod` uses on these GPUs, `prepare_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin` and `apply_fp4_marlin_linear`, with rows of 6 * identity as input, so the output is the weight matrix the kernel uses. Weights are the E2M1 values 0.5 to 6. On an H20 with SGLang 0.5.23 (main 2fd45ed82 gives the same):

| block scales | activations | weights decoded wrongly, of 1,048,576 |
|---|---|---|
| all 448; row 0 has blocks 2^-6, 2^-7, 2^-9, 7 * 2^-9 | bfloat16 | 48: the three subnormal blocks are 0 |
| same | float16 | 0 |
| all between 2^-9 and 2^-4 (`--small`) | bfloat16 | 524,304: every block below 2^-6 is 0 |
| same | float16 | 0 |

```
python repro_sglang_marlin_nvfp4_small_scales.py --dtype bfloat16
python repro_sglang_marlin_nvfp4_small_scales.py --small --dtype bfloat16
```

<details>
<summary>repro_sglang_marlin_nvfp4_small_scales.py</summary>

```python
"""SGLang: NVFP4 block scales below 2^-6 through the FP4 Marlin path that SGLang uses for NVFP4 linear layers
on SM80-SM99 (fp4_utils.initialize_fp4_gemm_config picks "marlin" there: A100, L40S, H100, H200, H20, ...).

Calls the two functions ModelOptFp4LinearMethod runs on those GPUs, prepare_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin (weight
preparation) and apply_fp4_marlin_linear (the GEMM), on one 256 x 4096 layer. Same layers as the vLLM repro:
default: every E4M3 block scale 448 except five blocks of row 0: 448, 2^-6, 2^-7, 2^-9, 7 * 2^-9.
--small: every scale small (2^-4 .. 2^-9), as in checkpoints whose E4M3 scales do not use the top of the range.
Weights are the positive E2M1 values 0.5..6 cycled, weight_scale_2 = 2^-4; the input is rows of 6 * identity,
so the output is 6 x the weight matrix the kernel uses, compared with 6 x E2M1 value x block scale x 2^-4.

    python repro_sglang_marlin_nvfp4_small_scales.py [--small] [--dtype bfloat16|float16]
"""
import argparse
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch

from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.marlin_utils_fp4 import apply_fp4_marlin_linear, prepare_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--small", action="store_true")
ap.add_argument("--dtype", default="bfloat16", choices=["bfloat16", "float16"])
args = ap.parse_args()
dtype = getattr(torch, args.dtype)
E2M1 = torch.tensor([0, .5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, -0., -.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -3, -4, -6])
N, K, G = 256, 4096, 16
torch.cuda.set_device(0)

codes = (torch.arange(N)[:, None] + torch.arange(K)[None, :]) % 7 + 1
if args.small:
    e = (torch.arange(N)[:, None] + torch.arange(K // G)[None, :]) % 6 + 4
    scales = torch.exp2(-e.float())
else:
    scales = torch.full((N, K // G), 448.0)
    scales[0, 1:5] = torch.tensor([2.0 ** -6, 2.0 ** -7, 2.0 ** -9, 7 * 2.0 ** -9])
scales = scales.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
gscale = 2.0 ** -4
packed = (codes[:, 0::2] | (codes[:, 1::2] << 4)).to(torch.uint8)

layer = torch.nn.Module()
layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(packed.cuda(), requires_grad=False)
layer.weight_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(scales.cuda(), requires_grad=False)
layer.weight_global_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(gscale, device="cuda"), requires_grad=False)
layer.output_size_per_partition, layer.input_size_per_partition = N, K
layer.params_dtype = dtype
layer.quant_config = SimpleNamespace(group_size=G)
prepare_nvfp4_layer_for_marlin(layer)

with torch.inference_mode():
    eye = 6 * torch.eye(K, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
    out = torch.cat([apply_fp4_marlin_linear(eye[r:r + 256], layer.weight, layer.weight_scale,
                                             layer.weight_global_scale, layer.workspace, N, K)
                     for r in range(0, K, 256)])
out = out.float().cpu().T
sc = scales.float()
ref = 6 * E2M1[codes] * sc.repeat_interleave(G, dim=1) * gscale

import sglang  # noqa: E402

print(f"sglang {sglang.__version__}, activations {args.dtype}, GPU {torch.cuda.get_device_name()}")
for blk in range(5):
    cols = slice(blk * G, blk * G + 7)
    s = float(sc[0, blk])
    print(f"row 0, block {blk} (scale {s:.6g}): expected {[round(x, 4) for x in (ref[0, cols] / s).tolist()]}"
          f"  got {[float(f'{x:.4g}') for x in (out[0, cols] / s).tolist()]}  (x scale)")
wrong = out != ref
tiny = wrong & (out.abs() < ref.abs() * 2.0 ** -100)
print(f"weights decoded differently from the checkpoint: {int(wrong.sum())} of {N * K} "
      f"({int((wrong & (out == 0)).sum())} as 0, {int(tiny.sum())} as less than 2^-100 of their value)")
for v in sorted(set(sc.flatten().tolist())):
    m = (sc == v).repeat_interleave(G, dim=1)
    print(f"  blocks with scale {v:.6g}: {int((wrong & m).sum())} of {int(m.sum())} weights wrong")
```

</details>

### Environment

issue.title: [Bug] Qwen3, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3-Omni-MoE, Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3 rerankers ignore checkpoint FP8 KV-cache scales
issue.body:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug With a checkpoint that declares a static FP8 KV cache (compressed-tensors `kv_cache_scheme`, or ModelOpt `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8`) and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, the Qwen3 family drops the per-layer `k_scale`/`v_scale` tensors, and the FP8 KV cache runs with a scale of 1.0. There are two causes. 1. `Qwen3Attention` builds `RadixAttention` without `quant_config` ([qwen3.py#L259](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py#L259)), so attention has no KV-cache method and no `k_scale`/`v_scale` parameters. Every model built on it is affected: `Qwen3ForCausalLM`, `Qwen3Model` (embedding), `Qwen3ForRewardModel`, `Qwen3ForSequenceClassification`, Qwen3-VL (and Cosmos3, which uses its loader), Qwen3-ASR and LightOnOCR. #46527 adds the argument. 2. With the argument, several loaders still drop the scale names. These have no rule for KV-scale names: [qwen3_classification.py#L77](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_classification.py#L77) (`Qwen3ForSequenceClassification`, `Qwen3ForRewardModel`), [qwen3_vl.py#L1702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1702) (Qwen3-VL, Cosmos3) and [qwen3_asr.py#L126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_asr.py#L126). The compressed-tensors name `.k_scale` is skipped as unknown, and the ModelOpt name `.k_proj.k_scale` is renamed to `qkv_proj.k_scale` by the stacked mapping and then skipped. Qwen3-VL-MoE and Qwen3-Omni-MoE also list `.k_scale`/`.v_scale` in the suffixes they skip ([qwen3_vl_moe.py#L235](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl_moe.py#L235), [qwen3_omni_moe.py#L580](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/91fd6756e773ab857d5f6ddf3876fead1992b29b/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_omni_moe.py#L580)); their attention is `Qwen3MoeAttention`, which gets the argument in #48750 (#48749). `Qwen3ForCausalLM`, `Qwen3Model` and LightOnOCR (which passes its language-model weights to `Qwen3ForCausalLM`) already call `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name`, so for them the argument from #46527 is enough. The causal LM, embedding and classification loaders log a warning per dropped name; the Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3-Omni-MoE, Qwen3-ASR and Cosmos3 loaders log nothing. v0.5.23 has the same code. The Qwen3-MoE causal loader also has no rule; that part is in #39942 / #39943. ### Reproduction `repro.py` uses one GPU and dummy weights, and only reads `config.json` of the given model. It declares a static FP8 KV cache in the format's own config, loads two scales for layer 0 under the names that format uses, runs the post-load step, and prints layer 0's attention.
repro.py ```python # usage: python repro.py [''] import json import sys import torch from sglang.srt.configs.load_config import LoadConfig from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig from sglang.srt.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel from sglang.srt.distributed.bootstrap import init_layer_runtime from sglang.srt.layers.dp_attention import initialize_dp_attention from sglang.srt.layers.moe import initialize_moe_config from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import initialize_fp8_gemm_config from sglang.srt.layers.radix_attention import RadixAttention from sglang.srt.model_loader.loader import DefaultModelLoader, _get_quantization_config, _initialize_model from sglang.srt.model_loader.utils import set_default_torch_dtype from sglang.srt.runtime_context import SpawnRanks, publish from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs repo, fmt, prefix = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] ov = json.loads(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else {} ov["quantization_config"] = { # a static FP8 KV cache, in each format's own config "ct": {"quant_method": "compressed-tensors", "config_groups": {}, "kv_cache_scheme": {"num_bits": 8, "type": "float", "strategy": "tensor", "dynamic": False, "symmetric": True}}, "modelopt": {"quant_method": "modelopt", "quant_algo": "FP8", "kv_cache_quant_algo": "FP8", "exclude_modules": ["lm_head"]}, }[fmt] # per-layer KV-cache scales of layer 0, named the way each tool exports them names = {"ct": ("self_attn.k_scale", "self_attn.v_scale"), "modelopt": ("self_attn.k_proj.k_scale", "self_attn.v_proj.v_scale")}[fmt] args = ServerArgs(model_path=repo, load_format="dummy", kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3", json_model_override_args=json.dumps(ov)) publish(args, role="scheduler", ranks=SpawnRanks(world_rank=0, gpu_id=0)) torch.cuda.set_device(0) init_distributed_environment(world_size=1, rank=0, local_rank=0, distributed_init_method="tcp://127.0.0.1:29571") initialize_model_parallel() initialize_dp_attention(server_args=args) cfg, lc = ModelConfig.from_server_args(args), LoadConfig(load_format="dummy") init_layer_runtime(model_config=cfg) initialize_moe_config() initialize_fp8_gemm_config() with set_default_torch_dtype(cfg.dtype), torch.device("cuda"): model = _initialize_model(cfg, lc, _get_quantization_config(cfg, lc)) model.load_weights([(f"{prefix}.{names[0]}", torch.tensor(0.25)), (f"{prefix}.{names[1]}", torch.tensor(0.0625))]) DefaultModelLoader.postprocess_weights(model, torch.device("cuda")) attn = [(n, m) for n, m in model.named_modules() if isinstance(m, RadixAttention) and m.layer_id == 0][0] method = type(attn[1].quant_method).__name__ if attn[1].quant_method is not None else None print(f"{type(model).__name__} {fmt}: {attn[0]} quant_method={method} k_scale={attn[1].k_scale_float} v_scale={attn[1].v_scale_float}") ```
On main `91fd675`: ``` $ for f in ct modelopt; do python repro.py Qwen/Qwen3-8B $f model.layers.0 '{"num_hidden_layers": 2}' python repro.py tomaarsen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-seq-cls $f model.layers.0 '{"num_hidden_layers": 2}' python repro.py Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct $f model.language_model.layers.0 '{"text_config": {"num_hidden_layers": 2}}' python repro.py Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct $f model.language_model.layers.0 '{"text_config": {"num_hidden_layers": 2, "num_experts": 8, "num_experts_per_tok": 2}}' done Qwen3ForCausalLM ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None Qwen3ForSequenceClassification ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None Qwen3ForCausalLM modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None Qwen3ForSequenceClassification modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=None k_scale=None v_scale=None ``` With #46527 and #48750 applied, `Qwen3ForCausalLM` prints `k_scale=0.25 v_scale=0.0625` for both formats, and the other three print the KV-cache method with `k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0`: ``` Qwen3ForCausalLM ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod k_scale=0.25 v_scale=0.0625 Qwen3ForSequenceClassification ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration ct: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 Qwen3ForCausalLM modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod k_scale=0.25 v_scale=0.0625 Qwen3ForSequenceClassification modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration modelopt: model.layers.0.self_attn.attn quant_method=ModelOptFp8KVCacheMethod k_scale=1.0 v_scale=1.0 ``` ### Environment
python3 -m sglang.check_env (trimmed) ``` Python: 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 12:30:59) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H20-3e GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 570.133.20 PyTorch: 2.14.1+cu130 sglang: 0.5.23 sglang-kernel: 0.4.10 flashinfer_python: 0.7.2 triton: 3.8.0 transformers: 5.19.0 huggingface_hub: 1.33.0 Hypervisor vendor:: KVM ```
Main `91fd675` was run from source in the same environment.

comment.diff_hunk:
@@ -607,6 +607,7 @@ async def update_weights(self, global_steps: int = None):
         # 0. update weights for sync training with colocated actor and rollout
         if self.backend == "naive":
             await asyncio.gather(*self.actor_wg.update_weights(global_steps=global_steps, mode=self.backend))
+            await self.resume_generation_replicas()
comment.body:
Agreed, fixed in b0e5f80a, but in `update_weights` rather than `switch_to_rollout`. The second resume came from this PR's naive `update_weights` path, which had started resuming the replicas itself. Every other naive caller (`switch_to_rollout`, colocate-async `on_step_end`, the fully-async hybrid switch and `DynamicResourceController`) already resumes right after `update_weights`, so dropping only the `switch_to_rollout` call would have left those resuming twice.

The naive path no longer resumes, so callers own the resume again, as on main. The sync trainer, whose `on_sample_end` this PR made abort the replicas, now resumes in `on_step_end` after its update, like the colocate-async trainer. `tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_weight_switch_resume_on_cpu.py` runs the real naive manager and counts `resume_generation()` per replica: once for the sync step, the colocate-async step and `switch_to_rollout(already_registered=True)`, and none inside `update_weights`. On the previous head, the hybrid and colocate paths resumed twice.

issue.title: [Bug]: Ministral-3 / Devstral-Small-2 FP8 with `--config-format hf`: vision tower and projector are built as FP8 and image embeddings are all zeros
issue.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py (trimmed) ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.14.0+cu130 CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 12:30:59) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA H20-3e ... GPU 7: NVIDIA H20-3e Nvidia driver version : 570.133.20 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.7.3 [pip3] torch==2.14.0 [pip3] transformers==5.22.1 [pip3] triton==3.8.0 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.33.0rc1.dev931+g5a92788a1 (git sha: 5a92788a1) ```
The Python sources were those of main `86564975c` (2026-11-06) on top of that nightly wheel; the files involved are the same in both. ### 🐛 Describe the bug **Summary** The FP8 checkpoints `mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512`, `-8B-`, `-14B-Instruct-2512` and `mistralai/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512` store the vision tower and the multimodal projector in BF16. Their `config.json` says so with whole module names: ```json "quantization_config": { "activation_scheme": "static", "modules_to_not_convert": ["model.vision_tower", "model.multi_modal_projector", "lm_head"], "quant_method": "fp8", "weight_block_size": null } ``` When vLLM reads the HF config (`--config-format hf`, for example `--config-format hf --load-format safetensors --tokenizer-mode hf`, or any copy of these models without `params.json`), `Fp8Config` ignores these entries. Every linear layer of the vision tower and the projector is built with `Fp8LinearMethod`, the BF16 checkpoint weights are loaded into FP8 parameters, and their `weight_scale` is never loaded. The model loads with no error, text prompts work, and the image embeddings are all zeros. The default Mistral-format path (`params.json`) is not affected. **Reproduction** Only `config.json` is downloaded; weights are dummy, with one text and one vision layer. ```python from vllm.config import set_current_vllm_config from vllm.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import LinearBase from vllm.model_executor.model_loader import get_model_loader from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port vllm_config = EngineArgs( model="mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512", config_format="hf", load_format="dummy", skip_tokenizer_init=True, enforce_eager=True, max_model_len=1024, hf_overrides={ "text_config": {"num_hidden_layers": 1}, "vision_config": {"num_hidden_layers": 1}, }, ).create_engine_config() with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config): init_distributed_environment( world_size=1, rank=0, local_rank=0, distributed_init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{get_open_port()}", backend="nccl", ) initialize_model_parallel(1, 1) model = get_model_loader(vllm_config.load_config).load_model( vllm_config=vllm_config, model_config=vllm_config.model_config ) print("modules_to_not_convert after mapping:", vllm_config.quant_config.ignored_layers) counts: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {} for name, module in model.named_modules(): if isinstance(module, LinearBase): key = (name.split(".")[0], type(module.quant_method).__name__) counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1 for (part, method), n in sorted(counts.items()): print(f"{part:22s} {method:24s} {n} linear layers") ``` Output: ```text modules_to_not_convert after mapping: ['language_model.model.vision_tower', 'language_model.model.multi_modal_projector', 'lm_head', 'language_model.model.vision_tower', 'language_model.model.multi_modal_projector', 'lm_head'] language_model Fp8LinearMethod 4 linear layers multi_modal_projector Fp8LinearMethod 2 linear layers vision_tower Fp8LinearMethod 4 linear layers ``` The 8B, 14B and Devstral-Small-2 configs give the same result. **Expected**: the vision tower and projector use `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, and only the language model uses `Fp8LinearMethod`. **Effect on outputs** - With the real `mistralai/Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512` on vLLM 0.33.0 (same code in these paths), served with `--config-format hf --load-format safetensors --tokenizer-mode hf` and asked "Describe this image." about a photo of two elephants, the model answers "I currently cannot view or analyze images directly. ...". Served the default way (Mistral format), it describes the two elephants. - On a small synthetic checkpoint with the same layout (BF16 vision tower and projector, FP8 language model, the same `modules_to_not_convert`), the image embeddings from `embed_multimodal` are all zeros, while transformers gives values up to 0.057 for the same weights and image. **Root cause** 1. `Fp8Config.apply_vllm_mapper` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py:150-152`) maps each entry through the model's rename mapper. The prefix rules of `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration.hf_to_vllm_mapper` end with a dot (`"model.vision_tower.": "vision_tower."`, `mistral3.py:462`), so the bare module name `model.vision_tower` does not match them and falls through to the catch-all `"model.": "language_model.model."` (`mistral3.py:467`). Most multimodal models in vLLM use dotted prefix keys like these. 2. `Fp8Config` matches ignore entries exactly (`ignored_layers_match_mode = "exact"`, `fp8.py:115`; `prefix in ignored_layers`, `quant_utils.py:641-642`). So even a correctly mapped `vision_tower` would not match `vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.attention.qkv_proj`. transformers treats an entry of `modules_to_not_convert` as the module and every layer inside it (`should_convert_module` in `transformers/quantizers/quantizers_utils.py`). Some models already work around this locally: `bailing_moe_v3_vl.py` uses prefix keys without the dot ("Match module names as well as parameter names for quantization") and passes `quant_config=None` to a tower listed in `ignored_layers`. Checkpoints that list every layer by full name, such as Qwen's FP8 exports, are not affected. Open PR #44628 proposes substring matching for the FP8 configs. That would cover point 2 but not point 1: the mapped entry `language_model.model.vision_tower` is not a substring of `vision_tower.transformer.layers.0.attention.qkv_proj`. **Suggested fix** In `Fp8Config`, also map each entry as a module prefix (`name + "."`), and treat an ignored module as covering every layer inside it, as transformers does. I have a patch with a regression test and can open a PR. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [ ] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

### 🐛 Describe the bug `nvfp4_marlin_process_scales` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/marlin_utils_fp4.py` turns the E4M3 block scales into the S0E5M3 bytes the Marlin kernel reads. It rescales them by a power of two (except for float16 activations), multiplies them by 2^7 and, since #37502, sets every value below 2 to zero: ```python marlin_scales = marlin_scales * (2**7) marlin_scales[marlin_scales < 2] = 0 ``` This drops every block scale below 2^-6 after the rescale, for both activation dtypes. E4M3 values below 2^-6 are exactly the E4M3 subnormals. - With bfloat16 activations these values cannot be represented: `dequant_fp8_scales` moves the top S0E5M3 bit to the top of the bfloat16 exponent, so a value below 2 would decode to about 2^-112 of itself. Dropping them is a limit of the format, but it happens without any message. - With float16 activations, `dequant_fp8_scales` reads the byte back as the top byte of a half, which holds these values exactly. The zeroing then drops weights the kernel could use: - E4M3 subnormal block scales (2^-9 to 7 * 2^-9), which ModelOpt exports contain in tensors whose largest block scale is near 448; - every block scale below 2^-6 in checkpoints whose block scales are not normalized to 448 (for example `weight_scale_2 = 1`), because no rescale is applied for float16. This is the case #34577 fixed for bfloat16. Turing GPUs, which have no bfloat16, always run this path with float16. **Repro.** One ModelOpt NVFP4 `ReplicatedLinear` (256 x 4096) is loaded through its weight loaders and `process_weights_after_loading` and fed rows of 6 * identity, so the output is the weight matrix the kernel uses. Weights are the E2M1 values 0.5 to 6. Results on vLLM 0.33.0 and on main 0eb619dc5 (identical): | block scales | activations | default kernel on SM90 (Humming) | Marlin | |---|---|---|---| | all 448; row 0 has blocks 2^-6, 2^-7, 2^-9, 7 * 2^-9 | bfloat16 | 0 weights wrong | 48 wrong: the three subnormal blocks are 0 | | same | float16 | 0 wrong | 48 wrong: the same three blocks are 0 | | all between 2^-9 and 2^-4 (`--small`) | bfloat16 | 0 wrong | 0 wrong (rescaled) | | same | float16 | 0 wrong | 524,304 of 1,048,576 weights are 0 (every block below 2^-6) | The block with scale 2^-6, the smallest normal E4M3 value, is kept in every case. **A real checkpoint.** nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-NVFP4 has 165,266 E4M3 subnormal block scales, in five tensors whose largest block scales are 320 to 448. 162,143 of them are in `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj` (of its 4,194,304 block scales; its largest is 352) and 749 in `k_proj`. Together they hold 2,200,141 nonzero weights of layer 0's fused qkv projection, in 5,409 of its 10,240 output rows. On SM75 to SM89 Marlin drops these weights by default (bfloat16), and also with `--dtype float16`. **Effect on this checkpoint**, served with vLLM 0.33.0, `--dtype float16 --kv-cache-dtype float16`, Marlin forced, 1x H20. WikiText-2 perplexity (raw test split, 8 windows of 2,048 tokens, 16,376 positions) is 3.5176 as is, and 3.5176 with identical per-token log-probabilities on a copy of the checkpoint whose subnormal block scales are set to 0, so Marlin drops exactly these blocks. Keeping them gives 3.5179 and changes the prediction at 0.09% of positions; GSM8K (5-shot, 1,319 questions) is 93.18% as is and 93.10% with them kept (93.25% on a second run as is). So on this model the dropped weights do not measurably change accuracy. The large loss is in checkpoints with small block scales, as in the `--small` row above. **Expected.** With float16 activations, keep these block scales, since the kernel decodes them. With bfloat16, where S0E5M3 cannot represent them, warn when nonzero scales are dropped.
repro_marlin_nvfp4_small_scales.py ```python """NVFP4 (ModelOpt) linear layer: block scales below 2^-6 are decoded as 0 by the Marlin NVFP4 kernel (MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel), the default NVFP4 linear kernel on SM75-SM89. Default layer (one 256 x 4096 layer, no padding): every E4M3 block scale is 448 (the largest E4M3 value; ModelOpt puts the largest block scales of a tensor near it) except five blocks of row 0: block 0: 448 block 1: 2^-6 (smallest normal E4M3) block 2: 2^-7 block 3: 2^-9 (smallest subnormal) block 4: 7 * 2^-9 (largest subnormal) --small: the same layer with every scale small, as in checkpoints whose E4M3 scales do not use the top of the E4M3 range (largest scale 2^-4): row r, block b has scale 2^-(4 + (r + b) % 6), i.e. 2^-4 .. 2^-9. Weights are the positive E2M1 values 0.5..6 cycled, weight_scale_2 = 2^-4 and input_scale = 1. The layer is fed rows of 6 * identity (exact under NVFP4 activation quantization too), so the output is 6 x the weight matrix the kernel actually uses, compared with 6 x E2M1 value x block scale x weight_scale_2. python repro_marlin_nvfp4_small_scales.py [--small] [--dtype bfloat16|float16] # default kernel python repro_marlin_nvfp4_small_scales.py [--small] [--dtype bfloat16|float16] --marlin # Marlin forced """ import argparse import os ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--marlin", action="store_true", help="disable Humming so the Marlin NVFP4 kernel is used") ap.add_argument("--small", action="store_true", help="all block scales between 2^-9 and 2^-4") ap.add_argument("--dtype", default="bfloat16", choices=["bfloat16", "float16"]) args = ap.parse_args() if args.marlin: os.environ["VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS"] = "HummingNvFp4LinearKernel" import torch # noqa: E402 from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config # noqa: E402 from vllm.distributed import ensure_model_parallel_initialized, init_distributed_environment # noqa: E402 from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import ReplicatedLinear # noqa: E402 from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.modelopt import ModelOptNvFp4Config # noqa: E402 dtype = getattr(torch, args.dtype) E2M1 = torch.tensor([0, .5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, -0., -.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -3, -4, -6]) N, K, G = 256, 4096, 16 quant = ModelOptNvFp4Config.from_config({"quantization": { "quant_algo": "NVFP4", "group_size": 16, "kv_cache_quant_algo": None, "exclude_modules": []}}) torch.cuda.set_device(0) vcfg = VllmConfig() with set_current_vllm_config(vcfg): init_distributed_environment(world_size=1, rank=0, local_rank=0, distributed_init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{os.environ.get('REPRO_PORT', 29513)}", backend="nccl") ensure_model_parallel_initialized(1, 1) with torch.device("cuda"): layer = ReplicatedLinear(K, N, bias=False, quant_config=quant, prefix="layer", params_dtype=dtype) # checkpoint tensors: E2M1 codes (low nibble = even k), E4M3 block scales, FP32 per-tensor scales codes = (torch.arange(N)[:, None] + torch.arange(K)[None, :]) % 7 + 1 # values 0.5 .. 6 if args.small: e = (torch.arange(N)[:, None] + torch.arange(K // G)[None, :]) % 6 + 4 scales = torch.exp2(-e.float()) else: scales = torch.full((N, K // G), 448.0) scales[0, 1:5] = torch.tensor([2.0 ** -6, 2.0 ** -7, 2.0 ** -9, 7 * 2.0 ** -9]) scales = scales.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) assert torch.equal(scales.float(), scales.float().to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float()) gscale = 2.0 ** -4 packed = (codes[:, 0::2] | (codes[:, 1::2] << 4)).to(torch.uint8) tensors = {"weight": packed, "weight_scale": scales, "weight_scale_2": torch.tensor([gscale]), "input_scale": torch.tensor([1.0])} for name, p in list(layer.named_parameters()): t = tensors.pop(name) p.weight_loader(p, t.to(p.dtype).cuda() if t.dtype == torch.float32 else t.cuda()) assert not tensors, f"unused checkpoint tensors: {list(tensors)}" with set_current_vllm_config(vcfg): layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer) with torch.inference_mode(): eye = 6 * torch.eye(K, dtype=dtype, device="cuda") out = torch.cat([layer(eye[r:r + 256])[0] for r in range(0, K, 256)]) # out[k, n] = 6 * weight(n, k) out = out.float().cpu().T sc = scales.float() ref = 6 * E2M1[codes] * sc.repeat_interleave(G, dim=1) * gscale kern = getattr(getattr(layer, "scheme", None), "kernel", None) or getattr(layer.quant_method, "kernel", None) print(f"activations {args.dtype}, kernel: {type(kern).__name__}") for blk in range(5): cols = slice(blk * G, blk * G + 7) s = float(sc[0, blk]) print(f"row 0, block {blk} (scale {s:.6g}): expected {[round(x, 4) for x in (ref[0, cols] / s).tolist()]}" f" got {[round(x, 4) for x in (out[0, cols] / s).tolist()]} (x scale)") wrong = out != ref print(f"weights decoded differently from the checkpoint: {int(wrong.sum())} of {N * K} " f"({int((wrong & (out == 0)).sum())} of them as 0)") for v in sorted(set(sc.flatten().tolist())): m = (sc == v).repeat_interleave(G, dim=1) print(f" blocks with scale {v:.6g}: {int((wrong & m).sum())} of {int(m.sum())} weights wrong") ``` ``` python repro_marlin_nvfp4_small_scales.py --dtype float16 --marlin python repro_marlin_nvfp4_small_scales.py --small --dtype float16 --marlin ```

issue.title: [vllm,sglang] feat: Support LoRA for DeepSeek V4 & DeepSeek V4.1 & GLM5.3 Flash
issue.body: ### What does this PR do? Depends on: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51368 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52552 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52626 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53361 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56327 - https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/pull/6044 - https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/pull/6199 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7054 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7521 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7522 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8018 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7763 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7762 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7500 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7501 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7502 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7503 - https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7678 Adds DeepSeek V4, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM5.3 Flash LoRA support to verl's vLLM weight-sync path. Previously a merge=False LoRA base sync orphaned the `.base_layer.` suffix on wrapped modules and mishandled the mxfp4 quant path, so DSV4 LoRA diverged from the actor. This reworks weight-name reconciliation to be runtime-probed (strict vs flat loader) instead of model-type-based, unwraps the LoRA-installed mxfp4 quant-method wrapper, and threads `peft_config` through the FP8/mxfp4 load path so the same reconciliation applies there. Tested with Megatron backend, GPU E2E (DSV4 merge=F GRPO, 2-node): step1/step2 pearson 0.9970/0.9950, aligned to run15 merge=T 0.9952/0.9944. ### Checklist Before Starting - [X] Search for similar PRs. Query: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=deepseek+v4+lora - [X] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI) - `{modules}` include `fsdp`, `megatron`, `veomni`, `sglang`, `vllm`, `rollout`, `trainer`, `ci`, `training_utils`, `recipe`, `hardware`, `deployment`, `ray`, `worker`, `single_controller`, `misc`, `perf`, `model`, `algo`, `env`, `tool`, `ckpt`, `doc`, `data`, `cfg`, `reward`, `fully_async`, `one_step_off` - If this PR involves multiple modules, separate them with `,` like `[megatron, fsdp, doc]` - `{type}` is in `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `chore`, `test` - If this PR breaks any API (CLI arguments, config, function signature, etc.), add `[BREAKING]` to the beginning of the title. - Example: `[BREAKING][fsdp, megatron] feat: dynamic batching` ### Test ```bash pytest tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py # GPU E2E: DSV4 merge=F GRPO 2-node — step1/step2 pearson 0.9970/0.9950 vs run15 merge=T 0.9952/0.9944 ``` Unit tests cover strict-vs-flat loader detection, per-expert routed leaves, and non-LoRA params on wrapped modules (e.g. DSV4 `gate.tid2eid` / `gate.e_score_correction_bias`). ### API and Usage Example For GLM-5.3-Flash, prepare every Ray node with a Bridge build providing `GLM53FlashModel` and its paired Megatron-Core, then launch with `VERL_USE_UV=0`. The frozen `megatron` extra pins Bridge 0.6.2, which lacks this wrapper. DSW CPU import checks passed against both the documented upstream source pair (Bridge `58382ddf`, Core `902feb8e`) and the separate Bridge `d16c26d5` environment used for GLM training. [Per-node setup and import check](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/cd9330c25a9408aeedc87a5abfb88562e9318a05/examples/tuning/lora/run_glm53_flash_megatron.sh#L12-L19) No CLI/API change. Behavior is automatic: `resolve_weight_name` probes the inner model's `load_weights` at runtime and toggles `.base_layer.` accordingly. For DSV4 merge=False LoRA, no extra config is needed beyond enabling LoRA + `merge=False`. ```bash # DSV4 merge=False LoRA (existing config; no new flags) actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.enable=True actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.merge=False actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.target_modules='["linear_wkv","linear_wgate","linear_wq_b","linear_weights_proj","linear_kv_proj","linear_q_down_proj","linear_q_up_proj","linear_proj","linear_fc1","linear_fc2","router"]' ``` ### Design & Code Changes **Runtime-probed `.base_layer.` reconciliation** (`verl/utils/vllm/utils.py`) - Adds `_inner_load_weights_is_strict`: probes the inner transformer's `load_weights` bytecode (`co_names`) to decide strict (keeps `.base_layer.`, DeepseekV2/DSV4) vs flat (strips it, Llama/Qwen3.5). Cached per class. - `resolve_weight_name` toggles one `.base_layer.` segment loader-style-aware, re-adds the suffix for non-LoRA params on a wrapped module, and reconciles per-expert routed leaves (strict keep / flat strip, gated by `_HAS_LORA_BASE_LAYER_PREFIX`). **mxfp4 LoRA unwrap** (`verl/utils/vllm/vllm_fp4_utils.py`) - Adds `_resolve_mxfp4_quant_method`: unwraps the `FusedMoEModularMethod` wrapper that merge=False LoRA installs over `Mxfp4MoEMethod` (stored as `old_quant_method`) so staging, layout derivation, and `process_weights_after_loading` repack reach the legacy method — the modular wrapper inherits a no-op post-load and would otherwise skip the repack. **FP8/mxfp4 name reconciliation** (`verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py`, `verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py`) - `load_quanted_weights` gains a `peft_config` parameter; when set (LoRA base sync), names run through `resolve_weight_name` against live params/buffers so `.base_layer.` is reconciled on the FP8/mxfp4 path too (e.g. DSV4 `compressor.fused_wkv_wgate`). Callers thread `peft_config` for both base and drafter loads. **LoRA MoE prefix** (`verl/utils/vllm/patch.py`) - Removes the eager `lora_base_layer_prefix` clearing block; the prefix is now reconciled through `resolve_weight_name` instead. **Tests** (`tests/utils/test_vllm_weight_name_normalization_on_cpu.py`) - Expanded coverage for strict-vs-flat loader detection, per-expert routed leaves, and non-LoRA params on wrapped modules. ### Checklist Before Submitting > [!IMPORTANT] > Please check all the following items before requesting a review, otherwise the reviewer might deprioritize this PR for review. - [X] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [X] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always` - [X] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs). - [X] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: ... - [X] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).) - [X] If your PR is related to the `recipe` submodule, please also update the reference to the submodule commit via `git submodule update --remote` or `cd recipe && git pull origin main`. ✨ Presented to you with [Mind Lab](https://www.mindlab.im/) - A Lab for Experiential Intelligence.

comment.body: Follow-up on [5728820172](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#pullrequestreview-5728820172) (fused full-stream VLM `(output, loss_mask)` tuple), revising my [earlier reply](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483#issuecomment-6617959203). The fused forward now unpacks the tuple in 51e7a973, with the same `full_stream_model and isinstance(output_orig, tuple)` check the unfused forward uses, so it no longer depends on the wrapper skipping the tuple when no `loss_mask` is passed. `tests/models/test_model_forward_fused.py` now has a full-stream wrapper that returns `(output, loss_mask)`. Without the fix it fails on the last pipeline stage (`AttributeError` on `log_probs`) and on a middle stage (the tuple is passed on unchanged).

The unwrap avoided that but processed the experts twice, since the pass also visits them directly. It now returns early for the wrapper. Test: `test_moe_lora_reload_processes_routed_experts_once`.

comment.body: Done: `kv_b_proj` now gets a dedicated `MLAKVBProjWithLoRA` (plus a fully sharded variant). `MLAAttention` marks the `kv_b_proj` it receives, so no MLA model changes. issue.title: [Bug] Checkpoint FP8 KV-cache scales are ignored: attention built without quant_config (GLM-4.5, Llama 4, Qwen3-MoE, GPT-OSS, HunYuan, HY3, K-EXAONE, LFM2)
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

These models build `RadixAttention` without `quant_config`, so attention gets no KV-cache method and no `k_scale`/`v_scale`. With a checkpoint that declares a static FP8 KV cache (compressed-tensors `kv_cache_scheme`, or ModelOpt `kv_cache_quant_algo: FP8`), `--kv-cache-dtype auto` picks an FP8 cache, the per-layer scales are dropped, and K/V are cached with scale 1.0. HunYuan and Llama 4 log a "... is not loaded" warning per tensor (HunYuan raises `KeyError` on ModelOpt names); the others are silent. Most of these loaders also have no KV-scale name rule, so the argument alone is not enough.

| Models | Attention (main `c03b6b3`) | Loader |
|---|---|---|
| GLM-4.5/4.6/4.7, GLM-4.5V, NextN | [glm4_moe.py#L287](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py#L287) | no rule ([glm4_moe](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py#L1072), [glm4v_moe](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/glm4v_moe.py#L110)) |
| Llama 4 | [llama4.py#L299](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/llama4.py#L299) | [`_handle_scale_remapping`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/mllama4.py#L721-L726) remaps the name, then skips the tensor |
| Qwen3-MoE (also Qwen3-VL-MoE, Qwen3-Omni-MoE, Flint), Mellum | [qwen3_moe.py#L589](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L589), [mellum.py#L244](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/mellum.py#L244) | no rule ([qwen3_moe](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py#L1137)); Qwen3-VL-MoE ignores `.k_scale`/`.v_scale` |
| GPT-OSS | [gpt_oss.py#L454](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/gpt_oss.py#L454); the decoder layer gives attention no quant config at all ([#L545](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/gpt_oss.py#L545)) | no rule |
| HunYuan V1 (A13B, dense) | [hunyuan.py#L333](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/hunyuan.py#L333) | has a rule |
| HY3, HY3 NextN | [hunyuan_v3.py#L280](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/hunyuan_v3.py#L280) | no rule (both loaders) |
| K-EXAONE, MTP | [exaone_moe.py#L383](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/exaone_moe.py#L383) | no rule |
| LFM2, LFM2-VL, LFM2-MoE | [lfm2.py#L174](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/lfm2.py#L174), [lfm2_moe.py#L238](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/lfm2_moe.py#L238) | no rule |

v0.5.23 has the same code (`glm4_moe.py:286`, `llama4.py:302`, `qwen3_moe.py:585`, ...). Public checkpoints whose calibrated scales load as 1.0 include `nvidia/Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct-NVFP4-MLPerf-Inference-Closed-V6.1-FP8-KV`, `intel-ai/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-MXFP4` and `CoolJohn-AI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-NVFP4-AutoRound`; the GLM-4.7 and GPT-OSS ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoints I found store scales of exactly 1.0.

Related but not covering this: #46527 adds the argument for Qwen3 (`qwen3.py`) only; #39942/#39943 add a name rule to the Qwen3-MoE, Qwen2 and Mixtral loaders but not the argument, so Qwen3-MoE still has nothing to load into; the closed, unmerged #20705 added the argument to several of these files; #12857 (closed) shows the Llama 4 warning.

Two things a fix must handle: `Mxfp4Config.get_quant_method` raises `NotImplementedError` for attention layers ([mxfp4.py#L386](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py#L386)), so GPT-OSS cannot pass its config straight through; and on CUDA `create_fused_set_kv_buffer_arg` asserts `layer.k_scale is None` ([utils.py#L344](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c03b6b3df5fe9aa86c1d56c0cdbb30d7a9158f5c/python/sglang/srt/models/utils.py#L344)), so Qwen3-MoE with the argument fails with `AssertionError: scale not supported` under `--kv-cache-dtype bf16`. A patch with a unit test (the argument for all of these but GPT-OSS, and the missing loader rules except Qwen3-MoE's, which #39943 adds) is in #48750.

### Reproduction

`repro.py` builds a tiny random checkpoint, adds per-layer scales under the names LLM Compressor uses, loads it with an FP8 KV cache, and dumps the loaded state dict with `Engine.save_sharded_model`.

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# usage: python repro.py {glm4-moe,llama4,gpt-oss,llama}
import glob, json, sys, tempfile
import torch, transformers as tf, sglang as sgl
from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file

if __name__ == "__main__":
    C = dict(num_hidden_layers=2, hidden_size=256, intermediate_size=512, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=64, vocab_size=1024)
    make, cfg, prefix = {  # tiny random models; prefix = checkpoint name of the decoder layers
        "glm4-moe": (tf.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config, lambda: tf.Glm4MoeConfig(**C, n_routed_experts=4, num_experts_per_tok=2, moe_intermediate_size=256, n_shared_experts=1, first_k_dense_replace=1, n_group=1, topk_group=1), "model.layers"),
        "llama4": (tf.Llama4ForConditionalGeneration, lambda: tf.Llama4Config(text_config=dict(C, num_local_experts=4, intermediate_size_mlp=512), vision_config=dict(num_hidden_layers=1)), "language_model.model.layers"),
        "gpt-oss": (tf.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config, lambda: tf.GptOssConfig(**C, num_local_experts=4, num_experts_per_tok=2, layer_types=["sliding_attention", "full_attention"]), "model.layers"),
        "llama": (tf.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config, lambda: tf.LlamaConfig(**C), "model.layers"),
    }[sys.argv[1]]
    path, dump = tempfile.mkdtemp(), tempfile.mkdtemp()
    make(cfg()).to(torch.bfloat16).save_pretrained(path)
    [shard] = glob.glob(f"{path}/model*.safetensors")
    t = load_file(shard)
    for i, (k, v) in enumerate([(0.5, 0.125), (0.25, 0.0625)]):  # per-layer scales, named as LLM Compressor names them
        t[f"{prefix}.{i}.self_attn.k_scale"], t[f"{prefix}.{i}.self_attn.v_scale"] = torch.tensor(k), torch.tensor(v)
    save_file(t, shard, metadata={"format": "pt"})
    c = json.load(open(f"{path}/config.json"))
    c["quantization_config"] = {"quant_method": "compressed-tensors", "format": "dense", "config_groups": {}, "kv_cache_scheme": {"num_bits": 8, "type": "float", "strategy": "tensor", "dynamic": False, "symmetric": True}}
    json.dump(c, open(f"{path}/config.json", "w"))
    engine = sgl.Engine(model_path=path, kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3", skip_tokenizer_init=True, disable_cuda_graph=True, mem_fraction_static=0.2, context_length=512)
    engine.save_sharded_model(path=dump, pattern=None, max_size=None)  # writes the loaded state dict
    engine.shutdown()
    scales = {n: x.item() for f in glob.glob(f"{dump}/*.safetensors") for n, x in load_file(f).items() if n.endswith(("attn.k_scale", "attn.v_scale"))}
    print(c["architectures"][0], scales or "-> no attention k_scale/v_scale (FP8 KV cache at 1.0)")
```
</details>

On v0.5.23 and on main `c03b6b3` (1x H20-3e):

```
$ for m in glm4-moe llama4 gpt-oss llama; do python repro.py $m; done
Glm4MoeForCausalLM -> no attention k_scale/v_scale (FP8 KV cache at 1.0)
Llama4ForConditionalGeneration -> no attention k_scale/v_scale (FP8 KV cache at 1.0)
GptOssForCausalLM -> no attention k_scale/v_scale (FP8 KV cache at 1.0)
LlamaForCausalLM {'model.layers.0.self_attn.attn.k_scale': 0.5, 'model.layers.0.self_attn.attn.v_scale': 0.125, 'model.layers.1.self_attn.attn.k_scale': 0.25, 'model.layers.1.self_attn.attn.v_scale': 0.0625}
```

`llama.py` passes `quant_config` and loads the scales. With the patch, `glm4-moe` and `llama4` print the same four values.

`python3 -m sglang.check_env` (trimmed), plus `compressed-tensors==0.18.0`; main `c03b6b3` was run from source in the same environment.

- `Mxfp4Config.get_quant_method` raises `NotImplementedError` for attention layers, and GPT-OSS's decoder layer builds its attention without a quant config at all, so the KV-cache method has to come from somewhere other than the MXFP4 config.

issue.body:

The output of python collect_env.py Output of `python -m vllm.collect_env`, trimmed: removed CPU flags, GPU topology, environment variables and the system-wide pip list (the library versions shown are
